1	# Worktree ownership
2
3	Read this before creating a worktree, or when a new checkout is missing its
4	dependencies or `.env`.
5
6	## The confusion this resolves
7
8	Three mechanisms create git worktrees, and they all look interchangeable:
9
10	- `claude --worktree <name>` / `isolation: worktree` / `/batch` — Claude Code's
11	  own, under `.claude/worktrees/`.
12	- `herdr worktree create --branch … --base …` — creates a checkout under
13	  `~/.herdr/worktrees/` and opens it as a herdr workspace.
14	- `git worktree add` by hand, or a tool like Worktrunk.
15
16	They are all standard git worktrees underneath, so nothing *breaks* if you mix
17	them. What breaks is the mental model: two lifecycle owners for one checkout,
18	and no single answer to "where do worktrees live on this machine?"
19
20	## The rule
21
22	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
23	|---|---|---|---|
24	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
25	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` | dies with the turn |
26	| Everything else | **`dev`** | as above | as above |
27
28	**Might a human come back to it tomorrow → `dev`. Does it die with this agent
29	turn → Claude Code native.**
30
31	Concretely:
32
33	- Two agents implementing *different approaches* to the same problem, so the
34	  best can be picked → Claude Code worktrees. They are disposable.
35	- Two agents working on *disjoint files of one feature* → no worktree at all.
36	  One checkout, one branch, separate panes. Worktrees isolate change streams;
37	  panes isolate agents.
38	- A feature you will still be working on next week → `dev start`.
39	- Picking up on a different machine → `dev park --cold --push` here,
40	  `dev resume` there. The branch is the identity; the directory is a cache.
41
42	## Why `dev` does not call `herdr worktree create`
43
44	`dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then calls
45	`herdr worktree open --path <path> --label <task>`.
46
47	The path policy has to hold on machines without herdr — a laptop, a CI box, a
48	server you ssh into. Delegating placement to herdr would mean worktrees land
49	somewhere different depending on what happens to be installed. Creating the
50	checkout with git and asking herdr only to *open* it keeps one policy and still
51	gets the full sidebar treatment: the workspace is grouped under its parent repo
52	with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
53
54	## Never nest a worktree inside a repository
55
56	`.claude/worktrees/` is acceptable for turn-scoped work because Claude Code
57	cleans it up and the directory is gitignored. For anything longer-lived, a
58	checkout inside another checkout means every file watcher, language server,
59	indexer, backup tool and `rg` run in the outer repo sees a second copy of the
60	whole tree.
61
62	`dev` refuses to create one, and will tell you to point
63	`paths.worktree_path` somewhere outside the repo.
64
65	If you do use `.claude/worktrees/`, keep `.claude/worktrees/` in `.gitignore`
66	so the contents never show as untracked files in the main checkout.
67
68	## Where dev puts them
69
70	Default:
71
72	```
73	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
74	```
75
76	Fully configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine — a
77	different volume, a different naming convention:
78
79	```toml
80	[paths]
81	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
82	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
83	```
84
85	Variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`,
86	`date`. Filters: `|slug` (filesystem-safe: `feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`),
87	`|lower`, `|base`.
88
89	The reason for a separate root rather than siblings of the repo: with one or
90	two worktrees, `repo/` and `repo.feat-auth/` side by side is perfectly clear.
91	With ten, the projects directory stops answering "what projects do I have?" —
92	the filesystem hierarchy starts doing git's job badly.
93
94	## Provisioning: making a worktree actually usable
95
96	A worktree is a **clean checkout**. It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, and
97	none of the gitignored files the project needs to run. Without provisioning,
98	every new worktree starts broken.
99
100	`dev wt create` (and `dev start`) builds an inspectable provisioning plan,
101	then applies it. See the plan before creating anything:
102
103	```bash
104	dev wt plan                 # detect project types and show every action
105	dev wt plan --write         # seed a committed .dev.toml from the result
106	dev wt provision --dry-run  # plan for an existing checkout
107	```
108
109	The settings live under `[worktree]` globally or in the repo's own `.dev.toml`:
110
111	```toml
112	[worktree]
113	# Gitignored files to carry over.
114	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
115
116	# Heavy directories to symlink instead of copy. Opt-in and empty by default —
117	# sharing node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that
118	# it must never happen by accident.
119	link = []
120
121	# "auto" detects from lockfiles, or give an explicit list.
122	post_create = "auto"
123
124	# How installed dependencies arrive. The safe default is reinstall.
125	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
126
127	[worktree.strategies]
128	node = "copy"               # override one ecosystem
129	```
130
131	**Only files that are both listed *and* gitignored are copied.** A tracked file
132	is already in the new checkout on the correct branch; copying the source
133	branch's version over it would be wrong. The classic mistake is listing
134	`.vscode/settings.json` — it is committed, so it is already there.
135
136	`post_create = "auto"` detects one command per ecosystem:
137
138	| Marker | Command |
139	|---|---|
140	| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` |
141	| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` |
142	| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
143	| `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
144	| `yarn.lock` | `yarn install --immutable` |
145	| `go.mod` | `go mod download` |
146	| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fetch` |
147	| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` |
148
149	A detected command whose tool is not installed is skipped, not failed. A failed
150	command is reported but leaves the checkout in place — it is usable, and
151	throwing it away would cost the branch for nothing.
152
153
154	## Copy, reinstall, link, or skip?
155
156	This is a per-ecosystem correctness decision, not merely a speed preference:
157
158	| Strategy | Effect | Default use |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| `reinstall` | Run the lockfile-derived install command | Always sound; default |
161	| `copy` | Duplicate the dependency directory from the source checkout | Faster where path-independent |
162	| `link` | Share one directory between checkouts | Fastest; usually unsafe |
163	| `skip` | Leave dependencies absent | Container/CI-driven projects |
164
165	`dev` encodes the non-obvious facts:
166
167	- Python `.venv` **cannot be copied or linked**: `pyvenv.cfg`, activation
168	  scripts and entry points bake in the old absolute path. `uv sync` uses a
169	  shared cache and is normally cheap anyway.
170	- Node `node_modules` can be copied, including pnpm's symlinks (links are
171	  recreated, not dereferenced). Sharing one tree is refused because an install
172	  in either checkout silently changes the other.
173	- Go modules are already in a global content-addressed cache; there is no local
174	  directory worth copying.
175	- Cargo `target/` can be copied, but is often larger than rebuilding. Sharing
176	  it is refused because concurrent builds write the same lock/artifacts.
177
178	An unsound configured strategy is not obeyed blindly: `dev wt plan` says why
179	and narrows it back to `reinstall`. A typo likewise becomes a warning rather
180	than silently skipping dependencies.
181
182	`post_create` and strategy are separate axes. An explicit command list replaces
183	the *derived install commands* but does not disable a `copy` strategy. A project
184	can copy `node_modules` and then run `make bootstrap`.
185
186	Per-repo override, committed next to the code so it reaches every machine:
187
188	```toml
189	# <repo>/.dev.toml
190	[worktree]
191	include     = [".env", "config/local.json"]
192	post_create = ["make bootstrap"]
193
194	[worktree.strategies]
195	node = "copy"
196	```
197
198	Re-run provisioning on an existing checkout with `dev wt provision`.
199
200	## Cleanup
201
202	```bash
203	dev wt rm feat/auth      # removes the checkout; the branch survives
204	```
205
206	Removing a worktree and abandoning a change stream are different decisions.
207	`dev` never deletes a branch as a side effect, and refuses to remove a checkout
208	with uncommitted changes without an explicit `--force`.
209
210	If a directory was deleted behind git's back, `dev wt rm` and `dev sweep` prune

```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2
3	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
4	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
5
6	## The problem
7
8	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
9	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
10	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
11	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
12
13	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
14	not the runtime.
15
16	## Pick a checkout mode before a lifecycle
17
18	A task records human intent; it does not imply a worktree:
19
20	| Command | Checkout boundary | Use when |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| `dev repo open api` | none; no task | browsing or truly ad-hoc work |
23	| `dev start api -t typo --direct` | current branch, usually main | one short tracked change |
24	| `dev start api -t small --branch-only` | branch in canonical checkout | lightweight isolation, no concurrency |
25	| `dev start api -t auth --base main` | branch + linked worktree | interruption, experiment, parallel writer |
26
27	Direct tasks go HOT ↔ WARM and finish with plain `dev done`; they cannot go
28	COLD because the canonical checkout cannot be removed. Branch-only tasks can go
29	cold after push by switching the canonical checkout back to base. The full
30	state machine below describes the default worktree mode.
31
32	Do not create isolation before it has a job. Equally, a new parallel worktree
33	starts from committed HEAD — it does not carry dirty main changes — so
34	checkpoint first when the new task depends on them.
35
36	## The four states
37
38	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
41	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
42	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
43	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
44
45	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
46
47	```
48	        dev start
49	            │
50	            ▼
51	         🔥 hot ──── dev done ────► ✅ done
52	          │  ▲
53	   dev park│  │dev resume
54	          ▼  │
55	        🌤 warm
56	          │  ▲
57	dev park  │  │dev resume
58	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)
59	        ❄️ cold
60	```
61
62	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
63	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
64
65	## Parking
66
67	```bash
68	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
69	```
70
71	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
72	next, closes the runtime session, and leaves the checkout boundary exactly
73	where it is. In direct mode that is the current branch; in worktree mode it is
74	the branch and linked checkout.
75
76	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
77	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
78	supply one.
79
80	Useful variations:
81
82	```bash
83	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
84	dev park --cold --push            # push, remove the worktree, keep the branch
85	dev park --keep-session           # record the state, leave the session open
86	```
87
88	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
89
90	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
91
92	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
93	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
94	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
95
96	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
97	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
98	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
99	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
100
101	## Cold, and why it is safe
102
103	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
104
105	- the branch still holds every commit;
106	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
107	  them too;
108	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
109
110	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
111	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
112
113	## Moving work between machines
114
115	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
116	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
117
118	On the machine holding the work:
119
120	```bash
121	dev park --cold --push
122	```
123
124	On the machine picking it up:
125
126	```bash
127	dev resume <task> --fetch
128	```
129
130	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
131	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
132	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
133	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
134
135	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
136	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
137	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
138
139	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
140	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
141	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
142
143	## Sweeping
144
145	```bash
146	dev sweep            # report only
147	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
148	```
149
150	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
151
152	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
153	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about.
154	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
155	  pushed, that could go cold.
156
157	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
158	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
159
160	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. The
161	reason cleanup usually does not happen is not unwillingness; it is the absence
162	of a trustworthy guarantee that the work is recoverable. Reporting first, and
163	requiring confirmation, is that guarantee.
164
165	## Integration
166
167	```bash
168	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
169	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via gh or glab
170	```
171
172	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
173	keeping in the base's history?**
174
175	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
176	  stay legible.
177	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
178	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
179
180	`dev done` refuses on a dirty tree, and `--delete-branch` only removes a branch
181	git agrees is fully contained in the base. "Merged" is not always "finished" —
182	work often continues on a branch after its first integration, which is why the
183	branch survives by default.
184
```
</details></tool-use>

12	func TestRenderHasValidFrontmatter(t *testing.T) {
13		body, err := skill.Render()
14		if err != nil {
15			t.Fatal(err)
16		}
17		if !strings.HasPrefix(body, "---\n") {
18			t.Fatal("SKILL.md must open with YAML frontmatter — a file that does not parse is silently skipped by every skill loader")
19		}
20		end := strings.Index(body[4:], "\n---")
21		if end < 0 {
22			t.Fatal("frontmatter is not terminated")
23		}
24		front := body[4 : end+4]
25		if !strings.Contains(front, "name: "+skill.Name) {
26			t.Errorf("frontmatter must name the skill %q:\n%s", skill.Name, front)
27		}
28		if !strings.Contains(front, "description:") {
29			t.Error("frontmatter needs a description — it is what a loader matches on")
30		}
31	}

33	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
34		t.Helper()
35		home := t.TempDir()
36		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")

47			t.Fatal(err)
48		}
49		r.Root = dest
50
51		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
52		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
53		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
54		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
55		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))

76	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {

332	func TestStrategySafety(t *testing.T) {

372	// asErr is errors.As without importing errors into every call site.
373	func asErr[T error](err error, target *T) bool {
374		for err != nil {
375			if t, ok := err.(T); ok {
376				*target = t
377				return true
378			}
379			u, ok := err.(interface{ Unwrap() error })
380			if !ok {
381				return false
382			}
383			err = u.Unwrap()
384		}
385		return false
386	}

```text
1	// Package skill embeds and installs dev's agent skill.
2	//
3	// The binary is the authority for its own skill, the same way `herdr --skill`
4	// is: a skill vendored separately drifts from the tool it documents, and an
5	// agent reading a stale command list is worse than one reading none. Embedding
6	// means the skill shipped is always the skill this build implements.
7	package skill
8
9	import (
10		"embed"
11		"fmt"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"strings"
16	)
17
18	//go:embed all:dev-cli
19	var files embed.FS
20
21	// Name is the skill's directory and frontmatter name.
22	//
23	// Deliberately not "dev", matching the binary: a skill is selected by its name
24	// and description, and "dev" describes nothing. The binary is typed dozens of
25	// times a day and should stay short; the skill is read by an agent deciding
26	// whether it is relevant, and should say what it covers.
27	const Name = "dev-cli"
28
29	// Render returns the SKILL.md body.
30	func Render() (string, error) {
31		b, err := files.ReadFile("dev-cli/SKILL.md")
32		if err != nil {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("bundled skill is missing: %w", err)
34		}
35		return string(b), nil
36	}
37
38	// Files walks the embedded skill tree, yielding relative paths and contents.
39	func Files() (map[string][]byte, error) {
40		out := map[string][]byte{}
41		err := fs.WalkDir(files, "dev-cli", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
42			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
43				return err
44			}
45			b, err := files.ReadFile(p)
46			if err != nil {
47				return err
48			}
49			out[strings.TrimPrefix(p, "dev-cli/")] = b
50			return nil
51		})
52		return out, err
53	}
54
55	// InstallResult reports what an install changed.
56	type InstallResult struct {
57		Dir     string
58		Written []string
59		Skipped []string
60		Links   []string
61	}
62
63	// DefaultDir is where the skill is installed: the shared agent skills
64	// directory, which Claude Code, Codex and others all read.
65	func DefaultDir() string {
66		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
67		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", "skills", Name)
68	}
69
70	// LinkDirs are the tool-specific directories that get a symlink back to the
71	// shared install, matching the layout these tools already use.
72	func LinkDirs() []string {
73		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
74		return []string{filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "skills")}
75	}
76
77	// Install writes the embedded skill to dir and links it into the per-tool
78	// skill directories. Writes are content-compared first, so re-running is a
79	// no-op and does not churn mtimes that other tools watch.
80	func Install(dir string, link bool) (InstallResult, error) {
81		res := InstallResult{Dir: dir}
82		all, err := Files()
83		if err != nil {
84			return res, err
85		}
86		if len(all) == 0 {
87			return res, fmt.Errorf("no skill files are embedded in this build")
88		}
89
90		for rel, content := range all {
91			dst := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
92			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
93				return res, err
94			}
95			if existing, err := os.ReadFile(dst); err == nil && string(existing) == string(content) {
96				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, rel)
97				continue
98			}
99			if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
100				return res, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", dst, err)
101			}
102			res.Written = append(res.Written, rel)
103		}
104
105		if !link {
106			return res, nil
107		}
108		for _, base := range LinkDirs() {
109			if _, err := os.Stat(base); err != nil {
110				continue // that tool is not installed here
111			}
112			target := filepath.Join(base, Name)
113			if existing, err := os.Readlink(target); err == nil {
114				if resolveLink(base, existing) == dir {
115					continue // already correct
116				}
117				os.Remove(target)
118			} else if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
119				// A real directory, not our symlink: never clobber it.
120				continue
121			}
122			if err := os.Symlink(dir, target); err != nil {
123				return res, fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", target, err)
124			}
125			res.Links = append(res.Links, target)
126		}
127		return res, nil
128	}
129
130	func resolveLink(base, link string) string {
131		if filepath.IsAbs(link) {
132			return filepath.Clean(link)
133		}
134		return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(base, link))
135	}
136

```text
package ignore

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// Extras are the blocks no language template provides but almost every
// repository wants. They are kept separate from the language sections so a
// later regeneration can replace a language block without losing them.
type Extras struct {
	// OS adds the platform's junk files (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db).
	OS bool
	// Editors adds editor and IDE local state.
	Editors bool
	// Agents adds the directories coding-agent harnesses create.
	Agents bool
	// Env adds the usual local secret files.
	Env bool
}

// DefaultExtras is what `dev gitignore` adds unless told otherwise.
func DefaultExtras() Extras { return Extras{OS: true, Editors: true, Agents: true, Env: true} }

const (
	// Markers delimit the region dev manages, so re-running it updates that
	// region and leaves anything the user added by hand untouched.
	blockBegin = "# >>> dev gitignore >>>"
	blockEnd   = "# <<< dev gitignore <<<"
)

// osSection returns the junk files the host platform scatters through a repo.
func osSection() string {
	switch runtime.GOOS {
	case "darwin":
		return `# macOS
.DS_Store
.AppleDouble
.LSOverride
._*
.Spotlight-V100
.Trashes`
	case "windows":
		return `# Windows
Thumbs.db
Thumbs.db:encryptable
ehthumbs.db
Desktop.ini
$RECYCLE.BIN/`
	default:
		return `# Linux
*~
.fuse_hidden*
.directory
.Trash-*
.nfs*`
	}
}

const editorsSection = `# Editors and IDEs
.idea/
*.iml
.vscode/*
!.vscode/settings.json
!.vscode/extensions.json
!.vscode/launch.json
*.swp
*.swo
.nvimlog
.null-ls_*`

// agentsSection covers the directories coding-agent harnesses create inside a
// repository. The worktree entries matter most: an agent's linked checkout
// left untracked makes every `git status` in the main checkout unreadable.
const agentsSection = `# Coding agent harnesses
.claude/worktrees/
.claude/settings.local.json
.aider*
.cursor/rules/_generated/
.specstory/history/`

const envSection = `# Local environment and secrets — never commit real values
.env
.env.*
!.env.example
!.env.template
*.local
.direnv/`

// Compose renders the managed block from the given sections and extras.
func Compose(sections []Section, extras Extras) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(blockBegin + "\n")
	b.WriteString("# Generated by `dev gitignore`. Edit outside this block, or re-run to update.\n")

	for _, s := range sections {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n# --- %s (%s) ---\n%s\n", s.Name, s.Source, s.Body)
	}

	var tail []string
	if extras.OS {
		tail = append(tail, osSection())
	}
	if extras.Editors {
		tail = append(tail, editorsSection)
	}
	if extras.Agents {
		tail = append(tail, agentsSection)
	}
	if extras.Env {
		tail = append(tail, envSection)
	}
	for _, t := range tail {
		b.WriteString("\n" + t + "\n")
	}

	b.WriteString(blockEnd + "\n")
	return b.String()
}

// Merge splices a generated block into an existing .gitignore.
//
// Replacing only the delimited region is what makes this safe to re-run: a
// project accumulates hand-written rules over time, and regenerating must
// never be the thing that loses them.
func Merge(existing, block string) string {
	start := strings.Index(existing, blockBegin)
	end := strings.Index(existing, blockEnd)
	if start >= 0 && end > start {
		tailStart := end + len(blockEnd)
		if tailStart < len(existing) && existing[tailStart] == '\n' {
			tailStart++
		}
		return existing[:start] + block + existing[tailStart:]
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(existing) == "" {
		return block
	}
	if !strings.HasSuffix(existing, "\n") {
		existing += "\n"
	}
	return existing + "\n" + block
}

// HasManagedBlock reports whether a file already carries dev's markers.
func HasManagedBlock(content string) bool {
	return strings.Contains(content, blockBegin) && strings.Contains(content, blockEnd)
}

// Detect infers which language templates a repository needs from the files it
// contains, so `dev gitignore` can be run with no arguments.
func Detect(dir string) []string {
	markers := map[string][]string{
		"Python":       {"pyproject.toml", "requirements.txt", "setup.py", "uv.lock", "Pipfile"},
		"Node":         {"package.json", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "yarn.lock", "bun.lockb"},
		"Go":           {"go.mod"},
		"Rust":         {"Cargo.toml"},
		"Ruby":         {"Gemfile"},
		"Java":         {"pom.xml"},
		"Gradle":       {"build.gradle", "build.gradle.kts"},
		"Elixir":       {"mix.exs"},
		"Terraform":    {"main.tf", ".terraform.lock.hcl"},
		"Dart":         {"pubspec.yaml"},
		"Swift":        {"Package.swift"},
		"Composer":     {"composer.json"},
		"TeX":          {"main.tex"},
		"VisualStudio": {"*.sln"},
	}
	var found []string
	for name, files := range markers {
		for _, f := range files {
			if strings.ContainsRune(f, '*') {
				if matches, _ := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, f)); len(matches) > 0 {
					found = append(found, name)
					break
				}
				continue
			}
			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, f)); err == nil {
				found = append(found, name)
				break
			}
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(found)
	return found
}

```text
package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/ignore"
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
)

func newGitignoreCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	var (
		stdout    bool
		offline   bool
		noOS      bool
		noEditors bool
		noAgents  bool
		noEnv     bool
		list      bool
	)
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:     "gitignore [language...]",
		Aliases: []string{"ignore"},
		Short:   "Write a .gitignore from GitHub's templates plus the entries every repo needs",
		Long: `Compose a .gitignore for this repository.

Language sections come from GitHub's published templates, fetched once and
cached. On top of those, dev adds the entries no language template covers but
almost every repository wants: the host platform's junk files, editor state,
local env files, and the directories coding-agent harnesses create — a
harness's linked worktree left untracked makes every git status in the main
checkout unreadable.

With no language argument, the languages are inferred from the files present.

Everything dev writes goes inside a delimited block, so re-running updates that
block and leaves rules you added by hand alone.

  dev gitignore                 # detect from the repo's files
  dev gitignore python node     # explicit
  dev gitignore --stdout        # preview without writing
  dev gitignore --no-agents     # skip the harness section`,
		Args: cobra.ArbitraryArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			ctx := ctxOf()

			if list {
				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Available without a network:")
				for _, n := range ignore.BundledNames() {
					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s\n", n)
				}
				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nAny name from https://github.com/github/gitignore works online.")
				return nil
			}

			// Operate on the repository root, not wherever the shell happens
			// to be: a .gitignore in a subdirectory only covers that subtree.
			cwd, err := os.Getwd()
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			target := cwd
			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd); err == nil {
				target = g.Root
			} else if !stdout {
				return fmt.Errorf("%s is not a git repository (use --stdout to preview anyway)",
					config.Contract(cwd))
			}

			names := args
			if len(names) == 0 {
				names = ignore.Detect(target)
				if len(names) == 0 {
					app.warnf("no language detected in %s — writing only the common sections",
						config.Contract(target))
				} else {
					fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "detected: %s\n", strings.Join(names, ", "))
				}
			}

			fetcher := ignore.NewFetcher(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "gitignore"))
			fetcher.Offline = offline

			var sections []ignore.Section
			for _, n := range names {
				s, err := fetcher.Get(ctx, n)
				if err != nil {
					// One unknown language must not lose the rest of the file.
					app.warnf("%v", err)
					continue
				}
				sections = append(sections, s)
			}

			extras := ignore.DefaultExtras()
			extras.OS = !noOS
			extras.Editors = !noEditors
			extras.Agents = !noAgents
			extras.Env = !noEnv

			block := ignore.Compose(sections, extras)
			if stdout {
				fmt.Fprint(app.Out, block)
				return nil
			}

			path := filepath.Join(target, ".gitignore")
			existing, _ := os.ReadFile(path)
			updated := ignore.Merge(string(existing), block)
			if string(existing) == updated {
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s is already up to date\n", config.Contract(path))
				return nil
			}
			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
				return err
			}

			verb := "wrote"
			if ignore.HasManagedBlock(string(existing)) {
				verb = "updated the managed block in"
			} else if len(existing) > 0 {
				verb = "appended a managed block to"
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s\n", verb, config.Contract(path))
			for _, s := range sections {
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %-14s %s\n", s.Name, s.Source)
			}
			return nil
		},
	}
	f := cmd.Flags()
	f.BoolVar(&stdout, "stdout", false, "print instead of writing the file")
	f.BoolVar(&offline, "offline", false, "use only cached and bundled templates")
	f.BoolVar(&list, "list", false, "list the templates available offline")
	f.BoolVar(&noOS, "no-os", false, "omit the host platform's junk files")
	f.BoolVar(&noEditors, "no-editors", false, "omit editor and IDE state")
	f.BoolVar(&noAgents, "no-agents", false, "omit coding-agent harness directories")
	f.BoolVar(&noEnv, "no-env", false, "omit local env and secret files")
	return cmd
}
```

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6
7	import (
8		"fmt"
9		"strings"
10		"time"
11	)
12
13	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
14	type State string
15
16	const (
17		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
18		Hot State = "hot"
19		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
20		Warm State = "warm"
21		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
22		Cold State = "cold"
23		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
24		Done State = "done"
25	)
26
27	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
28	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
29
30	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
31	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
32		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
33		for _, valid := range States {
34			if got == valid {
35				return got, nil
36			}
37		}
38		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
39	}
40
41	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
42	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
43		parts := make([]string, len(States))
44		for i, s := range States {
45			parts[i] = string(s)
46		}
47		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
48	}
49
50	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
51	func (s State) Icon() string {
52		switch s {
53		case Hot:
54			return "🔥"
55		case Warm:
56			return "🌤"
57		case Cold:
58			return "❄️"
59		case Done:
60			return "✅"
61		}
62		return "?"
63	}
64
65	// Label is the uppercase column form.
66	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
67
68	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
69	type CheckoutMode string
70
71	const (
72		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
73		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
74		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
75		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
76		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
77		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
78		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
79	)
80
81	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
82	type Task struct {
83		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
84		// stored inside the file.
85		ID string `toml:"-"`
86
87		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
88		Name string `toml:"name"`
89		// Repo is the repository's display name.
90		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
91		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
92		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
93		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
94		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
95		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
96		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
97		// integrate without re-guessing.
98		Base string `toml:"base"`
99		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
100		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
101		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
102		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
103		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
104		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
105
106		State State `toml:"state"`
107		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
108		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
109		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
110		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you

115
116		// AgentSession records a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"), so a
117		// parked task can be resumed with its conversation intact.
118		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
119		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a herdr
120		// workspace id). Advisory only — always re-resolved against the live
121		// runtime before use.
122		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
123
124		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
125		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
126	}
127
128	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
129	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
130	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
131	// semantics and must be explicit.
132	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
133		if t.Mode != "" {
134			return t.Mode
135		}
136		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
137			return ModeWorktree
138		}
139		return ModeBranch
140	}
141
142	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
143	func (t Task) Title() string {
144		if t.Name != "" {
145			return t.Name
146		}
147		return t.Branch
148	}
149
150	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
151	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
152	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
153
154	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
155	func (t Task) Validate() error {
156		switch {
157		case t.Repo == "":
158			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
159		case t.Branch == "":
160			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
161		case t.RepoPath == "":
162			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
163		}
164		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
165			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
166		}
167		switch t.Mode {
168		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
169		default:
170			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
171		}
172		return nil
173	}

210	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
211	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
212		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
213			return t.WorktreePath
214		}
215		return t.RepoPath
216	}
217
218	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
219	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
220	// anyone having to ask dev.
221	//
222	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
223	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
224	//
225	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
226	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
227	//
228	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
229	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
230	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
231		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
232			return
233		}
234		kv := map[string]string{
235			"stage": t.State.Label(),
236			"next":  t.Next,
237		}
238		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
239			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
240		}
241	}

243	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
244		p := res.Provision
245		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
246			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
247		}
248		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
249			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
250		}
251		for _, e := range p.Failures {
252			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
253		}
254	}

15	func newParkCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
16		var (
17			next   string
18			note   string
19			wip    bool
20			push   bool
21			cold   bool
22			keepRT bool
23		)
24		cmd := &cobra.Command{
25			Use:   "park [task]",
26			Short: "Stop working on a task without losing the thread",
27			Long: `Park the current task (or the one named) so its runtime session can close.
28
29	Parking is the missing move that makes a crowded sidebar shrink. It records
30	what to do next, optionally checkpoints uncommitted work, and closes the
31	runtime session — while leaving the branch and the worktree exactly where they
32	are. Closing a session is not abandoning a task.
33
34	  warm (default)  worktree and branch stay; session closes. Back within days.
35	  cold (--cold)   work is committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstruct
36	                  it anywhere later with dev resume.
37
38	A checkpoint commit is preferred over git stash: a stash is invisible in the
39	log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
40	machine, which is exactly what parking needs to support.`,
41			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
42			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
43				ctx := ctxOf()
44				t, err := resolveTask(app, args)
45				if err != nil {
46					return err
47				}
48
49				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
50				if cold && mode == task.ModeDirect {
51					return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s uses the canonical checkout on %s, so it cannot go cold; "+
52						"park it warm or finish it", t.Title(), t.Branch)
53				}
54				target := task.Warm
55				if cold {
56					target = task.Cold
57				}
58				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
59
60				if next != "" {
61					t.Next = next
62				}
63				if note != "" {
64					t.Note = note
65				}
66				if t.Next == "" {
67					app.warnf("no next action recorded — `dev park --next \"...\"` is what makes resuming cheap")
68				}
69
70				// Checkpoint before anything is closed or removed.
71				if _, statErr := os.Stat(checkout); statErr == nil {
72					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
73					if err != nil {
74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		return cmd
173	}
174
175	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
176	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
177		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
178			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
179		}
180		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
181		return nil
182	}
183
184	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
185	// directory when no argument is given.
186	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
187		if len(args) == 1 {
188			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
189		}
190		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
191		if err != nil {
192			return nil, err
193		}
194		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
197				config.Contract(cwd))
198		}
199		return t, nil
200	}

12	)
13
14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}

72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},
152		}
153		f := cmd.Flags()
154		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		return cmd

41	// Available reports whether the binary exists *and* a server is reachable.
42	// The binary alone is not enough: every dev call goes through the socket API,
43	// so a stopped server must degrade to the next backend rather than making
44	// every command fail.
45	func (h *Herdr) Available() bool {
46		if !haveBinary(h.bin) {
47			return false
48		}
49		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
50		defer cancel()

52		return err == nil

55	func (h *Herdr) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
56		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, h.bin, args...)
57		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
58		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
59		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
60			msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
61			if msg == "" {
62				msg = err.Error()
63			}
64			return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
65		}
66		return stdout.Bytes(), nil
67	}

96		}

127	// List implements Runtime. Workspaces carry no working directory of their own,
128	// so dev joins them against the pane list — panes are what actually have a cwd.
129	func (h *Herdr) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
130		var ws struct {
131			Workspaces []herdrWorkspace `json:"workspaces"`
132		}
133		if err := h.call(ctx, &ws, "workspace", "list"); err != nil {
134			return nil, err
135		}
136		var ps struct {
137			Panes []herdrPane `json:"panes"`
138		}
139		if err := h.call(ctx, &ps, "pane", "list"); err != nil {
140			// Directories are an enrichment; a workspace listing without them is
141			// still worth returning.
142			ps.Panes = nil
143		}
144
145		dirs := map[string]map[string]bool{}
146		agents := map[string]map[string]bool{}
147		for _, p := range ps.Panes {
148			if p.CWD != "" {
149				if dirs[p.WorkspaceID] == nil {
150					dirs[p.WorkspaceID] = map[string]bool{}
151				}
152				dirs[p.WorkspaceID][p.CWD] = true
153			}
154			if p.AgentSession != nil && p.AgentSession.Value != "" {
155				if agents[p.WorkspaceID] == nil {
156					agents[p.WorkspaceID] = map[string]bool{}
157				}
158				agents[p.WorkspaceID][p.AgentSession.Agent+":"+p.AgentSession.Value] = true
159			}
160		}
161
162		out := make([]Session, 0, len(ws.Workspaces))
163		for _, w := range ws.Workspaces {
164			out = append(out, Session{
165				Handle:        w.WorkspaceID,
166				Label:         w.Label,
167				Dirs:          keys(dirs[w.WorkspaceID]),
168				AgentSessions: keys(agents[w.WorkspaceID]),
169				AgentStatus:   w.AgentStatus,
170				Focused:       w.Focused,
171			})
172		}
173		return out, nil
174	}

176	// Open implements Runtime. An already-open directory is focused rather than
177	// opened twice.
178	func (h *Herdr) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error) {
179		if existing, err := h.List(ctx); err == nil {
180			for _, s := range existing {
181				for _, d := range s.Dirs {
182					if d == dir {
183						_ = h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", s.Handle)
184						return s.Handle, nil
185					}
186				}
187			}
188		}
189		args := []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", dir, "--no-focus"}
190		if label != "" {
191			args = append(args, "--label", label)
192		}
193		var res struct {
194			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
195		}
196		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
197			return "", err
198		}
199		return res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, nil
200	}

202	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
203	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
204	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
205	// ahead/behind row.
206	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
207		args := []string{"worktree", "open", "--path", path, "--no-focus"}
208		if label != "" {
209			args = append(args, "--label", label)
210		}
211		var res struct {
212			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
213			Worktree  herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
214		}
215		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
216			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
217			// more than it being tagged with git provenance.
218			return h.Open(ctx, path, label)
219		}
220		if res.Workspace.WorkspaceID != "" {
221			return res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, nil
222		}
223		return res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID, nil
224	}

226	// Close implements Runtime. This ends herdr's session state only — it never
227	// removes the checkout, the worktree or the branch, matching herdr's own
228	// separation of `workspace close` from `worktree remove`.
229	func (h *Herdr) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
230		if handle == "" {
231			return nil
232		}
233		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "close", handle)
234	}

236	// Annotate implements Runtime by reporting display-only workspace metadata.
237	//
238	// Note for users: a token only renders if the sidebar row layout in
239	// ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g. rows = [[..., "$stage"], ["$next"]].
240	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds silently and shows
241	// nothing.
242	func (h *Herdr) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
243		if handle == "" || len(kv) == 0 {
244			return nil
245		}
246		args := []string{"workspace", "report-metadata", handle, "--source", h.metadataSource}
247		for k, v := range kv {
248			if v == "" {
249				args = append(args, "--clear-token", k)
250				continue
251			}
252			args = append(args, "--token", k+"="+v)
253		}
254		return h.call(ctx, nil, args...)
255	}

257	func keys(m map[string]bool) []string {
258		if len(m) == 0 {
259			return nil
260		}
261		out := make([]string, 0, len(m))
262		for k := range m {
263			out = append(out, k)
264		}
265		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
266			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
267				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
268			}
269		}
270		return out
271	}

1	// Package skill embeds and installs dev's agent skill.
2	//
3	// The binary is the authority for its own skill, the same way `herdr --skill`
4	// is: a skill vendored separately drifts from the tool it documents, and an
5	// agent reading a stale command list is worse than one reading none. Embedding
6	// means the skill shipped is always the skill this build implements.
7	package skill
8
9	import (
10		"embed"
11		"fmt"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14		"path/filepath"
15		"strings"
16	)
17
18	//go:embed all:dev-cli
19	var files embed.FS
20
21	// Name is the skill's directory and frontmatter name.
22	//
23	// Deliberately not "dev", matching the binary: a skill is selected by its name
24	// and description, and "dev" describes nothing. The binary is typed dozens of
25	// times a day and should stay short; the skill is read by an agent deciding
26	// whether it is relevant, and should say what it covers.
27	const Name = "dev-cli"
28
29	// Render returns the SKILL.md body.
30	func Render() (string, error) {
31		b, err := files.ReadFile("dev-cli/SKILL.md")
32		if err != nil {
33			return "", fmt.Errorf("bundled skill is missing: %w", err)
34		}
35		return string(b), nil
36	}
37
38	// Files walks the embedded skill tree, yielding relative paths and contents.
39	func Files() (map[string][]byte, error) {
40		out := map[string][]byte{}
41		err := fs.WalkDir(files, "dev-cli", func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
42			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
43				return err
44			}
45			b, err := files.ReadFile(p)
46			if err != nil {
47				return err
48			}
49			out[strings.TrimPrefix(p, "dev-cli/")] = b
50			return nil
51		})
52		return out, err
53	}
54
55	// InstallResult reports what an install changed.
56	type InstallResult struct {
57		Dir     string
58		Written []string
59		Skipped []string
60		Links   []string
61	}
62
63	// DefaultDir is where the skill is installed: the shared agent skills
64	// directory, which Claude Code, Codex and others all read.
65	func DefaultDir() string {
66		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
67		return filepath.Join(home, ".agents", "skills", Name)
68	}
69
70	// LinkDirs are the tool-specific directories that get a symlink back to the
71	// shared install, matching the layout these tools already use.
72	func LinkDirs() []string {
73		home, _ := os.UserHomeDir()
74		return []string{filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "skills")}
75	}
76
77	// Install writes the embedded skill to dir and links it into the per-tool
78	// skill directories. Writes are content-compared first, so re-running is a
79	// no-op and does not churn mtimes that other tools watch.
80	func Install(dir string, link bool) (InstallResult, error) {
81		res := InstallResult{Dir: dir}
82		all, err := Files()
83		if err != nil {
84			return res, err
85		}
86		if len(all) == 0 {
87			return res, fmt.Errorf("no skill files are embedded in this build")
88		}
89
90		for rel, content := range all {
91			dst := filepath.Join(dir, rel)
92			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o755); err != nil {
93				return res, err
94			}
95			if existing, err := os.ReadFile(dst); err == nil && string(existing) == string(content) {
96				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, rel)
97				continue
98			}
99			if err := os.WriteFile(dst, content, 0o644); err != nil {
100				return res, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", dst, err)
101			}
102			res.Written = append(res.Written, rel)
103		}
104
105		if !link {
106			return res, nil
107		}
108		for _, base := range LinkDirs() {
109			if _, err := os.Stat(base); err != nil {
110				continue // that tool is not installed here
111			}
112			target := filepath.Join(base, Name)
113			if existing, err := os.Readlink(target); err == nil {
114				if resolveLink(base, existing) == dir {
115					continue // already correct
116				}
117				os.Remove(target)
118			} else if _, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil {
119				// A real directory, not our symlink: never clobber it.
120				continue
121			}
122			if err := os.Symlink(dir, target); err != nil {
123				return res, fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", target, err)
124			}
125			res.Links = append(res.Links, target)
126		}
127		return res, nil
128	}
129
130	func resolveLink(base, link string) string {
131		if filepath.IsAbs(link) {
132			return filepath.Clean(link)
133		}
134		return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(base, link))
135	}

29		return &cobra.Command{
30			Use:   "print",
31			Short: "Print SKILL.md to stdout",
32			Args:  cobra.NoArgs,
33			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
34				out, err := skill.Render()
35				if err != nil {
36					return err
37				}
38				fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
39				return nil
40			},
41		}
42	}
43
44	func newSkillInstallCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
45		var (
46			dir    string
47			noLink bool
48		)
49		cmd := &cobra.Command{
50			Use:   "install",
51			Short: "Install the skill into the agent skills directory",
52			Long: `Write the bundled skill to ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli and symlink it into the
53	per-tool skill directories that exist on this machine (~/.claude/skills).
54
55	Re-running is a no-op when nothing changed, so this is safe to call from a
56	dotfiles bootstrap on every apply.`,
57			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
58			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
59				target := dir
60				if target == "" {
61					target = skill.DefaultDir()
62				}
63				res, err := skill.Install(config.Expand(target), !noLink)
64				if err != nil {
65					return err
66				}
67				switch {
68				case len(res.Written) == 0:
69					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "skill already current at %s\n", config.Contract(res.Dir))
70				default:
71					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "installed %d file(s) to %s\n", len(res.Written), config.Contract(res.Dir))
72					for _, f := range res.Written {
73						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   %s\n", f)
74					}
75				}
76				for _, l := range res.Links {
77					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   linked %s\n", config.Contract(l))
78				}
79				return nil
80			},
81		}
82		f := cmd.Flags()
83		f.StringVar(&dir, "dir", "", "install directory (default: ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli)")
84		f.BoolVar(&noLink, "no-link", false, "do not symlink into per-tool skill directories")
85		return cmd
86	}

88	func newSkillSyncCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
89		var check bool
90		cmd := &cobra.Command{
91			Use:   "sync",
92			Short: "Regenerate the skill's command reference from the live command tree",
93			Long: `Rewrite the generated section of the skill's command reference from this
94	binary's actual command tree, so the documented flags can never drift from the
95	implemented ones.
96
97	With --check, report drift and exit non-zero instead of writing — the form to
98	wire into CI or a pre-push hook.`,
99			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
100			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
101				generated := generateCommandReference(cmd.Root())
102				return syncCommandReference(app, generated, check)
103			},
104		}
105		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&check, "check", false, "report drift and exit non-zero instead of writing")
106		return cmd
107	}
108
109	// generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
110	// the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
111	func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
112		var b strings.Builder
113		b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
114		writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
115		return b.String()
116	}
117
118	func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
119		if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" || c.Name() == "completion" {
120			return
121		}
122		if depth > 0 {
123			fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
124			if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
125				fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
126			}
127			if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
128				b.WriteString(flags)
129				b.WriteString("\n")
130			}
131		}
132		for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
133			writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
134		}
135	}
136
137	func renderFlags(c *cobra.Command) string {
138		var b strings.Builder
139		c.LocalNonPersistentFlags().VisitAll(func(f *pflag.Flag) {
140			if f.Hidden {
141				return
142			}
143			name := "--" + f.Name
144			if f.Shorthand != "" {
145				name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
146			}
147			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
148		})
149		return b.String()
150	}
151
152	func firstLine(s string) string {
153		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
154			return s[:i]
155		}
156		return s
157	}

3	import (

11	// Markers delimit the generated block inside the skill's command reference,
12	// so the hand-written parts of that file survive a regeneration.
13	const (
14		genBegin = "<!-- BEGIN GENERATED COMMANDS -->"
15		genEnd   = "<!-- END GENERATED COMMANDS -->"
16	)
17
18	// commandReferencePath is the file `dev skill sync` maintains, relative to the
19	// repository root. Sync only makes sense when run from a checkout of dev
20	// itself — the installed binary's copy is embedded and immutable.
21	const commandReferencePath = "internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md"
22
23	// syncCommandReference writes the generated block into the skill source, or
24	// reports drift when check is set.
25	func syncCommandReference(app *App, generated string, check bool) error {
26		path, err := findSkillSource()
27		if err != nil {
28			return err
29		}
30		current, err := os.ReadFile(path)
31		if err != nil {
32			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
33		}
34		updated, err := replaceBlock(string(current), generated)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38
39		if string(current) == updated {
40			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "command reference is current (%s)\n", commandReferencePath)
41			return nil
42		}
43		if check {
44			return errors.New("the skill's command reference is out of date — run `dev skill sync`")
45		}
46		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
47			return err
48		}
49		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "updated %s\n", commandReferencePath)
50		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "rebuild dev so the embedded copy matches: go build ./cmd/dev")
51		return nil
52	}
53
54	// replaceBlock swaps the content between the generated markers.
55	func replaceBlock(doc, generated string) (string, error) {
56		start := strings.Index(doc, genBegin)
57		end := strings.Index(doc, genEnd)
58		if start < 0 || end < 0 || end < start {
59			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing the %s / %s markers", genBegin, genEnd)
60		}
61		return doc[:start+len(genBegin)] + "\n\n" + generated + doc[end:], nil
62	}
63
64	// findSkillSource walks up from the working directory looking for dev's own
65	// checkout, so `dev skill sync` works from anywhere inside it.
66	func findSkillSource() (string, error) {
67		dir, err := os.Getwd()
68		if err != nil {
69			return "", err
70		}
71		for {
72			candidate := filepath.Join(dir, commandReferencePath)
73			if _, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil {
74				return candidate, nil
75			}
76			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
77			if parent == dir {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s not found — run `dev skill sync` from a checkout of dev-cli itself",
79					commandReferencePath)
80			}
81			dir = parent
82		}
83	}

3	import (
4		"errors"

11	// Markers delimit the generated block inside the skill's command reference,
12	// so the hand-written parts of that file survive a regeneration.
13	const (
14		genBegin = "<!-- BEGIN GENERATED COMMANDS -->"
15		genEnd   = "<!-- END GENERATED COMMANDS -->"
16	)
17
18	// commandReferencePath is the file `dev skill sync` maintains, relative to the
19	// repository root. Sync only makes sense when run from a checkout of dev
20	// itself — the installed binary's copy is embedded and immutable.
21	const commandReferencePath = "internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md"
22
23	// syncCommandReference writes the generated block into the skill source, or
24	// reports drift when check is set.
25	func syncCommandReference(app *App, generated string, check bool) error {
26		path, err := findSkillSource()
27		if err != nil {
28			return err
29		}
30		current, err := os.ReadFile(path)
31		if err != nil {
32			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
33		}
34		updated, err := replaceBlock(string(current), generated)
35		if err != nil {
36			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", path, err)
37		}
38
39		if string(current) == updated {
40			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "command reference is current (%s)\n", commandReferencePath)
41			return nil
42		}
43		if check {
44			return errors.New("the skill's command reference is out of date — run `dev skill sync`")
45		}
46		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(updated), 0o644); err != nil {
47			return err
48		}
49		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "updated %s\n", commandReferencePath)
50		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "rebuild dev so the embedded copy matches: go build ./cmd/dev")
51		return nil
52	}
53
54	// replaceBlock swaps the content between the generated markers.
55	func replaceBlock(doc, generated string) (string, error) {
56		start := strings.Index(doc, genBegin)
57		end := strings.Index(doc, genEnd)
58		if start < 0 || end < 0 || end < start {
59			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing the %s / %s markers", genBegin, genEnd)
60		}
61		return doc[:start+len(genBegin)] + "\n\n" + generated + doc[end:], nil
62	}
63
64	// findSkillSource walks up from the working directory looking for dev's own
65	// checkout, so `dev skill sync` works from anywhere inside it.
66	func findSkillSource() (string, error) {
67		dir, err := os.Getwd()
68		if err != nil {
69			return "", err
70		}
71		for {
72			candidate := filepath.Join(dir, commandReferencePath)
73			if _, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil {
74				return candidate, nil
75			}
76			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
77			if parent == dir {
78				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s not found — run `dev skill sync` from a checkout of dev-cli itself",
79					commandReferencePath)
80			}
81			dir = parent
82		}
83	}
84

1	// Package ignore assembles .gitignore files from GitHub's published templates
2	// plus the entries that every repository on a given machine wants but no
3	// language template includes.
4	//
5	// The split matters: a Python template says nothing about .DS_Store, and
6	// nothing at all about the worktree directories an agent harness creates —
7	// which, left untracked, show up as noise in every status.
8	package ignore
9
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"embed"
13		"fmt"
14		"io"
15		"net/http"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"
18		"sort"
19		"strings"
20		"time"
21	)
22
23	//go:embed all:templates
24	var bundled embed.FS
25
26	// TemplateAPI is GitHub's public gitignore endpoint. It needs no
27	// authentication, which is what lets this work before `gh auth login`.
28	const TemplateAPI = "https://api.github.com/gitignore/templates"
29
30	// Source records where a section's content came from, so the generated file
31	// can say so honestly.
32	type Source string
33
34	const (
35		// SourceRemote is GitHub's template API.
36		SourceRemote Source = "github"
37		// SourceCache is a previously fetched template on disk.
38		SourceCache Source = "cache"
39		// SourceBundled is a template compiled into the binary.
40		SourceBundled Source = "bundled"
41	)
42
43	// Section is one named block of the generated file.
44	type Section struct {
45		Name   string
46		Body   string
47		Source Source
48	}
49
50	// Fetcher resolves template names to content, preferring the network and
51	// falling back through the cache to the bundled copies.
52	type Fetcher struct {
53		CacheDir string
54		Client   *http.Client
55		// Offline skips the network entirely.
56		Offline bool
57		// BaseURL overrides the template endpoint; empty means TemplateAPI.
58		BaseURL string
59	}
60
61	// NewFetcher returns a fetcher caching under dir.
62	func NewFetcher(cacheDir string) *Fetcher {
63		return &Fetcher{
64			CacheDir: cacheDir,
65			Client:   &http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second},
66		}
67	}
68
69	// Get resolves one template by name, case-insensitively ("python", "Python",
70	// "PYTHON" all work, because nobody remembers GitHub's capitalisation).
71	func (f *Fetcher) Get(ctx context.Context, name string) (Section, error) {
72		canonical := Canonical(name)
73
74		if !f.Offline {
75			body, err := f.fetch(ctx, canonical)
76			if err == nil {
77				f.writeCache(canonical, body)
78				return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceRemote}, nil
79			}
80		}
81		if body, ok := f.readCache(canonical); ok {
82			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceCache}, nil
83		}
84		if body, ok := bundledTemplate(canonical); ok {
85			return Section{Name: canonical, Body: body, Source: SourceBundled}, nil
86		}
87		return Section{}, fmt.Errorf("no gitignore template for %q (offline, and no cached or bundled copy);"+
88			" available offline: %s", name, strings.Join(BundledNames(), ", "))
89	}
90
91	// Canonical normalises a template name to GitHub's own capitalisation where
92	// it is known, and otherwise title-cases the input.
93	func Canonical(name string) string {
94		lower := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))
95		if c, ok := knownNames[lower]; ok {
96			return c
97		}
98		if lower == "" {
99			return ""
100		}
101		return strings.ToUpper(lower[:1]) + lower[1:]
102	}
103
104	// knownNames maps the spellings people type to GitHub's file names. Only the
105	// cases where they differ need an entry.
106	var knownNames = map[string]string{
107		"python": "Python", "node": "Node", "nodejs": "Node", "js": "Node",
108		"javascript": "Node", "typescript": "Node", "ts": "Node",
109		"go": "Go", "golang": "Go", "rust": "Rust", "java": "Java",
110		"ruby": "Ruby", "elixir": "Elixir", "c": "C", "c++": "C++", "cpp": "C++",
111		"swift": "Swift", "kotlin": "Kotlin", "scala": "Scala", "haskell": "Haskell",
112		"r": "R", "julia": "Julia", "dart": "Dart", "flutter": "Dart",
113		"terraform": "Terraform", "unity": "Unity", "godot": "Godot",
114		"tex": "TeX", "latex": "TeX", "zig": "Zig", "lua": "Lua", "perl": "Perl",
115		"php": "Composer", "laravel": "Laravel", "rails": "Rails",
116		"android": "Android", "objective-c": "Objective-C", "objc": "Objective-C",
117		"csharp": "VisualStudio", "c#": "VisualStudio", "dotnet": "VisualStudio",
118	}
119
120	func (f *Fetcher) fetch(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, error) {
121		base := f.BaseURL
122		if base == "" {
123			base = TemplateAPI
124		}
125		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, base+"/"+name, nil)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/vnd.github.raw")
130		client := f.Client
131		if client == nil {
132			client = http.DefaultClient
133		}
134		resp, err := client.Do(req)
135		if err != nil {
136			return "", err
137		}
138		defer resp.Body.Close()
139		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
140			return "", fmt.Errorf("github returned %s for %s", resp.Status, name)
141		}
142		body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))
143		if err != nil {
144			return "", err
145		}
146		// The raw media type returns the file itself; if a proxy ignored the
147		// Accept header we would get JSON, which is not a usable gitignore.
148		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(string(body)), "{") {
149			return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected JSON response for %s", name)
150		}
151		return strings.TrimRight(string(body), "\n"), nil
152	}
153
154	func (f *Fetcher) cachePath(name string) string {
155		if f.CacheDir == "" {
156			return ""
157		}
158		return filepath.Join(f.CacheDir, name+".gitignore")
159	}
160
161	func (f *Fetcher) readCache(name string) (string, bool) {
162		p := f.cachePath(name)
163		if p == "" {
164			return "", false
165		}
166		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
167		if err != nil {
168			return "", false
169		}
170		return strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\n"), true
171	}
172
173	func (f *Fetcher) writeCache(name, body string) {
174		p := f.cachePath(name)
175		if p == "" {
176			return
177		}
178		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755); err != nil {
179			return // caching is an optimisation; failing to cache is not an error
180		}
181		_ = os.WriteFile(p, []byte(body+"\n"), 0o644)
182	}
183
184	func bundledTemplate(name string) (string, bool) {
185		b, err := bundled.ReadFile("templates/" + name + ".gitignore")
186		if err != nil {
187			return "", false
188		}
189		return strings.TrimRight(string(b), "\n"), true
190	}
191
192	// BundledNames lists the templates available with no network at all.
193	func BundledNames() []string {
194		entries, err := bundled.ReadDir("templates")
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil
197		}
198		var out []string
199		for _, e := range entries {
200			out = append(out, strings.TrimSuffix(e.Name(), ".gitignore"))
201		}
202		sort.Strings(out)
203		return out
204	}
205
