```go
package cli_test

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestGitignoreAgentArtifactContract(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "/dev/null")
	t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM", "/dev/null")

	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Chdir(h.repo.Root); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.Chdir(cwd) })

	h.mustRun("gitignore", "go", "--offline")

	tests := []struct {
		name        string
		path        string
		wantIgnored bool
	}{
		{name: "worktree state", path: ".claude/worktrees/task/file", wantIgnored: true},
		{name: "local Claude settings", path: ".claude/settings.local.json", wantIgnored: true},
		{name: "aider state", path: ".aider.conf.yml", wantIgnored: true},
		{name: "generated Cursor rules", path: ".cursor/rules/_generated/rule.md", wantIgnored: true},
		{name: "SpecStory history", path: ".specstory/history/session.md"},
		{name: "Claude plan", path: ".claude/plans/plan.md"},
		{name: "Cursor plan", path: ".cursor/plans/plan.md"},
		{name: "OpenCode plan", path: ".opencode/plans/plan.md"},
		{name: "Specify artifact", path: ".specify/spec.md"},
		{name: "Codex artifact", path: ".codex/plan.md"},
	}

	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			cmd := exec.Command("git", "check-ignore", "--no-index", "-q", "--", tc.path)
			cmd.Dir = h.repo.Root
			output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
			ignored := err == nil
			if err != nil {
				var exitErr *exec.ExitError
				if !errors.As(err, &exitErr) || exitErr.ExitCode() != 1 {
					t.Fatalf("git check-ignore %s: %v\n%s", filepath.ToSlash(tc.path), err, output)
				}
			}
			if ignored != tc.wantIgnored {
				t.Errorf("git considers %s ignored = %v, want %v", filepath.ToSlash(tc.path), ignored, tc.wantIgnored)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```text
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os/exec"
14		"strings"
15	)
16
17	// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
18	type Session struct {
19		// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
20		// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
21		Handle string
22		Label  string
23		// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
24		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
25		// value.
26		Dirs []string
27		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
28		// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
29		AgentStatus string
30		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
31		AgentSessions []string
32		Focused       bool
33	}
34
35	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
36	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
37		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
38			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
39			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
40			// $HOME active.
41			if d == dir || strings.HasPrefix(d, dir+"/") {
42				return true
43			}
44		}
45		return false
46	}
47
48	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
49	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
50	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
51	type Runtime interface {
52		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
53		Name() string
54		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
55		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
56		Available() bool
57		// Open makes dir live and returns a handle. Opening something already open
58		// focuses it rather than duplicating it.
59		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error)
60		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
61		// task entry.
62		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
63		// List enumerates live sessions.
64		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
65		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
66		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
67		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
68	}
69
70	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
71	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
72	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
73	type WorktreeOpener interface {
74		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error)
75	}
76
77	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
78	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
79
80	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
81		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
82	}
83
84	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
85	//
86	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
87	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then None.
88	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
89	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
90		herdr, tmux, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}
91		switch backend {
92		case "herdr":
93			return herdr
94		case "tmux":
95			return tmux
96		case "none":
97			return none
98		case "", "auto":
99			if herdr.Available() {
100				return herdr
101			}
102			if tmux.Available() {
103				return tmux
104			}
105			return none
106		}
107		return none
108	}
109
110	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
111	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), None{}} }
112
113	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
114	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
115		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
116		return err == nil
117	}
118
```

```text
13	// Herdr drives the herdr terminal workspace manager over its CLI, which emits
14	// JSON on stdout for every subcommand dev needs.
15	//
16	// Division of responsibility, deliberately: dev creates worktrees with plain
17	// `git worktree add` at its own configured path and then asks herdr to *open*
18	// that path. `herdr worktree create` is not used, because it would put the
19	// path policy in a second place — and that policy has to hold on machines
20	// where herdr is not installed at all.
21	type Herdr struct {
22		bin string
23		// metadataSource namespaces the workspace metadata tokens dev reports.
24		metadataSource string
25	}
26
27	// NewHerdr returns the herdr adapter.
28	func NewHerdr() *Herdr { return &Herdr{bin: "herdr", metadataSource: "dev"} }
29
30	// WithMetadataSource sets the --source id used for workspace metadata tokens.
31	func (h *Herdr) WithMetadataSource(src string) *Herdr {
32		if src != "" {
33			h.metadataSource = src
34		}
35		return h
36	}
37
38	// Name implements Runtime.
39	func (h *Herdr) Name() string { return "herdr" }
40
41	// Available reports whether the binary exists *and* a server is reachable.
42	// The binary alone is not enough: every dev call goes through the socket API,
43	// so a stopped server must degrade to the next backend rather than making
44	// every command fail.
45	func (h *Herdr) Available() bool {
46		if !haveBinary(h.bin) {
47			return false
48		}
49		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
50		defer cancel()
51		_, err := h.run(ctx, "workspace", "list")
52		return err == nil
53	}
54
55	func (h *Herdr) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
56		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, h.bin, args...)
57		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
58		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
59		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
60			msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
61			if msg == "" {
62				msg = err.Error()
63			}
64			return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
65		}
66		return stdout.Bytes(), nil
67	}

69	// herdrEnvelope is the common shape of every herdr CLI JSON response.
70	type herdrEnvelope struct {
71		ID     string          `json:"id"`
72		Error  *herdrError     `json:"error"`
73		Result json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
74	}
75
76	type herdrError struct {
77		Code    string `json:"code"`
78		Message string `json:"message"`
79	}

81	// call runs a herdr subcommand and decodes result into out.
82	func (h *Herdr) call(ctx context.Context, out any, args ...string) error {
83		raw, err := h.run(ctx, args...)
84		if err != nil {
85			return err
86		}
87		var env herdrEnvelope
88		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &env); err != nil {
89			return fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: unexpected output: %w", strings.Join(args, " "), err)
90		}
91		if env.Error != nil {
92			return fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s (%s)", strings.Join(args, " "), env.Error.Message, env.Error.Code)
93		}
94		if out == nil {
95			return nil
96		}
97		return json.Unmarshal(env.Result, out)
98	}

127	// List implements Runtime. Workspaces carry no working directory of their own,
128	// so dev joins them against the pane list — panes are what actually have a cwd.
129	func (h *Herdr) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
130		var ws struct {
131			Workspaces []herdrWorkspace `json:"workspaces"`
132		}
133		if err := h.call(ctx, &ws, "workspace", "list"); err != nil {
134			return nil, err
135		}
136		var ps struct {
137			Panes []herdrPane `json:"panes"`
138		}
139		if err := h.call(ctx, &ps, "pane", "list"); err != nil {
140			// Directories are an enrichment; a workspace listing without them is
141			// still worth returning.
142			ps.Panes = nil
143		}
144
145		dirs := map[string]map[string]bool{}
146		agents := map[string]map[string]bool{}
147		for _, p := range ps.Panes {
148			if p.CWD != "" {
149				if dirs[p.WorkspaceID] == nil {
150					dirs[p.WorkspaceID] = map[string]bool{}
151				}
152				dirs[p.WorkspaceID][p.CWD] = true
153			}
154			if p.AgentSession != nil && p.AgentSession.Value != "" {
155				if agents[p.WorkspaceID] == nil {
156					agents[p.WorkspaceID] = map[string]bool{}
157				}
158				agents[p.WorkspaceID][p.AgentSession.Agent+":"+p.AgentSession.Value] = true
159			}
160		}
161
162		out := make([]Session, 0, len(ws.Workspaces))
163		for _, w := range ws.Workspaces {
164			out = append(out, Session{
165				Handle:        w.WorkspaceID,
166				Label:         w.Label,
167				Dirs:          keys(dirs[w.WorkspaceID]),
168				AgentSessions: keys(agents[w.WorkspaceID]),
169				AgentStatus:   w.AgentStatus,
170				Focused:       w.Focused,
171			})
172		}
173		return out, nil
174	}

176	// Open implements Runtime. An already-open directory is focused rather than
177	// opened twice.
178	func (h *Herdr) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error) {
179		if existing, err := h.List(ctx); err == nil {
180			for _, s := range existing {
181				for _, d := range s.Dirs {
182					if d == dir {
183						_ = h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", s.Handle)
184						return s.Handle, nil
185					}
186				}
187			}
188		}
189		args := []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", dir, "--no-focus"}
190		if label != "" {
191			args = append(args, "--label", label)
192		}
193		var res struct {
194			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
195		}
196		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
197			return "", err
198		}
199		return res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, nil
200	}

202	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
203	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
204	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
205	// ahead/behind row.
206	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
207		args := []string{"worktree", "open", "--path", path, "--no-focus"}
208		if label != "" {
209			args = append(args, "--label", label)
210		}
211		var res struct {
212			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
213			Worktree  herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
214		}
215		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
216			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
217			// more than it being tagged with git provenance.
218			return h.Open(ctx, path, label)
219		}
220		if res.Workspace.WorkspaceID != "" {
221			return res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, nil
222		}
223		return res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID, nil
224	}
225
226	// Close implements Runtime. This ends herdr's session state only — it never
227	// removes the checkout, the worktree or the branch, matching herdr's own
228	// separation of `workspace close` from `worktree remove`.
229	func (h *Herdr) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
230		if handle == "" {
231			return nil
232		}
233		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "close", handle)
234	}
235
236	// Annotate implements Runtime by reporting display-only workspace metadata.
237	//
238	// Note for users: a token only renders if the sidebar row layout in
239	// ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g. rows = [[..., "$stage"], ["$next"]].
240	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds silently and shows
241	// nothing.
242	func (h *Herdr) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
243		if handle == "" || len(kv) == 0 {
244			return nil
245		}
246		args := []string{"workspace", "report-metadata", handle, "--source", h.metadataSource}
247		for k, v := range kv {
248			if v == "" {
249				args = append(args, "--clear-token", k)
250				continue
251			}
252			args = append(args, "--token", k+"="+v)
253		}
254		return h.call(ctx, nil, args...)
255	}
256
257	func keys(m map[string]bool) []string {
258		if len(m) == 0 {
259			return nil
260		}
261		out := make([]string, 0, len(m))
262		for k := range m {
263			out = append(out, k)
264		}
265		for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
266			for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
267				out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
268			}
269		}
270		return out
271	}
```

```text
11	// process can never change its parent's working directory.

14	// Name implements Runtime.

16
17	// Available implements Runtime; the null backend always is.

19
20	// Open implements Runtime by reporting the directory to change into.
21	func (None) Open(_ context.Context, dir, _ string) (string, error) { return dir, nil }
22
23	// Close implements Runtime as a no-op: there is no session to end.
24	func (None) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }
```

```text
1	package runtime
2
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"context"
6		"fmt"
7		"os/exec"
8		"regexp"
9		"strings"
10	)
11
12	// Tmux is the fallback backend for machines without herdr. It models a task as
13	// a named tmux session rooted at the checkout.
14	type Tmux struct{ bin string }
15
16	// NewTmux returns the tmux adapter.
17	func NewTmux() *Tmux { return &Tmux{bin: "tmux"} }
18
19	// Name implements Runtime.
20	func (t *Tmux) Name() string { return "tmux" }
21
22	// Available reports whether tmux is installed. Unlike herdr, tmux needs no
23	// running server for `new-session -d` to work, so presence is enough.
24	func (t *Tmux) Available() bool { return haveBinary(t.bin) }
25
26	func (t *Tmux) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) (string, error) {
27		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, t.bin, args...)
28		var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
29		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
30		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
31			msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
32			if msg == "" {
33				msg = err.Error()
34			}
35			return "", fmt.Errorf("tmux %s: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
36		}
37		return strings.TrimRight(stdout.String(), "\n"), nil
38	}
39
40	// tmuxUnsafe covers the characters tmux treats specially in session names:
41	// a "." or ":" would make the name ambiguous with window/pane addressing.
42	var tmuxUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[.:\s]+`)
43
44	// SessionName converts a task label into a legal tmux session name.
45	func SessionName(label string) string {
46		s := tmuxUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(label, "-")
47		s = strings.Trim(s, "-")
48		if s == "" {
49			return "dev"
50		}
51		return s
52	}
53
54	// List implements Runtime. An absent server means "no sessions", not an error.
55	func (t *Tmux) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
56		out, err := t.run(ctx, "list-sessions", "-F", "#{session_name}\t#{session_path}\t#{?session_attached,1,0}")
57		if err != nil {
58			// "no server running on ..." is the normal idle case.
59			if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "no server running") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "error connecting") {
60				return nil, nil
61			}
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		var sessions []Session
65		for _, line := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
66			if line == "" {
67				continue
68			}
69			f := strings.Split(line, "\t")
70			if len(f) < 2 {
71				continue
72			}
73			s := Session{Handle: f[0], Label: f[0], Dirs: []string{f[1]}}
74			if len(f) > 2 {
75				s.Focused = f[2] == "1"
76			}
77			sessions = append(sessions, s)
78		}
79		return sessions, nil
80	}
81
82	// Open implements Runtime, reusing a session that already exists under that
83	// name rather than creating a duplicate.
84	func (t *Tmux) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (string, error) {
85		name := SessionName(label)
86		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "has-session", "-t", "="+name); err == nil {
87			return name, nil
88		}
89		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "new-session", "-d", "-s", name, "-c", dir); err != nil {
90			return "", err
91		}
92		return name, nil
93	}
94
95	// Close implements Runtime: it kills the session only. The checkout is
96	// untouched.
97	func (t *Tmux) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
98		if handle == "" {
99			return nil
100		}
101		if _, err := t.run(ctx, "has-session", "-t", "="+handle); err != nil {
102			return nil // already gone
103		}
104		_, err := t.run(ctx, "kill-session", "-t", "="+handle)
105		return err
106	}
107
108	// Annotate implements Runtime. tmux has no metadata channel, so dev writes the
109	// task state into the session's user option, where a status-line format can
110	// pick it up with #{@dev_stage} if the user wants it.
111	func (t *Tmux) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
112		if handle == "" {
113			return nil
114		}
115		for k, v := range kv {
116			if _, err := t.run(ctx, "set-option", "-t", "="+handle, "-q", "@dev_"+k, v); err != nil {
117				return err
118			}
119		}
120		return nil
121	}
```

```text
79	func TestBackendContract(t *testing.T) {
```

```text
17	// Manager creates and removes worktrees according to the configured policy.
18	type Manager struct {
19		Cfg config.Config
20		// Runtime surfaces a new checkout in the multiplexer. May be nil.
21		Runtime runtime.Runtime
22		Log     io.Writer
23	}
24
25	// CreateRequest describes one worktree to create.
26	type CreateRequest struct {
27		// RepoPath is the main checkout that owns the worktree.
28		RepoPath string
29		// RepoName is used in the path template and as the session label.
30		RepoName string
31		// Branch is the change stream. Created from Base when it does not exist.
32		Branch string
33		// Base is the ref a new branch starts from.
34		//
35		// Passing this explicitly matters more than it looks: without a base, git
36		// branches from the current HEAD, so a worktree created while standing on
37		// feature/A silently inherits feature/A's commits.
38		Base string
39		// Category feeds the path template.
40		Category string
41		// Path overrides the templated location entirely.
42		Path string
43		// Label names the runtime session.
44		Label string
45		// NoProvision skips dependency install and gitignored-file copying.
46		NoProvision bool
47		// NoRuntime skips surfacing the checkout in the multiplexer.
48		NoRuntime bool
49		// Focus opens the runtime session focused.
50		Focus bool
51	}
52
53	// CreateResult reports what was created.
54	type CreateResult struct {
55		Path          string
56		Branch        string
57		BranchCreated bool
58		Provision     Result
59		RuntimeHandle string
60		RuntimeName   string
61	}
62
63	// ErrExists reports a worktree that is already checked out for that branch.
64	type ErrExists struct {
65		Branch string
66		Path   string
67	}
68
69	func (e *ErrExists) Error() string {
70		return fmt.Sprintf("branch %s is already checked out at %s", e.Branch, e.Path)
71	}
72
73	func (m *Manager) logf(format string, args ...any) {
74		if m.Log != nil {
75			fmt.Fprintf(m.Log, format+"\n", args...)
76		}
77	}
78
79	// Create adds a linked worktree, provisions it and surfaces it in the runtime.
80	func (m *Manager) Create(ctx context.Context, req CreateRequest) (*CreateResult, error) {
81		if req.Branch == "" {
82			return nil, errors.New("branch is required")
83		}
84		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, req.RepoPath)
85		if err != nil {
86			return nil, err
87		}
88		// Always operate from the main checkout: creating a worktree from inside
89		// another worktree works, but the relative paths and the base ref get
90		// confusing fast.
91		repoPath := repo.MainRoot
92		if req.RepoName == "" {
93			req.RepoName = repo.Name
94		}
95
96		// Git refuses to check one branch out twice, so an existing worktree for
97		// this branch is a reuse, not an error the user needs to resolve.
98		if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch); err == nil && ok {
99			return nil, &ErrExists{Branch: req.Branch, Path: existing.Path}
100		}
101
102		path := req.Path
103		if path == "" {
104			path, err = m.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(req.RepoName, repoPath, req.Branch, req.Category)
105			if err != nil {
106				return nil, err
107			}
108		} else {
109			path = config.Expand(path)
110		}
111		if err := m.checkTarget(path, repoPath); err != nil {
112			return nil, err
113		}
114
115		base := req.Base
116		branchExisted := gitx.BranchExists(ctx, repoPath, req.Branch)
117		if !branchExisted {
118			if base == "" {
119				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
120			}
121			if base != "" && !gitx.RefExists(ctx, repoPath, base) {
122				return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, repoPath)
123			}
124		}
125
126		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
127			return nil, fmt.Errorf("create worktree parent: %w", err)
128		}
129		if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, repoPath, path, req.Branch, base); err != nil {
130			return nil, err
131		}
132		m.logf("worktree %s -> %s", req.Branch, config.Contract(path))
133
134		res := &CreateResult{Path: path, Branch: req.Branch, BranchCreated: !branchExisted}
135
136		if !req.NoProvision {
137			// SettingsFor folds in the repo's own .dev.toml, so a project can pin
138			// its setup where a teammate on another machine picks it up too.
139			p := &Provisioner{
140				Settings: SettingsFor(m.Cfg, repoPath),
141				Timeout:  m.Cfg.Worktree.ProvisionTimeout.Duration,
142				Log:      m.Log,
143			}
144			pr, err := p.Provision(ctx, repoPath, path)
145			if err != nil {
146				// The checkout exists and is usable; provisioning is best-effort.
147				m.logf("warning: provisioning: %v", err)
148			}
149			res.Provision = pr
150		}
151
152		if !req.NoRuntime && m.Runtime != nil {
153			label := req.Label
154			if label == "" {
155				label = req.RepoName + "/" + req.Branch
156			}
157			handle, err := m.surface(ctx, path, label)
158			if err != nil {
159				m.logf("warning: could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
160			} else if m.Runtime.Name() != "none" {
161				res.RuntimeHandle, res.RuntimeName = handle, m.Runtime.Name()
162			}
163		}
164		return res, nil
165	}
166
167	// surface registers the checkout with the runtime. When the backend
168	// understands git worktrees it is asked to open it as one, which is what makes
169	// the checkout appear grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
170	// ahead/behind row rather than as an unrelated directory.
171	func (m *Manager) surface(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (string, error) {
172		if wo, ok := m.Runtime.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
173			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, path, label)
174		}
175		return m.Runtime.Open(ctx, path, label)
176	}
177
178	// checkTarget refuses locations that would cause trouble later.
179	func (m *Manager) checkTarget(path, repoPath string) error {
180		if info, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
181			if !info.IsDir() {
182				return fmt.Errorf("%s exists and is not a directory", path)
183			}
184			entries, err := os.ReadDir(path)
185			if err != nil {
186				return err
187			}
188			if len(entries) > 0 {
189				return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists and is not empty", config.Contract(path))
190			}
191		}
192		// A worktree nested inside another checkout means every indexer, file
193		// watcher and ripgrep run in the outer repo sees a second copy of the
194		// tree. dev keeps checkouts as siblings under the worktree root instead.
195		if path == repoPath || strings.HasPrefix(path, repoPath+string(filepath.Separator)) {
196			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create a worktree inside the repository (%s); "+
197				"set paths.worktree_path to a location outside %s",
198				config.Contract(path), config.Contract(repoPath))
199		}
200		return nil
201	}
202
203	// RemoveRequest describes a worktree removal.
204	type RemoveRequest struct {
205		RepoPath string
206		Path     string
207		// Force allows removing a checkout with uncommitted changes. dev never
208		// sets this on its own: losing uncommitted work is exactly the outcome the
209		// tool exists to prevent.
210		Force bool
211		// RuntimeHandle is closed before the checkout is removed, so the
212		// multiplexer is not left pointing at a deleted directory.
213		RuntimeHandle string
214	}
215
216	// Remove deletes a worktree checkout. It never deletes the branch — that stays
217	// a separate, explicit decision, matching git's own separation.
218	func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, req RemoveRequest) error {
219		if req.RuntimeHandle != "" && m.Runtime != nil {
220			if err := m.Runtime.Close(ctx, req.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
221				m.logf("warning: could not close runtime session %s: %v", req.RuntimeHandle, err)
222			}
223		}
224		if _, err := os.Stat(req.Path); errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
225			// The directory is already gone; clear git's administrative entry.
226			return gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, req.RepoPath)
227		}
228		if err := gitx.RemoveWorktree(ctx, req.RepoPath, req.Path, req.Force); err != nil {
229			return err
230		}
231		m.logf("removed worktree %s", config.Contract(req.Path))
232		return nil
233	}
234
235	// DirtyCheck reports whether a checkout has uncommitted work, so callers can
236	// refuse to remove it without an explicit --force.
237	func DirtyCheck(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, gitx.Status, error) {
238		st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, path)
239		if err != nil {
240			return false, st, err
241		}
242		return st.Dirty(), st, nil
243	}
```

```text
332	func TestStrategySafety(t *testing.T) {
333		python := wt.DetectEcosystems(withFiles(t, "uv.lock"))[0]
334		node := wt.DetectEcosystems(withFiles(t, "package-lock.json"))[0]
335
336		// A virtualenv cannot survive being copied or shared; node_modules can be
337		// copied but should not be shared.
338		if ok, why := python.SupportsStrategy(wt.Copy); ok {
339			t.Error("copying a virtualenv must not be allowed")
340		} else if why == "" {
341			t.Error("a refusal must explain itself")
342		}
343		if ok, _ := python.SupportsStrategy(wt.Link); ok {
344			t.Error("sharing a virtualenv must not be allowed")
345		}
346		if ok, _ := node.SupportsStrategy(wt.Copy); !ok {
347			t.Error("node_modules copies soundly")
348		}
349		if ok, _ := node.SupportsStrategy(wt.Link); ok {
350			t.Error("sharing one node_modules between checkouts should not be a default-allowed strategy")
351		}
352		for _, e := range []wt.Ecosystem{python, node} {
353			for _, s := range []wt.Strategy{wt.Reinstall, wt.Skip} {
354				if ok, _ := e.SupportsStrategy(s); !ok {
355					t.Errorf("%s should always support %s", e.Name, s)
356				}
357			}
358		}
359	}

372	// asErr is errors.As without importing errors into every call site.
373	func asErr[T error](err error, target *T) bool {
374		for err != nil {
375			if t, ok := err.(T); ok {
376				*target = t
377				return true
378			}
379			u, ok := err.(interface{ Unwrap() error })
380			if !ok {
381				return false
382			}
383			err = u.Unwrap()
384		}
385		return false
386	}
```

```text
34
35	  default        create a branch + linked worktree, provision it, open a
36	                 runtime session, and record the task. Safest for work that
37	                 may be interrupted or run in parallel.
38	  --branch-only  create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout, with no
39	                 worktree. Lighter, but that checkout cannot host another
40	                 branch concurrently.
41	  --direct       track the branch already checked out in the canonical repo —
42	                 usually main — without creating either a branch or worktree.
43	                 Best for one-session ad-hoc changes.
44
45	For untracked ad-hoc navigation, use "dev repo open" or press Enter in the
46	TUI's REPOS view; that opens the project without creating any task at all.
47
48	With no repo argument, the repository containing the current directory is used.
49	Always pass --base for an unattended branch/worktree task.`,
50			Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
51			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
52				ctx := ctxOf()
53				if direct && (branchOnly || noWorktree) {
54					return errors.New("--direct and --branch-only are different modes; pick one")
55				}
56				branchOnly = branchOnly || noWorktree
57
58				// Resolve the repository: an explicit argument, else the cwd.
59				var repoPath, repoName, category string
60				if len(args) == 1 {
61					r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.ScanRoots(), args[0])

64					}

68					if err != nil {
69						return err
70					}

72					if err != nil {

74					}
75					repoPath, repoName = g.MainRoot, g.Name
76				}
77

79					if branch != "" && !direct {
80						name = branch
81					} else {

83					}
84				}
85

96					}

100					}
101					branch, base = st.Branch, st.Branch
102
103				case branchOnly:
104					mode = task.ModeBranch

106						branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
107					}
108					if base == "" {

110					}
111
112				default:

114						branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
115					}
116					if base == "" {
117						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
118					}
119				}
120
121				id := task.MakeID(repoName, branch)
122				if existing, err := app.Tasks.Get(id); err == nil && existing.State != task.Done {
123					return fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
124						existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
125				}
126
127				t := &task.Task{
128					Name: name, Repo: repoName, RepoPath: repoPath,
129					Branch: branch, Base: base, Mode: mode,
130					State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(), Next: next,
131				}

133
134				switch mode {

136					handle, err := rt.Open(ctx, repoPath, repoName+"/"+name)
137					if err != nil {
138						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
139					} else if rt.Name() != "none" {
140						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
141					}
142
143				case task.ModeBranch:

145						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "switch", branch); err != nil {
146							return fmt.Errorf("switch to %s: %w", branch, err)
147						}
148					} else {
149						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "switch", "-c", branch, base); err != nil {
150							return fmt.Errorf("create and switch to %s from %s: %w", branch, base, err)
151						}
152					}
153					handle, err := rt.Open(ctx, repoPath, repoName+"/"+branch)

210	// checkoutOf is where a task's code lives right now.
211	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
212		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
213			return t.WorktreePath
214		}
215		return t.RepoPath
216	}
217
218	// annotate pushes the task's state and next action into the runtime as
219	// display-only metadata, so a sidebar can show why a session is open without
220	// anyone having to ask dev.
221	//
222	// For herdr this lands as workspace metadata tokens. A token only renders if
223	// the sidebar row layout in ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g.
224	//
225	//	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
226	//	rows = [["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"], ["branch", "git_status"], ["$next"]]
227	//
228	// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds and shows nothing,
229	// which is why dev never treats a failure here as an error.
230	func annotate(app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, t *task.Task) {
231		if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
232			return
233		}
234		kv := map[string]string{
235			"stage": t.State.Label(),
236			"next":  t.Next,
237		}
238		if err := rt.Annotate(ctxOf(), t.RuntimeHandle, kv); err != nil {
239			app.warnf("could not annotate the runtime session: %v", err)
240		}
241	}

243	func reportProvision(app *App, res *wt.CreateResult) {
244		p := res.Provision
245		if n := len(p.Copied); n > 0 {
246			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   copied    %d gitignored file(s): %s\n", n, strings.Join(p.Copied, ", "))
247		}
248		if n := len(p.Linked); n > 0 {
249			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   linked    %s\n", strings.Join(p.Linked, ", "))
250		}
251		for _, e := range p.Failures {
252			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "   warning   %v\n", e)
253		}
254	}
```

```text
11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its
12	// parent repo in a sidebar instead of listing it as an unrelated directory.
13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (string, error) {
```

```text
14	func newResumeCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			noProvision bool
17			fetch       bool
18			force       bool
19		)
20		cmd := &cobra.Command{
21			Use:   "resume <task>",
22			Short: "Pick a task back up, rebuilding whatever is missing",
23			Long: `Make a parked task hot again.
24
25	Warm tasks still have their worktree, so this just reopens a runtime session.
26	Cold tasks do not: the worktree is rebuilt from the branch, which is why going
27	cold is safe in the first place — the branch, not the directory, is the task's
28	identity.
29
30	If the task is owned by another machine, resuming here takes ownership. Two
31	machines writing the same branch is the one way to make this workflow produce
32	a conflict, so dev asks before doing it.`,
33			Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
34			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
35				ctx := ctxOf()
36				t, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
37				if err != nil {
38					return err
39				}
40
41				host := config.Hostname()
42				if !t.OwnedBy(host) && !force {
43					return fmt.Errorf("task %s is owned by %s.\n"+
44						"Make sure that machine has pushed its work, then re-run with --force to take ownership",
45						t.ID, t.Owner)
46				}
47
48				if fetch {
49					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "fetch", "--prune", "origin"); err != nil {
50						app.warnf("fetch failed: %v", err)
51					}
52				}
53
54				rt := app.Runtime()
55				mode := t.EffectiveMode()
56				checkout := checkoutOf(t)
57
58				switch mode {
59				case task.ModeWorktree:
60					_, statErr := os.Stat(checkout)
61					// Rebuild the worktree when it is gone — the cold-to-hot path.
62					if t.WorktreePath == "" || statErr != nil {
63						base := t.Base
64						// Prefer the published branch: a cold task's work lives on
65						// the remote, and a stale local ref could drop it.
66						if remote := "origin/" + t.Branch; gitx.RefExists(ctx, t.RepoPath, remote) {
67							base = remote
68						}
69						m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
70						res, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
71							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, RepoName: t.Repo, Branch: t.Branch,
72							Base: base, Label: t.Title(), NoProvision: noProvision,
73						})
74						if err != nil {
75							var exists *wt.ErrExists
76							if asError(err, &exists) {
77								t.WorktreePath = exists.Path
78							} else {
79								return err
80							}
81						} else {
82							t.WorktreePath, t.RuntimeHandle = res.Path, res.RuntimeHandle
83							reportProvision(app, res)
84							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebuilt    %s\n", config.Contract(res.Path))
85						}
86						checkout = t.WorktreePath
87					}
88
89				case task.ModeBranch:
90					checkout = t.RepoPath
91					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
92					if err != nil {
93						return err
94					}
95					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
96						if st.Dirty() {
97							return fmt.Errorf("cannot switch the canonical checkout from %s to %s: %s",
98								st.Branch, t.Branch, st.Breakdown())
99						}
100						if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "switch", t.Branch); err != nil {
101							return err
102						}
103					}
104
105				case task.ModeDirect:
106					checkout = t.RepoPath
107					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
108					if err != nil {
109						return err
110					}
111					if st.Branch != t.Branch {
112						return fmt.Errorf("direct task %s tracks %s, but the canonical checkout is on %s; "+
113							"switch back explicitly or start a worktree task", t.Title(), t.Branch, st.Branch)
114					}
115				}
116				if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
117					handle, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, checkout, t.Title())
118					if err != nil {
119						app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
120					}
121					if rt.Name() != "none" {
122						t.RuntimeHandle = handle
123					}
124				}
125
126				t.State = task.Hot
127				t.Owner = host
128				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				annotate(app, rt, t)
132
133				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s  %s on %s (%s)\n",
134					task.Hot.Icon(), t.Title(), t.Repo, t.Branch, mode)
135				if t.Next != "" {
136					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   next      %s\n", t.Next)
137				}
138				if t.AgentSession != "" {
139					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   agent     %s (resumable)\n", t.AgentSession)
140				}
141				if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout); err == nil {
142					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   git       %s\n", st.Summary())
143					if st.Behind > 0 {
144						app.warnf("branch is %d behind upstream — `git pull --ff-only` before you start", st.Behind)
145					}
146				}
147				if rt.Name() == "none" {
148					app.cdDirective(checkout)
149				}
150				return nil
151			},
152		}
153		f := cmd.Flags()
154		f.BoolVar(&noProvision, "no-provision", false, "skip dependency install when rebuilding a worktree")
155		f.BoolVar(&fetch, "fetch", true, "fetch from origin first")
156		f.BoolVar(&force, "force", false, "take ownership of a task owned by another machine")
157		return cmd
158	}
```

```text
44
```

```text
370				}
371				for _, e := range res.Failures {
372					app.warnf("%v", e)
373				}
374				return nil
375			},
376		}
377		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&dryRun, "dry-run", false, "show the plan instead of applying it")
378		return cmd
379	}
380
381	func newWtPlanCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
382		var (
383			repoRef string
384			write   bool
385		)
386		cmd := &cobra.Command{
387			Use:   "plan",
388			Short: "Show what a new worktree of this repo would be provisioned with",
389			Long: `Report the project types detected in this repository and exactly what
390	provisioning a new worktree would do — which gitignored files get copied,
391	which dependency directories are copied or shared, and which install commands
392	run.
393
394	A worktree that comes up broken is the commonest reason people abandon
395	worktrees, and the config alone cannot answer "what will this actually do":
396	that depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed here, and
397	which files are genuinely gitignored. This computes all of it and changes
398	nothing.
399
400	With --write, seed a .dev.toml from what was detected, so the repository can
401	commit its own setup and every machine gets the same one.`,
402			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
403			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
404				ctx := ctxOf()
405				repoPath, _, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
406				if err != nil {
407					return err
408				}
409				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, repoPath)
410				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, repoPath)
411
412				if write {
413					return writeRepoTemplate(app, repoPath, plan, set)
414				}
415				renderPlan(app, plan, repoPath)
416				return nil
417			},
418		}
419		f := cmd.Flags()
420		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
421		f.BoolVar(&write, "write", false, "seed a .dev.toml in the repository from what was detected")
422		return cmd
423	}
424
425	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
426	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
427		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
428
429		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
430			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
431		} else {
432			t := NewTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
433			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
434				deps := "—"
435				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
436					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
437				} else {
438					deps = "global cache"
439				}
440				tool := "installed"
441				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
442					tool = "MISSING: " + e.Tool
443				}
444				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
445			}
446			t.Render(app.Out)
447		}
448
449		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
450		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
451			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
452		} else {
453			st := NewTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
454			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
455				mark := "✓"
456				if s.Skipped {
457					mark = "·"
458				}
459				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
460			}
461			st.Render(app.Out)
462		}
463
464		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
465			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\nwarning: %s\n", w)
466		}
467		if plan.Empty() {
468			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
469				"worktree.post_create, or commit a .dev.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
470		}
471	}
472
473	// writeRepoTemplate seeds a .dev.toml from the detected plan.
474	//
475	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
476	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
477	// rediscover it.
478	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
479		path := filepath.Join(repoPath, wt.OverrideFilename)
480		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
481			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
482		}
483
484		var b strings.Builder
485		b.WriteString("# dev worktree setup for this repository.\n")
486		b.WriteString("#\n")
487		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
488		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
489		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
490		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
491
492		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
493		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
494		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
495		b.WriteString("include = [")
496		for i, inc := range set.Include {
497			if i > 0 {
498				b.WriteString(", ")
499			}
500			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
501		}
502		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
503
504		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
505			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
506			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
507				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
508			}
509			b.WriteString("#\n")
510			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
511			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
512			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
513
514			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
515			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
516			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
517			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
518			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
519			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
520			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
521				switch {
522				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
523					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
524						e.Name, e.Manager)
525				case e.CopySafe:
526					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
527				default:
528					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
529				}
530			}
531		} else {
532			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
533			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
534			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
535		}
536
537		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
538			return err
539		}
540		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
541		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
542		return nil
543	}
```

```text
10	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
11	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
12	type Repo struct {
13		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
14		Root string
15		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
16		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
17		GitCommonDir string
18		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
19		Name string
20		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
21		// the main checkout.
22		IsLinkedWorktree bool
23		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
24		MainRoot string
25		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
26		Bare bool
27	}
28
29	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
30	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
31
32	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
33	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
34		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
35		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
36		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
37			"rev-parse",
38			"--path-format=absolute",
39			"--show-toplevel",
40			"--git-common-dir",
41			"--is-bare-repository",
42		)
43		if err != nil {
44			return Repo{}, err
45		}
46		f := lines(out)
47		r := Repo{}
48		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
49		switch len(f) {
50		case 3:
51			r.Root = f[0]
52			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
53			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
54		case 2:
55			r.GitCommonDir = f[0]
56			r.Bare = f[1] == "true"
57		default:
58			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
59		}
60
61		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
62		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
63		if r.Bare {
64			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
65		} else {
66			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
67		}
68		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.Root != r.MainRoot
69		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
70		if r.Bare {
71			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
72			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
73			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
74				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
75			}
76		}
77		return r, nil
78	}
79
80	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
81	// a full Discover.
82	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
83		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
84		return err == nil
85	}
86
87	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
88	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
89	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
90	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
91	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
92		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
93			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
94				return b
95			}
96		}
97		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
98			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
99				return cand
100			}
101		}
102		return ""
103	}
104
105	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
106	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
107		if name == "" {
108			name = "origin"
109		}
110		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
111		if err != nil {
112			return ""
113		}
114		return out
115	}
116
117	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
118	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
119	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
120	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
121	// semantics should use Remote instead.
122	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
123		if commonDir == "" {
124			return ""
125		}
126		if name == "" {
127			name = "origin"
128		}
129		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
130		if err != nil {
131			return ""
132		}
133		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
134		section := ""
135		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
136			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
137			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
138				continue
139			}
140			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
141				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
142				continue
143			}
144			if section != want {
145				continue
146			}
147			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
148			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
149				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
150			}
151		}
152		return ""
153	}
```

```text
1	// Package wt creates, provisions and removes the linked worktrees dev owns.
2	//
3	// Ownership, stated once so agents and humans stop improvising: dev owns every
4	// worktree a person might come back to tomorrow — features, fixes, experiments,
5	// cross-machine handoffs — and places them at the configured path template.
6	// Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/` stays for turn-scoped subagent isolation
7	// that dies with the turn. dev never calls `herdr worktree create`, because
8	// the path policy has to hold on machines without herdr; it creates the
9	// worktree with git and asks herdr only to *open* it.
10	package wt
11
12	import (
13		"bufio"
14		"context"
15		"errors"
16		"fmt"
17		"io"
18		"os"
19		"os/exec"
20		"path/filepath"
21		"time"
22	)
23
24	// Provisioner brings a fresh checkout up to a working state.
25	//
26	// A worktree is a clean checkout: no node_modules, no .venv, and none of the
27	// gitignored env files the project needs. Without this step every new worktree
28	// starts broken, which is the commonest reason people give up on worktrees.
29	type Provisioner struct {
30		Settings Settings
31		Timeout  time.Duration
32		// Log receives progress lines; nil discards them.
33		Log io.Writer
34	}
35
36	// Result records what provisioning did, so callers can report it honestly.
37	type Result struct {
38		Copied  []string
39		Linked  []string
40		Ran     []string
41		Skipped []string
42		// Failures are non-fatal: a failed `npm ci` leaves a usable checkout the
43		// user can fix by hand, so it is reported rather than rolled back.
44		Failures []error
45	}
46
47	func (p *Provisioner) logf(format string, args ...any) {
48		if p.Log != nil {
49			fmt.Fprintf(p.Log, format+"\n", args...)
50		}
51	}
52
53	// Provision brings dst up to a working state, using src as the source of
54	// gitignored files and any copied dependency trees.
55	func (p *Provisioner) Provision(ctx context.Context, src, dst string) (Result, error) {
56		plan := BuildPlan(ctx, p.Settings, src)
57		return p.Apply(ctx, plan, src, dst)
58	}
59
60	// Apply executes a plan. Splitting this from BuildPlan is what lets
61	// `dev wt plan` show exactly what would happen without doing any of it.
62	func (p *Provisioner) Apply(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, src, dst string) (Result, error) {
63		var res Result
64		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
65			p.logf("warning: %s", w)
66		}
67
68		for _, step := range plan.Steps {
69			if step.Skipped {
70				res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" ("+step.Why+")")
71				continue
72			}
73			switch step.Kind {
74			case StepCopyFile:
75				if err := p.copyFileStep(src, dst, step.What); err != nil {
76					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
77					continue
78				}
79				res.Copied = append(res.Copied, step.What)
80				p.logf("copied %s", step.What)
81
82			case StepCopyDir:
83				from, to := filepath.Join(src, step.What), filepath.Join(dst, step.What)
84				if _, err := os.Lstat(to); err == nil {
85					res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" (already present)")
86					continue
87				}
88				p.logf("copying %s …", step.What)
89				if err := copyTree(from, to); err != nil {
90					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", step.What, err))
91					continue
92				}
93				res.Copied = append(res.Copied, step.What+"/")
94				p.logf("copied %s", step.What)
95
96			case StepLinkDir:
97				if err := p.linkStep(src, dst, step.What); err != nil {
98					if errors.Is(err, errAlreadyPresent) {
99						res.Skipped = append(res.Skipped, step.What+" (already present)")
100						continue
101					}
102					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
103					continue
104				}
105				res.Linked = append(res.Linked, step.What)
106				p.logf("linked %s", step.What)
107
108			case StepRun:
109				p.logf("running: %s", step.What)
110				if err := p.runShell(ctx, dst, step.What); err != nil {
111					res.Failures = append(res.Failures, err)
112					continue
113				}
114				res.Ran = append(res.Ran, step.What)
115			}
116		}
117		return res, nil
118	}
119
120	var errAlreadyPresent = errors.New("already present")
121
122	func (p *Provisioner) copyFileStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
123		from, to := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)
124		info, err := os.Lstat(from)
125		if err != nil {
126			return nil // vanished between planning and applying; nothing to do
127		}
128		if _, err := os.Stat(to); err == nil {
129			return nil // never clobber what the checkout already has
130		}
131		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(to), 0o755); err != nil {
132			return err
133		}
134		if err := copyFile(from, to, info.Mode()); err != nil {
135			return fmt.Errorf("copy %s: %w", rel, err)
136		}
137		return nil
138	}
139
140	func (p *Provisioner) linkStep(src, dst, rel string) error {
141		target, link := filepath.Join(src, rel), filepath.Join(dst, rel)
142		if _, err := os.Stat(target); err != nil {
143			return fmt.Errorf("link %s: not present in the source checkout", rel)
144		}
145		if _, err := os.Lstat(link); err == nil {
146			return errAlreadyPresent
147		}
148		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(link), 0o755); err != nil {
149			return err
150		}
151		if err := os.Symlink(target, link); err != nil {
152			return fmt.Errorf("link %s: %w", rel, err)
153		}
154		return nil
155	}
156
157	func (p *Provisioner) runShell(ctx context.Context, dir, command string) error {
158		timeout := p.Timeout
159		if timeout <= 0 {
160			timeout = 10 * time.Minute
161		}
162		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
163		defer cancel()
164
165		shell := os.Getenv("SHELL")
166		if shell == "" {
167			shell = "/bin/sh"
168		}
169		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, shell, "-c", command)
170		cmd.Dir = dir
171		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = p.Log, p.Log
172		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
173			if ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded {
174				return fmt.Errorf("post_create %q timed out after %s", command, timeout)
175			}
176			return fmt.Errorf("post_create %q: %w", command, err)
177		}
178		return nil
179	}
180
181	func copyFile(from, to string, mode os.FileMode) error {
182		in, err := os.Open(from)
183		if err != nil {
184			return err
185		}
186		defer in.Close()
187		out, err := os.OpenFile(to, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, mode.Perm())
188		if err != nil {
189			return err
190		}
191		defer out.Close()
192		w := bufio.NewWriter(out)
193		if _, err := io.Copy(w, in); err != nil {
194			return err
195		}
196		return w.Flush()
197	}
198
199	// copyTree duplicates a directory.
200	//
201	// Symlinks are recreated rather than followed: a pnpm node_modules is a farm
202	// of links into a global store, and dereferencing them would turn a 200MB
203	// copy into several gigabytes of duplicated packages.
204	func copyTree(from, to string) error {
205		return filepath.Walk(from, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
206			if err != nil {
207				return err
208			}
209			rel, err := filepath.Rel(from, path)
210			if err != nil {
211				return err
212			}
213			target := filepath.Join(to, rel)
214
215			switch {
216			case info.IsDir():
217				return os.MkdirAll(target, info.Mode().Perm())
218			case info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0:
219				dest, err := os.Readlink(path)
220				if err != nil {
221					return err
222				}
223				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
224					return err
225				}
226				os.Remove(target)
227				return os.Symlink(dest, target)
228			case info.Mode().IsRegular():
229				if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0o755); err != nil {
230					return err
231				}
232				return copyFile(path, target, info.Mode())
233			}
234			return nil // sockets, devices and the like have no place in a checkout
235		})
236	}
```

```text
256	// Load reads config.toml over the defaults. A missing file is not an error —
257	// dev must be useful with zero setup. A malformed file is, because silently
258	// falling back to defaults would send worktrees to the wrong volume.
259	func Load(path string) (Config, error) {
260		cfg := Default()
261		if path == "" {
262			path = ConfigFile()
263		}
264		md, err := toml.DecodeFile(path, &cfg)
265		switch {
266		case errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist):
267			return cfg, nil
268		case err != nil:
269			return cfg, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", path, err)
270		}
271		if undecoded := md.Undecoded(); len(undecoded) > 0 {
272			// Unknown keys are usually typos ("worktree_dir" vs "worktree_root").
273			// Warn rather than fail so a newer config still works on an older dev.
274			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: unknown key(s) in %s: %v\n", path, undecoded)
275		}
276		cfg.Source = path
277		return cfg, cfg.Validate()
278	}
279
280	// Validate catches the settings that would otherwise fail deep inside a
281	// worktree create, when a directory has already been made.
282	func (c Config) Validate() error {
283		switch c.Runtime.Backend {
284		case "", "auto", "herdr", "tmux", "none":
285		default:
286			return fmt.Errorf("runtime.backend %q: want auto, herdr, tmux or none", c.Runtime.Backend)
287		}
288		if c.Paths.WorktreePath == "" {
289			return errors.New("paths.worktree_path must not be empty")
290		}
291		if _, err := Render(c.Paths.WorktreePath, c.probeVars()); err != nil {
292			return fmt.Errorf("paths.worktree_path: %w", err)
293		}
294		switch c.Bootstrap.Layout {
295		case "", "flat", "preserve":
296		default:
297			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.layout %q: want flat or preserve", c.Bootstrap.Layout)
298		}
299		if c.Bootstrap.MaxDepth < 0 {
300			return fmt.Errorf("bootstrap.max_depth must be zero (unlimited) or positive")
301		}
302		if c.Forge.RemoteLimit < 0 {
303			return fmt.Errorf("forge.remote_limit must be zero (use default) or positive")
304		}
305		validStrategy := func(v string) bool {
306			switch v {
307			case "", "reinstall", "copy", "link", "skip":
308				return true
309			}
310			return false
311		}
312		if !validStrategy(c.Worktree.Strategy) {
313			return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategy %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip", c.Worktree.Strategy)
314		}
315		for ecosystem, strategy := range c.Worktree.Strategies {
316			if !validStrategy(strategy) {
317				return fmt.Errorf("worktree.strategies.%s %q: want reinstall, copy, link or skip",
318					ecosystem, strategy)
319			}
320		}
321		validColumns := map[string]bool{
322			"repo": true, "branch": true, "git": true, "live": true,
323			"latest": true, "worktrees": true, "tasks": true,
324			"category": true, "path": true,
325		}
326		for i, column := range c.TUI.Repos.Columns {
327			if !validColumns[column] {
328				return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.columns[%d] %q: unknown column", i, column)
329			}
330		}
331		switch c.EffectiveRepoSort() {
332		case "activity", "latest", "name", "git", "tasks":
333		default:
334			return fmt.Errorf("tui.repos.sort %q: want activity, latest, name, git or tasks", c.TUI.Repos.Sort)
335		}
336		seen := map[string]string{}
337		for i, t := range c.TUI.Tools {
338			switch {
339			case t.Key == "":
340				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key is required", i)
341			case t.Run == "":
342				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d] (%s): run is required", i, t.Key)
343			}
344			if binding, ok := ReservedKey(t.Key); ok {
345				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is the dashboard's %q binding; pick another",
346					i, t.Key, binding)
347			}
348			if prev, ok := seen[t.Key]; ok {
349				return fmt.Errorf("tui.tools[%d]: key %q is already bound to %q", i, t.Key, prev)
350			}
351			seen[t.Key] = t.Name
352		}
353		return nil
354	}
```

```text
162	// findTry locates an existing try whose name contains the slug, preferring the
163	// most recent when several match.
164	func findTry(root, slug string) string {
165		entries, err := os.ReadDir(root)
166		if err != nil {
167			return ""
168		}
169		var best string
170		var bestTime time.Time
171		for _, e := range entries {
172			if !e.IsDir() || !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(e.Name()), strings.ToLower(slug)) {
173				continue
174			}
175			info, err := e.Info()
176			if err != nil {
177				continue
178			}
179			if info.ModTime().After(bestTime) {
180				best, bestTime = filepath.Join(root, e.Name()), info.ModTime()
181			}
182		}
183		return best
184	}
185
186	func openOrCD(app *App, ctx context.Context, dir, label string) error {
187		rt := app.Runtime()
188		if rt.Name() == "none" {
189			app.cdDirective(dir)
190			return nil
191		}
192		if _, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, dir, label); err != nil {
193			app.warnf("could not open a session: %v", err)
194		}
195		return nil
196	}
```

```text
1	// Package cli assembles dev's command tree. Commands stay thin: they parse
2	// flags, call into the domain packages, and render. All policy lives in
3	// config, gitx, wt, task and runtime so it can be tested without a terminal.
4	package cli

6	import (
7		"context"

13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
15	)
16
17	// App is the state shared by every command.
18	type App struct {
19		Cfg   config.Config
20		Tasks *task.Store
21
22		Out io.Writer
23		Err io.Writer
24
25		// configPath is the --config override; empty means the XDG default.
26		configPath string
27		// runtimeOverride is the --runtime flag; empty means use the config.
28		runtimeOverride string
29		// noRuntime disables all multiplexer interaction for one invocation.
30		noRuntime bool
31	}
32
33	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
34	func (a *App) Load() error {
35		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
36		if err != nil {
37			return err
38		}
39		a.Cfg = cfg
40		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
41		if a.Out == nil {
42			a.Out = os.Stdout
43		}
44		if a.Err == nil {
45			a.Err = os.Stderr
46		}
47		return nil
48	}
49
50	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring
51	// --runtime and --no-runtime.
52	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
53		if a.noRuntime {
54			return runtime.None{}
55		}
56		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
57		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
58			backend = a.runtimeOverride
59		}
60		rt := runtime.Select(backend)
61		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
62			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
63		}
64		return rt
65	}
66
67	// printf writes to the command's stdout.
68	func (a *App) printf(format string, args ...any) {
69		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, format, args...)
70	}
71
72	// warnf writes a non-fatal notice to stderr, so it never pollutes piped output.
73	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
74		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: "+format+"\n", args...)
75	}
76
77	// cdDirective emits the marker the shell wrapper installed by
78	// `dev shell-init` looks for. A child process cannot change its parent's
79	// working directory, so the only way `dev resume` can leave the user *in* the
80	// checkout is to ask the shell to do it.
81	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) {
82		fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
```

```text
14	// StepKind is what a provisioning step does.
15	type StepKind string
16
17	const (
18		// StepCopyFile copies one gitignored file into the new checkout.
19		StepCopyFile StepKind = "copy"
20		// StepCopyDir duplicates a dependency directory.
21		StepCopyDir StepKind = "copy-dir"
22		// StepLinkDir symlinks a directory so both checkouts share it.
23		StepLinkDir StepKind = "link"
24		// StepRun executes a shell command in the new checkout.
25		StepRun StepKind = "run"
26	)
27
28	// Step is one action in a provisioning plan.
29	type Step struct {
30		Kind StepKind
31		// What is the path or command the step acts on.
32		What string
33		// Why explains the step in one line, for `dev wt plan`.
34		Why string
35		// Ecosystem names the language this step belongs to, empty for the
36		// file-copying steps that belong to no ecosystem.
37		Ecosystem string
38		// Skipped marks a step that will not run, with Why holding the reason.
39		Skipped bool
40	}

42	// Plan is everything provisioning would do to a new worktree of a repository,
43	// computed without touching anything.
44	//
45	// Making this inspectable matters more than it looks: a worktree that comes up
46	// broken is the single most common reason people stop using worktrees at all,
47	// and "what will this actually do" is not answerable from the config alone —
48	// it depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed, and which
49	// files are genuinely gitignored.
50	type Plan struct {
51		RepoPath   string
52		Ecosystems []Ecosystem
53		Steps      []Step
54		// Warnings are problems that will not stop provisioning but will surprise
55		// someone: an unsound strategy that was downgraded, a missing tool.
56		Warnings []string
57	}
58
59	// Runnable returns the steps that will actually execute.
60	func (p Plan) Runnable() []Step {
61		var out []Step
62		for _, s := range p.Steps {
63			if !s.Skipped {
64				out = append(out, s)
65			}
66		}
67		return out
68	}
69
70	// Empty reports a plan that would do nothing at all.
71	func (p Plan) Empty() bool { return len(p.Runnable()) == 0 }
72
73	// Settings are the provisioning inputs, resolved from global config and any
74	// per-repo .dev.toml.
75	type Settings struct {
76		Include    []string
77		Link       []string
78		Cmds       config.PostCreate
79		Strategy   Strategy
80		Strategies map[string]string
81	}
82
83	// SettingsFor resolves the effective provisioning settings for a repository.
84	func SettingsFor(cfg config.Config, repoPath string) Settings {
85		s := Settings{
86			Include:    cfg.Worktree.Include,
87			Link:       cfg.Worktree.Link,
88			Cmds:       cfg.Worktree.PostCreate,
89			Strategy:   Reinstall,
90			Strategies: map[string]string{},
91		}
92		if v, ok := ParseStrategy(cfg.Worktree.Strategy); ok {
93			s.Strategy = v
94		}
95		for k, v := range cfg.Worktree.Strategies {
96			s.Strategies[k] = v
97		}
98		if o, ok := LoadRepoOverride(repoPath); ok {
99			if len(o.Worktree.Include) > 0 {
100				s.Include = o.Worktree.Include
101			}
102			if len(o.Worktree.Link) > 0 {
103				s.Link = o.Worktree.Link
104			}
105			if o.Worktree.PostCreate != nil {
106				s.Cmds = *o.Worktree.PostCreate
107			}
108			if o.Worktree.Strategy != "" {
109				// Keep an invalid value so strategyFor can report it in the plan
110				// instead of silently turning a repo-local typo into reinstall.
111				s.Strategy = Strategy(o.Worktree.Strategy)
112			}
113			for k, v := range o.Worktree.Strategies {
114				s.Strategies[k] = v
115			}
116		}
117		return s
118	}
119
120	// strategyFor resolves the strategy for one ecosystem, narrowing to something
121	// sound and recording why when it has to.
122	func (s Settings) strategyFor(e Ecosystem) (Strategy, string) {
123		want := s.Strategy
124		if _, ok := ParseStrategy(string(want)); !ok {
125			return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q is not a strategy (want %s), using reinstall",
126				e.Name, want, joinStrategies())
127		}
128		if v, ok := s.Strategies[e.Name]; ok {
129			if parsed, ok := ParseStrategy(v); ok {
130				want = parsed
131			} else {
132				return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q is not a strategy (want %s), using reinstall",
133					e.Name, v, joinStrategies())
134			}
135		}
136		// An ecosystem with no dependency directory has nothing to copy or share,
137		// so those strategies collapse to reinstalling — which for a global cache
138		// is nearly free anyway.
139		if len(e.DepDirs) == 0 && (want == Copy || want == Link) {
140			return Reinstall, ""
141		}
142		if ok, hazard := e.SupportsStrategy(want); !ok {
143			return Reinstall, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s is unsound here — %s; using reinstall instead",
144				e.Name, want, hazard)
145		}
146		return want, ""
147	}
148
149	func joinStrategies() string {
150		parts := make([]string, len(Strategies))
151		for i, s := range Strategies {
152			parts[i] = string(s)
153		}
154		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
155	}
156
157	// BuildPlan computes what provisioning a new worktree of repoPath would do.
158	// It reads the filesystem and asks git which files are ignored, but changes
159	// nothing.
160	func BuildPlan(ctx context.Context, set Settings, repoPath string) Plan {
161		p := Plan{RepoPath: repoPath, Ecosystems: DetectEcosystems(repoPath)}
162
163		// Gitignored files to carry over.
164		if files, err := ignoredMatching(ctx, repoPath, set.Include); err != nil {
165			p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings, "could not list ignored files: "+err.Error())
166		} else {
167			for _, rel := range files {
168				info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(repoPath, rel))
169				if err != nil {
170					continue
171				}
172				if info.IsDir() {
173					continue // directories belong to `link`, not `include`
174				}
175				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{
176					Kind: StepCopyFile, What: rel,
177					Why: "gitignored, so the checkout would not have it",
178				})
179			}
180		}
181
182		// Explicit symlinks, which are always the user's own decision.
183		for _, rel := range set.Link {
184			step := Step{Kind: StepLinkDir, What: rel, Why: "configured in worktree.link"}
185			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoPath, rel)); err != nil {
186				step.Skipped, step.Why = true, "not present in the source checkout"
187			}
188			p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
189		}
190
191		// Dependencies, per ecosystem.
192		//
193		// The strategy and post_create are separate axes. A strategy says how a
194		// dependency directory arrives; post_create says what commands run. So an
195		// explicit command list replaces the *derived install commands* but still
196		// leaves copy and link in effect — a project that bootstraps with `make
197		// setup` may still want its node_modules copied rather than rebuilt.
198		explicit := !set.Cmds.Auto
199		for _, e := range p.Ecosystems {
200			strategy, warn := set.strategyFor(e)
201			if warn != "" {
202				p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings, warn)
203			}
204
205			switch strategy {
206			case Copy, Link:
207				kind, verb := StepCopyDir, "copied"
208				if strategy == Link {
209					kind, verb = StepLinkDir, "shared"
210				}
211				for _, dir := range e.DepDirs {
212					step := Step{
213						Kind: kind, What: dir, Ecosystem: e.Name,
214						Why: fmt.Sprintf("%s dependencies, %s instead of reinstalling", e.Manager, verb),
215					}
216					if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(repoPath, dir)); err != nil {
217						step.Skipped = true
218						step.Why = "not present in the source checkout — nothing to " + string(strategy)
219					}
220					p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
221				}
222
223			case Skip:
224				if explicit {
225					continue
226				}
227				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{
228					Kind: StepRun, What: e.Install, Ecosystem: e.Name,
229					Why: "strategy is skip", Skipped: true,
230				})
231
232			default: // Reinstall
233				if explicit {
234					continue // the configured command list replaces this
235				}
236				step := Step{
237					Kind: StepRun, What: e.Install, Ecosystem: e.Name,
238					Why: e.Marker + " detected",
239				}
240				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
241					step.Skipped = true
242					step.Why = e.Tool + " is not installed on this machine"
243					p.Warnings = append(p.Warnings,
244						fmt.Sprintf("%s needs %s, which is not installed — worktrees will come up without its dependencies",
245							e.Name, e.Tool))
246				}
247				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, step)
248			}
249		}
250
251		// An explicit command list, when configured.
252		if explicit {
253			for _, c := range set.Cmds.Commands {
254				p.Steps = append(p.Steps, Step{Kind: StepRun, What: c, Why: "configured in worktree.post_create"})
255			}
256		}
257		return p
258	}
259
260	// ignoredMatching asks git which of the patterns name real, ignored files.
261	//
262	// Using git rather than matching by hand means .gitignore semantics —
263	// negations, directory rules, nested ignore files — are exactly right, and
264	// that a *tracked* file matching a pattern is never returned. A tracked file
265	// is already in the new checkout on the correct branch; copying the source
266	// branch's version over it would be wrong.
267	func ignoredMatching(ctx context.Context, src string, patterns []string) ([]string, error) {
268		if len(patterns) == 0 {
269			return nil, nil
270		}
271		args := []string{"ls-files", "--others", "--ignored", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--"}
272		args = append(args, patterns...)
273		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, src, args...)
274		if err != nil {
275			return nil, err
276		}
277		var rels []string
278		for _, f := range strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(out, "\x00"), "\x00") {
279			if f != "" {
280				rels = append(rels, f)
281			}
282		}
283		return rels, nil
284	}
```

```text
13	// Version is set at build time via -ldflags.

16	const rootLong = `dev is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent runtimes.
17
18	It exists to keep three things separate that otherwise collapse into one:
19
20	  git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
21	  git worktree    a disposable local checkout
22	  herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
23	  dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
24
25	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. dev persists only
26	what git cannot answer — a task's state, its owner and its next action — so
27	closing a runtime session never means losing the thread.`
28
29	// NewRootCommand builds the whole command tree writing to the process streams.
30	func NewRootCommand() *cobra.Command {
31		return NewRootCommandWithIO(os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
32	}
33
34	// NewRootCommandWithIO builds the command tree writing to the given streams.
35	// Commands write through App rather than through cobra, so this is the seam
36	// tests use to capture output without redirecting the process's file
37	// descriptors.
38	func NewRootCommandWithIO(out, errOut io.Writer) *cobra.Command {
39		app := &App{Out: out, Err: errOut}
40
41		root := &cobra.Command{
42			Use:           "dev",
43			Short:         "Manage repos, worktrees and work-in-progress across agent runtimes",
44			Long:          rootLong,
45			Version:       Version,
46			SilenceUsage:  true,
47			SilenceErrors: true,
48			// Bare `dev` shows the inventory, which is the question the tool
49			// exists to answer.
50			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
51				if printSkill, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("skill"); printSkill {
52					out, err := skill.Render()
53					if err != nil {
54						return err
55					}
56					fmt.Fprint(app.Out, out)
57					return nil
58				}
59				// A terminal gets the dashboard; a pipe gets the listing, so
60				// `dev | grep` and `dev > file` behave as expected.
61				if interactive() {
62					return runTUI(app)
63				}
64				return runList(app, listOptions{})
65			},
66			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
67				return app.Load()
68			},
69		}
70
71		pf := root.PersistentFlags()
72		pf.StringVar(&app.configPath, "config", "", "path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)")
73		pf.StringVar(&app.runtimeOverride, "runtime", "", "override runtime backend: herdr, tmux or none")
74		pf.BoolVar(&app.noRuntime, "no-runtime", false, "do not touch any terminal multiplexer")
75
76		// Mirrors `herdr --skill`: the binary is the authority for its own agent
77		// skill, so a dotfiles installer can sync it without vendoring a copy.
78		root.Flags().Bool("skill", false, "print the bundled agent skill and exit")
79
80		root.AddCommand(
81			newListCmd(app),
82			newTUICmd(app),
83			newStatusCmd(app),
84			newStartCmd(app),
85			newParkCmd(app),
86			newResumeCmd(app),
87			newDoneCmd(app),
88			newSweepCmd(app),
89			newAdoptCmd(app),

91			newWorktreeCmd(app),
92			newRepoCmd(app),
93			newGitignoreCmd(app),
94			newTryCmd(app),
95			newGraduateCmd(app),
96			newStatsCmd(app),
97			newHelpTopicCmd(app),
98			newSkillCmd(app),
99			newDoctorCmd(app),
100			newShellInitCmd(app),
101			newConfigCmd(app),
102			newCacheCmd(app),
103			newEditCmd(app),
104		)
105		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
106		root.SetOut(out)
107		root.SetErr(errOut)
108		return root
109	}
110
111	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes.
112	func Execute() int {
113		root := NewRootCommand()
114		if err := root.Execute(); err != nil {
115			msg := err.Error()
116			// cobra already printed usage errors in a readable form.
117			if !strings.HasPrefix(msg, "unknown command") {
118				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "dev: "+msg)
119			}
120			return 1
121		}
122		return 0
123	}
```

```text
103			case !r.CheckoutExists:
```

```text
20	// Row is one task enriched with everything derived live.
21	type Row struct {
22		Task *task.Task
23
24		// Checkout is where the task's code currently lives: its worktree if it

26		Checkout string
```
