28		// cold task, or one whose worktree was removed behind dev's back, is not.
29		CheckoutExists bool
30		// WorktreeMissing flags a task that records a worktree path which is no
31		// longer a registered git worktree — the drift `dev sweep` reports.
32		WorktreeMissing bool
33
34		// Status is the live git status of Checkout. Zero when there is nothing
35		// on disk to inspect.
36		Status    gitx.Status
37		StatusErr error
38
39		// LastCommit is the author time of HEAD, used to age a task.
40		LastCommit time.Time
41
42		// Session is the live runtime session hosting this checkout, if any.
43		Session *runtime.Session
44		// sessionsTracked reports whether the runtime can observe sessions at all.
45		// With the "none" backend it cannot, so "hot but nothing live" is not
46		// drift — it is the only state that backend can ever produce.
47		sessionsTracked bool
48	}

50	// Live reports whether a runtime session is currently hosting this task.
51	func (r Row) Live() bool { return r.Session != nil }
52
53	// StateDrift reports a task whose recorded state disagrees with reality:
54	// hot with no live session, or warm/cold with one. It is what `dev sweep`
55	// turns into suggestions — dev reports drift and never silently rewrites it.
56	func (r Row) StateDrift() string {
57		if r.sessionsTracked {
58			switch r.Task.State {
59			case task.Hot:
60				if !r.Live() {
61					return "no live session"
62				}
63			case task.Warm, task.Cold:
64				if r.Live() {
65					return "session is live"
66				}
67			}
68		}
69		if r.Task.State == task.Cold && r.CheckoutExists && r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
70			return "worktree still on disk"
71		}
72		if r.WorktreeMissing {
73			return "worktree is gone"
74		}
75		return ""
76	}
77
78	// Age is how long since the task's last commit, falling back to when the entry
79	// was last written for a task with no commits of its own.
80	func (r Row) Age() time.Duration {
81		ref := r.LastCommit
82		if ref.IsZero() || r.Task.Updated.After(ref) {
83			ref = r.Task.Updated
84		}
85		if ref.IsZero() {
86			return 0
87		}
88		return time.Since(ref)
89	}

91	// Options tunes what a Collect call spends time on.
92	type Options struct {
93		// SkipRuntime avoids querying the multiplexer, for callers that only need
94		// git facts (and for tests).
95		SkipRuntime bool
96		// SkipGit avoids running git per task, for a fast listing.
97		SkipGit bool
98	}

100	// Collect builds the enriched inventory. Git probes run concurrently: each is
101	// a handful of process spawns, and a machine with dozens of tasks would
102	// otherwise make `dev ls` feel slow.
103	func Collect(ctx context.Context, tasks []*task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opts Options) []Row {
104		rows := make([]Row, len(tasks))
105
106		var sessions []runtime.Session
107		tracked := false
108		if !opts.SkipRuntime && rt != nil && rt.Name() != "none" {
109			if s, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
110				sessions, tracked = s, true
111			}
112		}
113
114		var wg sync.WaitGroup
115		// Bound concurrency: git is process-heavy and an unbounded fan-out over a
116		// large inventory would thrash.
117		sem := make(chan struct{}, 8)
118
119		for i, t := range tasks {
120			rows[i].Task = t
121			rows[i].Checkout = checkoutOf(t)
122
123			if opts.SkipGit || rows[i].Checkout == "" {
124				continue
125			}
126			wg.Add(1)
127			go func(i int) {
128				defer wg.Done()
129				sem <- struct{}{}
130				defer func() { <-sem }()
131				enrich(ctx, &rows[i])
132			}(i)
133		}
134		wg.Wait()
135
136		for i := range rows {
137			rows[i].Session = matchSession(sessions, rows[i])
138			rows[i].sessionsTracked = tracked
139		}
140		return rows
141	}

143	func checkoutOf(t *task.Task) string {
144		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
145			return t.WorktreePath
146		}
147		return t.RepoPath
148	}

150	func enrich(ctx context.Context, r *Row) {
151		info, err := os.Stat(r.Checkout)
152		r.CheckoutExists = err == nil && info.IsDir()
153		if !r.CheckoutExists {
154			if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
155				r.WorktreeMissing = true
156			}
157			return
158		}
159		if st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Checkout); err != nil {
160			r.StatusErr = err
161		} else {
162			r.Status = st
163		}
164		if unix, _, err := gitx.LastCommit(ctx, r.Checkout); err == nil && unix > 0 {
165			r.LastCommit = time.Unix(unix, 0)
166		}
167		// A recorded worktree that git no longer knows about is drift worth
168		// surfacing: the directory may exist while the administrative entry is gone.
169		if r.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
170			if _, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Task.RepoPath, r.Task.Branch); err == nil && !ok {
171				r.WorktreeMissing = true
172			}
173		}
174	}

176	// matchSession picks the runtime session hosting a row's checkout. An exact
177	// directory match is preferred over a containing one, so a worktree's own
178	// session always wins over the parent repo's.
179	func matchSession(sessions []runtime.Session, r Row) *runtime.Session {
180		if r.Checkout == "" {
181			return nil
182		}
183		var contains *runtime.Session
184		for i := range sessions {
185			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
186				if d == r.Checkout {
187					return &sessions[i]
188				}
189				if strings.HasPrefix(d, r.Checkout+"/") && contains == nil {
190					contains = &sessions[i]
191				}
192			}
193		}
194		return contains
195	}

209		out := rows[:0:0]

219			}
220			if f.DirtyOnly && !r.Status.Dirty() {
221				continue
222			}
223			out = append(out, r)
224		}

226	}

74						return err
75					}
76					switch {
77					case wip && st.Dirty():
78						msg := "wip: checkpoint"
79						if t.Next != "" {
80							msg = "wip: checkpoint — " + t.Next
81						}
82						made, err := gitx.WipCommit(ctx, checkout, msg)
83						if err != nil {
84							return err
85						}
86						if made {
87							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   committed  %s\n", msg)
88						}
89					case st.Dirty() && cold:
90						return fmt.Errorf("%s has uncommitted changes; going cold removes the worktree.\n"+
91							"Commit them, or re-run with --wip to checkpoint automatically",
92							config.Contract(checkout))
93					case st.Dirty():
94						app.warnf("%s has uncommitted changes (kept in place; --wip checkpoints them)",
95							config.Contract(checkout))
96					}
97
98					if push {
99						if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
100							return err
101						}
102					}
103					if cold {
104						st, err = gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
105						if err != nil {
106							return err
107						}
108						if !st.Published() || st.Ahead > 0 {
109							return fmt.Errorf("%s is not fully pushed (%s); a cold task must be reconstructible "+
110								"from the remote.\nRun `dev park --cold --push`", t.Branch, st.Summary())
111						}
112					}
113				}
114
115				rt := app.Runtime()
116				if !keepRT && t.RuntimeHandle != "" {
117					if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
118						app.warnf("could not close the runtime session: %v", err)
119					} else {
120						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   closed     %s session %s\n", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle)
121					}
122					t.RuntimeHandle = ""
123				}
124
125				if cold && t.WorktreePath != "" {
126					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
127					if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
128						RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath,
129					}); err != nil {
130						return err
131					}
132					// The path is cleared, but the branch stays: that is what makes
133					// the task reconstructible rather than lost.
134					t.WorktreePath = ""
135				}
136				if cold && mode == task.ModeBranch {
137					// Free the canonical checkout for other work. The branch remains
138					// local + remote and resume switches back to it.
139					base := t.Base
140					if base == "" {
141						base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, t.RepoPath)
142					}
143					if base == "" {
144						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but its base branch is unknown")
145					}
146					if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
147						return fmt.Errorf("task is pushed, but could not switch canonical checkout back to %s: %w",
148							base, err)
149					}
150				}
151
152				t.State = target
153				t.Owner = config.Hostname()
154				if err := app.Tasks.Save(t); err != nil {
155					return err
156				}
157				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s %s is %s", target.Icon(), t.Title(), target.Label())
158				if t.Next != "" {
159					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, " — next: %s", t.Next)
160				}
161				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
162				return nil
163			},
164		}
165		f := cmd.Flags()
166		f.StringVarP(&next, "next", "n", "", "what to do when you come back")
167		f.StringVar(&note, "note", "", "free-form note")
168		f.BoolVar(&wip, "wip", false, "checkpoint uncommitted work as a wip: commit")
169		f.BoolVar(&push, "push", false, "push the branch so another machine can pick it up")
170		f.BoolVar(&cold, "cold", false, "go cold: remove the worktree after confirming everything is pushed")
171		f.BoolVar(&keepRT, "keep-session", false, "leave the runtime session open")
172		return cmd
173	}
174
175	// pushBranch publishes a branch, setting upstream on first push.
176	func pushBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, dir, branch string) error {
177		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, dir, "push", "--set-upstream", "origin", branch); err != nil {
178			return fmt.Errorf("push %s: %w", branch, err)
179		}
180		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   pushed     origin/%s\n", branch)
181		return nil
182	}
183
184	// resolveTask picks the task an argument names, or infers it from the current
185	// directory when no argument is given.
186	func resolveTask(app *App, args []string) (*task.Task, error) {
187		if len(args) == 1 {
188			return app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
189		}
190		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
191		if err != nil {
192			return nil, err
193		}
194		t, err := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd)
195		if err != nil {
196			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no task for %s — name one explicitly, or run this inside a task's checkout",
197				config.Contract(cwd))
198		}
199		return t, nil
200	}

28
29	Two integration modes, matching the two shapes a branch's history takes:

31	  --ff    rebase onto the base and fast-forward it. Use when the branch's
32	          commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
33	  --pr    push and open a pull/merge request with gh or glab, leaving the
34	          merge to review and CI. Use when someone (or something) should look

36
37	With neither, dev only reports what it would do.

39	Cleanup is deliberately conservative: the worktree is removed, the task entry
40	is marked done, and the branch is deleted only with --delete-branch. A merged
41	branch that still has unpushed commits is never deleted.`,

69					}

74					}

172	func directPushHint(push bool) string {
173		if push {
174			return " --push"

179	// fastForward rebases the task branch onto its base and then moves the base
180	// forward, producing a linear history with no merge commit.
181	//
182	// merge --ff-only is the guardrail: if the rebase did not actually put the
183	// branch ahead of the base, the merge fails loudly instead of quietly creating
184	// a merge commit the user did not ask for.
185	func fastForward(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
186		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   rebasing   %s onto %s\n", t.Branch, base)
187		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rebase", base); err != nil {
188			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nThe rebase left conflicts to resolve in %s.\n"+
189				"Fix them, `git rebase --continue`, then re-run dev done --ff",
190				err, config.Contract(checkout))
191		}
192		// The base branch lives in the main checkout, not the worktree.
193		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   merging    %s into %s (fast-forward only)\n", t.Branch, base)
194		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "switch", base); err != nil {
195			return err
196		}
197		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, t.RepoPath, "merge", "--ff-only", t.Branch); err != nil {
198			return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\n%s could not be fast-forwarded. Something else moved it; "+
199				"rebase again or integrate by hand", err, base)
200		}
201		return nil
202	}
203
204	// deleteMergedBranch removes a branch only when git agrees its commits are already
205	// contained in the base — the check that makes cleanup safe.
206	func deleteMergedBranch(ctx context.Context, app *App, repoPath, branch, base string) error {
207		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", branch, base); err != nil {
208			return fmt.Errorf("keeping branch %s: it has commits not in %s", branch, base)
209		}
210		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "branch", "-d", branch); err != nil {
211			return fmt.Errorf("could not delete %s: %w", branch, err)
212		}
213		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   deleted    branch %s\n", branch)
214		return nil
215	}
216
217	// openPR pushes the branch and asks the forge CLI to open a pull/merge
218	// request. When no forge CLI is available dev prints the push result and the
219	// URL to open by hand, rather than failing: the branch being published is the
220	// part that actually matters.
221	func openPR(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout, base string) error {
222		if err := pushBranch(ctx, app, checkout, t.Branch); err != nil {
223			return err
224		}
225		kind := forge.Detect(ctx, t.RepoPath)
226		f, err := forge.For(kind)
227		if err != nil || !f.Available() {
228			app.warnf("no forge CLI for this remote — the branch is pushed; open the request in your browser")
229			return nil
230		}
231		url, err := f.CreatePR(ctx, checkout, forge.PRRequest{
232			Base: base, Head: t.Branch, Fill: true,
233		})
234		if err != nil {
235			return err
236		}
237		if url != "" {
238			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   opened     %s\n", url)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

package cli

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
)

func guardSharedCheckout(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, checkout string) error {
	if app.allowSharedCheckout {
		return nil
	}
	activities, err := checkoutAgentActivities(ctx, rt, checkout, os.Getenv("HERDR_PANE_ID"))
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("check live agents before opening %s: %w", config.Contract(checkout), err)
	}
	if len(activities) == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	var occupied []string
	for _, activity := range activities {
		label := activity.Agent
		if activity.Name != "" {
			label = activity.Name
		}
		if label == "" {
			label = "agent"
		}
		state := activity.Status
		if state == "" {
			state = "unknown"
		}
		occupied = append(occupied, fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s, pane %s)", label, state, activity.PaneID))
	}
	return fmt.Errorf("%s is already occupied by %s; use a separate worktree, or pass --allow-shared-checkout only after coordinating disjoint file ownership",
		config.Contract(checkout), strings.Join(occupied, ", "))
}

// checkoutAgentActivities returns recognized agents whose reported cwd resolves
// to the same canonical Git worktree root as checkout. A pane is excluded only
// when its exact ID matches excludePane; lifecycle state never makes it free.
func checkoutAgentActivities(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, checkout, excludePane string) ([]runtime.AgentActivity, error) {
	lister, ok := rt.(runtime.AgentActivityLister)
	if !ok {
		return nil, nil
	}
	target, ok := canonicalWorktreeRoot(ctx, checkout)
	if !ok {
		return nil, nil
	}
	activities, err := lister.AgentActivities(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	out := make([]runtime.AgentActivity, 0, len(activities))
	for _, activity := range activities {
		if excludePane != "" && activity.PaneID == excludePane {
			continue
		}
		root, ok := canonicalWorktreeRoot(ctx, activity.CWD)
		if ok && root == target {
			out = append(out, activity)
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

func canonicalWorktreeRoot(ctx context.Context, dir string) (string, bool) {
	if dir == "" {
		return "", false
	}
	repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, dir)
	if err != nil || repo.Root == "" {
		return "", false
	}
	root := filepath.Clean(repo.Root)
	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(root); err == nil {
		root = filepath.Clean(resolved)
	}
	return root, true
}

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

type herdrCall struct {
	args []string
	out  string
	err  error
}

func scriptedHerdr(t *testing.T, calls ...herdrCall) *Herdr {
	t.Helper()
	index := 0
	h := NewHerdr()
	h.runCommand = func(_ context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
		t.Helper()
		if index >= len(calls) {
			t.Fatalf("unexpected herdr call: %v", args)
		}
		call := calls[index]
		index++
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(args, call.args) {
			t.Fatalf("herdr call %d = %v, want %v", index, args, call.args)
		}
		return []byte(call.out), call.err
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if index != len(calls) {
			t.Errorf("used %d herdr calls, want %d", index, len(calls))
		}
	})
	return h
}

func TestHerdrOpenReturnsExactCreatedRootPane(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t,
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "list"}, out: `{"id":"1","result":{"workspaces":[]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"pane", "list"}, out: `{"id":"2","result":{"panes":[]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", "/repo", "--no-focus", "--label", "child"}, out: `{"id":"3","result":{"workspace":{"workspace_id":"w7"},"tab":{"tab_id":"w7:t1"},"root_pane":{"pane_id":"w7:p12"}}}`},
	)

	got, err := h.Open(context.Background(), "/repo", "child")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := OpenResult{Handle: "w7", Surface: "workspace", Opened: true, Created: true, RootPaneID: "w7:p12"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("Open = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestHerdrOpenReuseHasNoLaunchablePane(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t,
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "list"}, out: `{"id":"1","result":{"workspaces":[{"workspace_id":"w4"}]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"pane", "list"}, out: `{"id":"2","result":{"panes":[{"pane_id":"w4:p9","workspace_id":"w4","cwd":"/repo"}]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "focus", "w4"}, out: `{"id":"3","result":{}}`},
	)

	got, err := h.Open(context.Background(), "/repo", "ignored")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.Handle != "w4" || got.Surface != "workspace" || !got.Opened || got.Created || got.RootPaneID != "" {
		t.Fatalf("reused Open = %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestHerdrOpenWorktreeReturnsExactRootPane(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t, herdrCall{
		args: []string{"worktree", "open", "--path", "/wt/repo", "--no-focus", "--label", "child"},
		out:  `{"id":"1","result":{"workspace":{"workspace_id":"w7"},"worktree":{"open_workspace_id":"w7"},"root_pane":{"pane_id":"w7:p12"}}}`,
	})

	got, err := h.OpenWorktree(context.Background(), "/wt/repo", "child")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := OpenResult{Handle: "w7", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true, Created: true, RootPaneID: "w7:p12"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("OpenWorktree = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestHerdrOpenWorktreeReuseHasNoLaunchablePane(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t, herdrCall{
		args: []string{"worktree", "open", "--path", "/wt/repo", "--no-focus"},
		out:  `{"id":"1","result":{"worktree":{"open_workspace_id":"w8"}}}`,
	})
	got, err := h.OpenWorktree(context.Background(), "/wt/repo", "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.Handle != "w8" || got.Surface != "worktree" || !got.Opened || got.Created || got.RootPaneID != "" {
		t.Fatalf("reused worktree = %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestHerdrWorktreeFallbackNeverAdvertisesPane(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t,
		herdrCall{args: []string{"worktree", "open", "--path", "/wt/repo", "--no-focus", "--label", "child"}, err: errors.New("unsupported")},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "list"}, out: `{"id":"2","result":{"workspaces":[]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"pane", "list"}, out: `{"id":"3","result":{"panes":[]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", "/wt/repo", "--no-focus", "--label", "child"}, out: `{"id":"4","result":{"workspace":{"workspace_id":"w9"},"root_pane":{"pane_id":"w9:p1"}}}`},
	)
	got, err := h.OpenWorktree(context.Background(), "/wt/repo", "child")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.Handle != "w9" || got.Surface != "workspace" || !got.Created || got.RootPaneID != "" {
		t.Fatalf("fallback = %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestHerdrMissingRootPaneFailsClosed(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t,
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "list"}, out: `{"id":"1","result":{"workspaces":[]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"pane", "list"}, out: `{"id":"2","result":{"panes":[]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", "/repo", "--no-focus"}, out: `{"id":"3","result":{"workspace":{"workspace_id":"w7"}}}`},
	)
	got, err := h.Open(context.Background(), "/repo", "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !got.Opened || got.Created || got.RootPaneID != "" {
		t.Fatalf("missing root pane must not be launchable: %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestHerdrRejectsMissingHandleAndMalformedOutput(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		out  string
	}{
		{name: "missing handle", out: `{"id":"3","result":{"root_pane":{"pane_id":"w7:p1"}}}`},
		{name: "malformed", out: `not json`},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := scriptedHerdr(t,
				herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "list"}, out: `{"id":"1","result":{"workspaces":[]}}`},
				herdrCall{args: []string{"pane", "list"}, out: `{"id":"2","result":{"panes":[]}}`},
				herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", "/repo", "--no-focus"}, out: tc.out},
			)
			if _, err := h.Open(context.Background(), "/repo", ""); err == nil {
				t.Fatal("malformed successful response must fail")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestHerdrAgentActivitiesUseForegroundCWDAndAllStates(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t, herdrCall{
		args: []string{"agent", "list"},
		out: `{"id":"1","result":{"agents":[` +
			`{"agent":"claude","name":"reviewer","agent_status":"done","cwd":"/old","foreground_cwd":"/repo","pane_id":"w1:p2","workspace_id":"w1"},` +
			`{"agent":"codex","agent_status":"unknown","cwd":"/repo2","pane_id":"w2:p1","workspace_id":"w2"}` +
			`]}}`,
	})
	got, err := h.AgentActivities(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(got) != 2 || got[0].CWD != "/repo" || got[0].Status != "done" || got[1].Status != "unknown" {
		t.Fatalf("AgentActivities = %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestHerdrEnvelopeErrorIsReported(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t, herdrCall{
		args: []string{"agent", "list"},
		out:  `{"id":"1","error":{"code":"unavailable","message":"server stopped"}}`,
	})
	_, err := h.AgentActivities(context.Background())
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "server stopped (unavailable)") {
		t.Fatalf("AgentActivities error = %v", err)
	}
}

package cli

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx/gittest"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
)

type activityRuntime struct {
	activities []runtime.AgentActivity
	activityErr error
	activityCalls int
	openResult runtime.OpenResult
	openCalls int
	annotations []map[string]string
}

func (r *activityRuntime) Name() string    { return "herdr" }
func (r *activityRuntime) Available() bool { return true }
func (r *activityRuntime) Open(context.Context, string, string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
	r.openCalls++
	return r.openResult, nil
}
func (r *activityRuntime) OpenWorktree(context.Context, string, string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
	r.openCalls++
	return r.openResult, nil
}
func (r *activityRuntime) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }
func (r *activityRuntime) List(context.Context) ([]runtime.Session, error) { return nil, nil }
func (r *activityRuntime) Annotate(_ context.Context, _ string, kv map[string]string) error {
	copy := make(map[string]string, len(kv))
	for k, v := range kv {
		copy[k] = v
	}
	r.annotations = append(r.annotations, copy)
	return nil
}
func (r *activityRuntime) AgentActivities(context.Context) ([]runtime.AgentActivity, error) {
	r.activityCalls++
	return r.activities, r.activityErr
}

func TestCheckoutAgentActivitiesUsesCanonicalWorktreeRoots(t *testing.T) {
	r := gittest.New(t)
	linked := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "linked")
	r.Git("branch", "feat/other")
	r.Git("worktree", "add", linked, "feat/other")
	other := gittest.New(t)

	rt := &activityRuntime{activities: []runtime.AgentActivity{
		{PaneID: "w1:p1", Agent: "claude", Status: "working", CWD: r.Root},
		{PaneID: "w1:p2", Agent: "claude", Status: "idle", CWD: r.Root},
		{PaneID: "w1:p3", Agent: "codex", Status: "done", CWD: filepath.Join(r.Root, "nested")},
		{PaneID: "w1:p4", Agent: "claude", Status: "unknown", CWD: linked},
		{PaneID: "w2:p1", Agent: "claude", Status: "blocked", CWD: other.Root},
	}}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(r.Root, "nested"), 0o755); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	got, err := checkoutAgentActivities(context.Background(), rt, r.Root, "w1:p1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(got) != 2 || got[0].PaneID != "w1:p2" || got[1].PaneID != "w1:p3" {
		t.Fatalf("activities = %+v; want idle and done agents in the same worktree only", got)
	}
}

func TestGuardSharedCheckoutFailsClosedAndOverrideBypasses(t *testing.T) {
	r := gittest.New(t)
	rt := &activityRuntime{activities: []runtime.AgentActivity{{
		PaneID: "w1:p2", Agent: "claude", Name: "reviewer", Status: "unknown", CWD: r.Root,
	}}}
	app := &App{}
	if err := guardSharedCheckout(context.Background(), app, rt, r.Root); err == nil ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "reviewer (unknown, pane w1:p2)") {
		t.Fatalf("collision error = %v", err)
	}

	app.allowSharedCheckout = true
	calls := rt.activityCalls
	if err := guardSharedCheckout(context.Background(), app, rt, r.Root); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("explicit override should allow the checkout: %v", err)
	}
	if rt.activityCalls != calls {
		t.Fatal("override should not query agent activity")
	}

	app.allowSharedCheckout = false
	rt.activities = nil
	rt.activityErr = errors.New("agent inventory unavailable")
	if err := guardSharedCheckout(context.Background(), app, rt, r.Root); err == nil ||
		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "agent inventory unavailable") {
		t.Fatalf("activity lookup must fail closed: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestStatusShowsEveryRecognizedAgentState(t *testing.T) {
	r := gittest.New(t)
	rt := &activityRuntime{activities: []runtime.AgentActivity{
		{PaneID: "w1:p1", WorkspaceID: "w1", Agent: "claude", Name: "author", Status: "working", CWD: r.Root},
		{PaneID: "w1:p2", WorkspaceID: "w1", Agent: "codex", Status: "done", CWD: r.Root},
	}}
	var out, errOut bytes.Buffer
	app := &App{
		Cfg: config.Default(), Tasks: task.NewStore(t.TempDir()),
		Out: &out, Err: &errOut, runtimeInstance: rt,
	}
	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Chdir(r.Root); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.Chdir(cwd) })

	cmd := newStatusCmd(app)
	cmd.SetArgs(nil)
	if err := cmd.Execute(); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got := out.String()
	for _, want := range []string{
		"activity   author:working w1:p1 (w1)",
		"activity   codex:done w1:p2 (w1)",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("status missing %q:\n%s", want, got)
		}
	}
}

package cli

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx/gittest"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
)

type startFixture struct {
	t      *testing.T
	repo   *gittest.Repo
	app    *App
	stdout bytes.Buffer
	stderr bytes.Buffer
}

func newStartFixture(t *testing.T, rt runtime.Runtime) *startFixture {
	t.Helper()
	r := gittest.New(t)
	cfg := config.Default()
	cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot = filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "Worktrees")
	cfg.Paths.WorktreePath = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}"
	cfg.Worktree.Include = nil
	cfg.Worktree.PostCreate = config.PostCreate{}
	f := &startFixture{t: t, repo: r}
	f.app = &App{
		Cfg: cfg, Tasks: task.NewStore(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "tasks")),
		Out: &f.stdout, Err: &f.stderr, runtimeInstance: rt,
	}
	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Chdir(r.Root); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.Chdir(cwd) })
	return f
}

func (f *startFixture) run(args ...string) error {
	f.t.Helper()
	cmd := newStartCmd(f.app)
	cmd.SetArgs(args)
	return cmd.Execute()
}

func decodeSingleStartJSON(t *testing.T, raw string) startJSON {
	t.Helper()
	dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(raw))
	var got startJSON
	if err := dec.Decode(&got); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("start output is not JSON: %v\n%s", err, raw)
	}
	var extra any
	if err := dec.Decode(&extra); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Fatalf("start output contains more than one JSON value: %v\n%s", err, raw)
	}
	return got
}

func TestStartJSONReturnsExactHerdrWorktreeTargetAndOrigin(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID", "w-parent")
	t.Setenv("HERDR_PANE_ID", "w-parent:p3")
	rt := &activityRuntime{openResult: runtime.OpenResult{
		Handle: "w-child", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true,
		Created: true, RootPaneID: "w-child:p9",
	}}
	f := newStartFixture(t, rt)

	if err := f.run("--task", "child task", "--branch", "feat/child", "--base", "main",
		"--runtime-label", "child-task ← parent", "--json"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	got := decodeSingleStartJSON(t, f.stdout.String())
	if got.TaskID != "repo__feat-child" || got.Repo != "repo" || got.Branch != "feat/child" || got.Base != "main" || got.Mode != "worktree" {
		t.Fatalf("identity fields = %+v", got)
	}
	if !filepath.IsAbs(got.RepoPath) || !filepath.IsAbs(got.WorktreePath) || !filepath.IsAbs(got.Checkout) || got.Checkout != got.WorktreePath {
		t.Fatalf("paths must be absolute and checkout must be the worktree: %+v", got)
	}
	wantRuntime := startRuntimeJSON{
		Name: "herdr", Handle: "w-child", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true,
		Created: true, RootPaneID: "w-child:p9",
	}
	if got.Runtime != wantRuntime {
		t.Fatalf("runtime = %+v, want %+v", got.Runtime, wantRuntime)
	}
	if got.RuntimeLabel != "child-task ← parent" || got.Origin.WorkspaceID != "w-parent" || got.Origin.PaneID != "w-parent:p3" {
		t.Fatalf("label/origin = %q %+v", got.RuntimeLabel, got.Origin)
	}
	if len(rt.openLabels) != 1 || rt.openLabels[0] != "child-task ← parent" {
		t.Fatalf("runtime labels = %v", rt.openLabels)
	}
	if !containsAnnotation(rt.annotations, map[string]string{
		"origin_workspace": "w-parent", "origin_pane": "w-parent:p3",
	}) {
		t.Fatalf("origin metadata was not attached to the target: %v", rt.annotations)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(f.stderr.String(), "worktree feat/child") {
		t.Fatalf("diagnostics should remain on stderr: %q", f.stderr.String())
	}
	taskBody, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(f.app.Tasks.Dir, got.TaskID+".toml"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if strings.Contains(string(taskBody), "w-parent") || strings.Contains(string(taskBody), "child-task ← parent") {
		t.Fatalf("origin and runtime label must remain transient:\n%s", taskBody)
	}
}

func TestStartJSONNeverAdvertisesUnlaunchablePane(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		rt   runtime.Runtime
	}{
		{name: "none", rt: runtime.None{}},
		{name: "tmux", rt: &activityRuntime{name: "tmux", openResult: runtime.OpenResult{
			Handle: "tmux-task", Surface: "session", Opened: true, Created: true, RootPaneID: "not-a-herdr-pane",
		}}},
		{name: "herdr reuse", rt: &activityRuntime{openResult: runtime.OpenResult{
			Handle: "w7", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true, RootPaneID: "stale-pane",
		}}},
		{name: "herdr fallback", rt: &activityRuntime{openResult: runtime.OpenResult{
			Handle: "w8", Surface: "workspace", Opened: true, Created: true, RootPaneID: "fallback-pane",
		}}},
		{name: "runtime failure", rt: &activityRuntime{openErr: errors.New("open failed")}},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newStartFixture(t, tc.rt)
			if err := f.run("--task", tc.name, "--base", "main", "--json"); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			got := decodeSingleStartJSON(t, f.stdout.String())
			if got.Runtime.RootPaneID != "" {
				t.Fatalf("unlaunchable runtime advertised pane %q: %+v", got.Runtime.RootPaneID, got.Runtime)
			}
			if tc.name == "none" && strings.Contains(f.stdout.String(), "\ncd ") {
				t.Fatalf("JSON stdout contains a shell directive: %q", f.stdout.String())
			}
			if tc.name == "runtime failure" && (!strings.Contains(f.stderr.String(), "open failed") || got.Runtime.Opened) {
				t.Fatalf("runtime failure not represented honestly: stderr=%q runtime=%+v", f.stderr.String(), got.Runtime)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestStartJSONSaveFailureEmitsNoSuccessObject(t *testing.T) {
	rt := &activityRuntime{openResult: runtime.OpenResult{Handle: "w7", Surface: "workspace", Opened: true, Created: true}}
	f := newStartFixture(t, rt)
	blocked := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "not-a-directory")
	if err := os.WriteFile(blocked, []byte("x"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f.app.Tasks = task.NewStore(filepath.Join(blocked, "tasks"))

	if err := f.run("--task", "save failure", "--direct", "--json"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected task save failure")
	}
	if f.stdout.Len() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("failed start emitted success stdout: %q", f.stdout.String())
	}
	if rt.openCalls != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("runtime side effect should have happened before save failure, calls=%d", rt.openCalls)
	}
}

func TestStartHumanOutputAndDefaultLabelRemainCompatible(t *testing.T) {
	f := newStartFixture(t, runtime.None{})
	if err := f.run("--task", "quick fix", "--direct"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	out := f.stdout.String()
	if !strings.Contains(out, "quick fix  repo on main (direct)") || !strings.Contains(out, "\ncd ") {
		t.Fatalf("human output changed unexpectedly: %q", out)
	}
}

func TestStartCollisionGuardsCanonicalCheckoutBeforeBranchSwitch(t *testing.T) {
	for _, args := range [][]string{
		{"--task", "direct", "--direct"},
		{"--task", "branch", "--branch-only", "--branch", "feat/branch", "--base", "main"},
	} {
		t.Run(args[1], func(t *testing.T) {
			rt := &activityRuntime{}
			f := newStartFixture(t, rt)
			rt.activities = []runtime.AgentActivity{{
				PaneID: "w1:p2", Agent: "claude", Status: "idle", CWD: f.repo.Root,
			}}
			if err := f.run(args...); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "already occupied") {
				t.Fatalf("collision should block start: %v", err)
			}
			if rt.openCalls != 0 {
				t.Fatal("runtime must not open after a collision")
			}
			if branch := f.repo.Git("branch", "--show-current"); branch != "main" {
				t.Fatalf("collision switched branch to %s", branch)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestStartCollisionExcludesOnlyCallerPaneAndHonorsExplicitOverride(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("HERDR_PANE_ID", "w1:p1")
	rt := &activityRuntime{activities: []runtime.AgentActivity{
		{PaneID: "w1:p1", Agent: "claude", Status: "working"},
	}}
	f := newStartFixture(t, rt)
	rt.activities[0].CWD = f.repo.Root
	if err := f.run("--task", "same pane", "--direct"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("caller pane should be excluded: %v", err)
	}

	rt2 := &activityRuntime{}
	f2 := newStartFixture(t, rt2)
	rt2.activities = []runtime.AgentActivity{{PaneID: "w1:p2", Agent: "claude", Status: "done", CWD: f2.repo.Root}}
	f2.app.allowSharedCheckout = true
	if err := f2.run("--task", "coordinated", "--direct"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("explicit override should proceed: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestStartOriginSkipsMissingAndSelfOrigins(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name      string
		workspace string
		pane      string
		target    string
	}{
		{name: "missing", workspace: "", pane: "", target: "w2"},
		{name: "self", workspace: "w2", pane: "w2:p1", target: "w2"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Setenv("HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID", tc.workspace)
			t.Setenv("HERDR_PANE_ID", tc.pane)
			rt := &activityRuntime{}
			app := &App{Out: io.Discard, Err: io.Discard}
			got := annotateStartOrigin(app, rt, runtime.OpenResult{Handle: tc.target, Opened: true, Created: true})
			if got != (startOriginJSON{}) || len(rt.annotations) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("origin should be skipped: got=%+v annotations=%v", got, rt.annotations)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestAllowSharedCheckoutIsOnePersistentOverride(t *testing.T) {
	root := NewRootCommandWithIO(io.Discard, io.Discard)
	flag := root.PersistentFlags().Lookup("allow-shared-checkout")
	if flag == nil || flag.DefValue != "false" {
		t.Fatalf("persistent override flag = %+v", flag)
	}
	if root.Flags().Lookup("allow-shared-checkout") != flag {
		t.Fatal("allow-shared-checkout should be defined once at the root")
	}
}

func containsAnnotation(have []map[string]string, want map[string]string) bool {
	for _, annotation := range have {
		match := len(annotation) == len(want)
		for key, value := range want {
			if annotation[key] != value {
				match = false
			}
		}
		if match {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"reflect"

func TestTmuxOpenReportsCreationAndReuseWithoutPane(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		hasErr  error
		created bool
		calls   [][]string
	}{
		{name: "reuse", calls: [][]string{{"has-session", "-t", "=child-task"}}},
		{name: "create", hasErr: errors.New("missing"), created: true, calls: [][]string{
			{"has-session", "-t", "=child-task"},
			{"new-session", "-d", "-s", "child-task", "-c", "/repo"},
		}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var calls [][]string
			tm := NewTmux()
			tm.runCommand = func(_ context.Context, args ...string) (string, error) {
				calls = append(calls, append([]string(nil), args...))
				if len(calls) == 1 {
					return "", tc.hasErr
				}
				return "", nil
			}
			got, err := tm.Open(context.Background(), "/repo", "child task")
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got.Handle != "child-task" || got.Surface != "session" || !got.Opened || got.Created != tc.created || got.RootPaneID != "" {
				t.Fatalf("Open = %+v", got)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(calls, tc.calls) {
				t.Fatalf("calls = %v, want %v", calls, tc.calls)
			}
		})
	}
}

1	# Parallel agents
2
3	How to run several coding agents without them stepping on each other.
4
5	## The one rule
6
7	> **Worktree per change stream. Pane per agent.**
8
9	Not one worktree per agent. Isolation should follow the *git mutation
10	boundary*, not the identity of who is typing.
11
12	```
13	one independent change stream
14	        → one worktree
15	        → one workspace
16	        → N tabs / panes
17	        → N agents
18	```
19
20	## When agents can share a checkout
21
22	They can, and often should, when **file ownership is clear**:
23
24	| Parallel work | Same checkout? |
25	|---|---|
26	| One researching, one coding | yes |
27	| Frontend and backend | yes |
28	| Tests and implementation | usually |
29	| `src/foo/*` and `src/bar/*` | yes |
30	| Both editing `package.json` | risky |
31	| Both changing one API surface | risky |
32	| Both running a formatter or codegen | risky |
33	| Both doing large refactors | no |
34	| Either running `checkout` / `reset` / `rebase` | no |
35
36	The question is never "how many agents?" It is **"can these two mutate the same
37	state?"**
38
39	## When they need worktrees
40
41	- Mutually exclusive *approaches* to one problem, to be compared and one kept.
42	- Unknown file ranges.
43	- Any agent that will run git operations changing HEAD.
44
45	```bash
46	dev wt create exp/jwt      --base main
47	dev wt create exp/session  --base main
48	dev wt create exp/oauth    --base main
49	```
50
51	Then compare, keep one, remove the rest. These branches are execution
52	artifacts, not architecture — they are meant to disappear.
53
54	## Two layers, two owners
55
56	```
57	outer isolation   dev      change streams a human will return to
58	inner isolation   Claude   turn-scoped subagent worktrees, auto-cleaned
59	```
60
61	Do not nest one inside the other. A `dev` worktree containing a Claude worktree
62	raises questions with no good answers: which branch am I committing to, who
63	cleans up, does closing the session delete the branch.
64
65	Inside a `dev` worktree, just run the agent — no `--worktree` flag needed. The
66	directory is already the isolation.
67
68	## Bringing environment into a worktree
69
70	Every worktree is a clean checkout: no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
71	`dev` provisions on create. If an agent reports a project that will not run in
72	a fresh worktree, that is usually the cause:
73
74	```bash
75	dev wt provision      # re-run it
76	```
77
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Worktrees
2
3	A worktree is a second working directory for the same repository: its own
4	files, its own checked-out branch, sharing one history and one remote.
5
6	## What they are actually for
7
8	**Preventing two writers from editing the same files at once.** Not feature
9	management — that is what branches are for.
10
11	So the question is never "how many agents am I running?" It is:
12
13	> Could these two writers touch the same file?
14
15	- Different files, one goal → one checkout is fine. Several agents, several
16	  panes, one branch.
17	- Different *approaches* to the same problem → one worktree each, so they can
18	  be compared and the loser discarded.
19	- Anything where the file ranges are unknown → worktrees.
20
21	## Who owns which worktree
22
23	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
24	|---|---|---|---|
25	| Feature, fix, experiment, handoff | `dev` | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until done or swept |
26	| Turn-scoped agent isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | dies with the turn |
27
28	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this turn → Claude Code.**
29
30	Never put a long-lived worktree inside the repository. Every file watcher,
31	language server, indexer and `rg` run in the outer repo then sees a second copy
32	of the whole tree.
33
34	## Commands
35
36	```bash
37	dev wt create feat/auth --base main   # create at the configured path
38	dev wt list                           # every worktree of this repo
39	dev wt open feat/auth                 # open an existing one
40	dev wt rm feat/auth                   # remove the checkout; branch survives
41	dev wt provision                      # re-run setup on an existing checkout
42	```
43
44	## Always pass a base
45
46	```bash
47	dev wt create fix/orderbook --base main
48	```
49
50	Without `--base`, a new branch starts from the **current HEAD**. Create a
51	worktree while standing on `feature/A` and `fix/orderbook` quietly inherits
52	`feature/A`'s commits. This is the single most common way to end up with a
53	history nobody intended.
54
55	## A worktree starts empty of everything untracked
56
57	No `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`. `dev` fixes this on create:
58
59	- copies the gitignored files listed in `worktree.include`;
60	- symlinks anything in `worktree.link` (opt-in);
61	- runs `post_create`, detected from lockfiles when set to `"auto"`.
62
63	Only files that are **both listed and gitignored** are copied. A tracked file
64	is already in the checkout on the correct branch — copying the other branch's
65	version over it would be wrong.
66
67	## Removing one
68
69	```bash
70	dev wt rm feat/auth
71	```
72
73	Never deletes the branch. A dirty checkout needs an explicit `--force`, and
74	that refusal is the feature, not an obstacle.
75
76	If the directory was deleted behind git's back, `git worktree prune` clears the
77	stale entry — `dev wt rm` and `dev sweep` do this for you.
78
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	name: dev-cli
3	description: 'Manage repositories and work-in-progress with the dev CLI: bootstrap existing machines, organise repos without destructive moves, own worktree lifecycle and provisioning, track HOT/WARM/COLD tasks, navigate via TUI, and bridge gh/glab/herdr/tmux. Use when starting, parking or resuming work; scanning or organising repos; choosing a worktree mechanism; fixing worktree setup; or cleaning stale branches, checkouts and sessions.'
4	---
5
6	# dev-cli
7
8	The `dev` command is a thin glue layer over git, worktrees, forges and agent
9	runtimes. It exists to stop four different things collapsing into one:
10
11	```
12	git remote      durable code state, the source of truth
13	git worktree    a disposable local checkout
14	herdr / tmux    a per-host live runtime
15	dev             human intent: what am I working on, and what is next
16	```
17
18	Everything derivable from git or the runtime is derived live. `dev` persists
19	only what git cannot answer — a task's **state**, **owner** and **next
20	action** — in one TOML file per task under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`.
21
22	**The problem it solves:** when a terminal multiplexer's sidebar is the only
23	record of what you are working on, nothing can ever be closed. `dev` gives that
24	record a home outside the runtime, so closing a session stops meaning
25	abandoning a task.
26
27	## Check it is there first
28
29	`dev` is not installed everywhere. Before using it:
30
31	```bash
32	command -v dev || echo "not installed"
33	dev doctor          # what works on this machine, and what degrades
34	```
35
36	Only **git** is required. `herdr`, `tmux`, `gh` and `glab` each enable more and
37	degrade cleanly when absent — never make a step hard-depend on one.
38
39	## Worktree ownership — read this before creating any worktree
40
41	There are three mechanisms that create git worktrees, and picking the wrong one
42	is the most common source of confusion. The rule:
43
44	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
45	|---|---|---|---|
46	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff — anything you might return to | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path`, default `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>` | until `dev done` or `dev sweep` |
47	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation (`isolation: worktree`, `/batch`, `EnterWorktree`) | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (keep gitignored) | dies with the turn |
48	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
49
50	**Rule of thumb: might a human come back to it tomorrow → `dev`. Does it die
51	with this agent turn → Claude Code native.**
52
53	Why `dev` does not delegate to `herdr worktree create`: the path policy has to
54	hold on machines where herdr is not installed. `dev` creates the checkout with
55	plain git and asks herdr only to *open* it — which still makes it appear in the
56	sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
57
58	Never nest a `dev` worktree inside a repository. A checkout inside another
59	checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second copy of
60	the tree. `dev` refuses to do it.
61
62	Full detail: `references/worktree-ownership.md`.
63
64	## The task lifecycle
65
66	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
67	|---|---|---|---|
68	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
69	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
70	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
71	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
72
73	```bash
74	dev repo open api                                  # ad hoc; no task/worktree
75	dev start api --task "typo" --direct                # track current/main directly
76	dev start api --task "small" --branch-only --base main
77	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # isolated worktree → hot
78	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
79	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
80	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
81	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
82	```
83
84	**Parking is the move that matters.** `dev park --next "…"` is what makes it
85	safe to close a session, and the `--next` text is what makes resuming cheap.
86	Always suggest a `--next` when parking.
87
88	Full detail: `references/task-lifecycle.md`.
89
90	## Pick the task's checkout mode
91
92	A task does not imply a worktree. Use the lightest explicit boundary:
93
94	- `dev repo open <repo>` / REPOS Enter — ad-hoc open, no task at all.
95	- `dev start … --direct` / REPOS `d` — track current branch (usually main),
96	  create no branch/worktree. HOT ↔ WARM only; `dev done` needs no merge mode.
97	- `dev start … --branch-only` — create and switch a branch in the canonical
98	  checkout. No concurrent branch there.
99	- `dev start …` / REPOS `s` — default isolated branch + worktree. Use once work
100	  may be interrupted, experimental, or parallel.
101
102	Do not create isolation before it has a job, but do not carry dirty main changes
103	into a parallel task implicitly either: a worktree starts from committed HEAD.
104	Checkpoint first when the new task depends on that work.
105
106	## Everyday commands
107
108	```bash
109	dev                        # interactive dashboard (plain listing when piped)
110	dev edit                   # open the effective config; generate it first if absent
111	dev ls                     # what am I working on, everywhere
112	dev ls --json              # stable machine-readable form (also over ssh)
113	dev status                 # what is this directory: repo, branch, task, session
114	dev sweep                  # what has gone stale or drifted, and what to do
115	dev sweep --apply          # act on it, confirming each change
116
117	dev wt create feat/auth --base main    # worktree at the configured path
118	dev wt list                            # every worktree of this repo
119	dev wt plan                            # what a new worktree would be set up with
120	dev wt plan --write                    # seed a committed .dev.toml from it
121	dev wt rm feat/auth                    # remove the checkout; the branch stays
122
123	dev repo list              # every repo under the scan roots
124	dev repo clone owner/name  # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
125	dev repo sync --all        # fetch + prune, and report what moved
126	dev repo remote [query]     # search authenticated gh + glab repositories
127	dev bootstrap ~/code       # recursively inventory an existing machine
128	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects   # plan a non-destructive symlink catalog
129	dev gitignore              # .gitignore from GitHub templates + the common bits
130	dev adopt                  # import existing worktrees/sessions/branches as tasks
131
132	dev try redis-streams      # dated scratch directory for an experiment
133	dev graduate redis-streams --category Infra   # promote it into a real project
134
135	dev stats --heatmap        # where the time actually went
136	dev stats backfill --repo api  # seed one repo; TUI H then b does this in place
137	dev stats path             # durable XDG data, not cache
138	dev cache list             # regenerable forge/gitignore caches
139	dev help worktrees         # quick-reference pages
140	```
141
142	Complete generated reference: `references/commands.md`.
143
144	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
145
146	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
147	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
148	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
149
150	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
151	`paths.scan_roots` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
152
153	```bash
154	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
155	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
156	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
157	```
158
159	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
160	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
161
162	## Dashboard and forge inventory
163
164	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS and REMOTE views, switched with tab or vim-style h/l.
165	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` lazily, uses a short-lived private
166	cache, and `/` filters provider, owner/name and description. Enter opens a local
167	clone; `c` confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote
168	[query] --json` for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query.
169
170	REPOS has explicit LIVE and LATEST columns: latest is the newest dirty-file
171	mtime, commit, or task update. Detail shows the Herdr/tmux handle and agent
172	status. `[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R`
173	reverses it.
174
175	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
176	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
177	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
178	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
179	regenerable forge/gitignore data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
180
181	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
182	explicitly. Runtime
183	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
184
185	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
186	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
187	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
188	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
189	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
190	the binding should be portable across machines.
191
192	## Editing configuration
193
194	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
195	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
196	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
197
198	## Rules for agents
199
200	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
201	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
202	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
203
204	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
205	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
206	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
207	   history unattended.
208
209	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
210	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
211	   user before overriding it.
212
213	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
214	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
215	   for them.
216
217	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
218	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
219	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
220
221	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
222	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
223	   pushed.
224
225	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
226	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
227	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
228	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
229	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
230	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
231	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
232
233	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
234	   panes isolate *agents*. Several agents working on disjoint files of one
235	   feature belong in one checkout.
236
237	9. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
238	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
239	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
240	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
241
242	10. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
243	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
244	   their judgement, not yours.
245
246	11. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
247	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
248	   `dev cache clear` only for remote/gitignore caches.
249
250	12. **Read Git state as counts, not a dirty boolean.** `⇡`/`⇣` are upstream
251	   divergence; `=` conflicts, `+` staged, `!` unstaged, `?` untracked. Use
252	   `dev status` or JSON for the unique-path and type breakdown before cleanup.
253
254	13. **Commit messages stay English** and follow Conventional Commits, even when
255	   the conversation is in another language — see the companion `git-workflow`
256	   skill, which owns commit conventions, SemVer and branch naming. This skill
257	   does not duplicate them.
258
259	## When to use this skill
260
261	- "What am I working on?" / "我在做什麼" / too many terminal workspaces open.
262	- Starting, parking or resuming a piece of work.
263	- "Where should this worktree go?" / "should I use `claude --worktree` or herdr?"
264	- A new worktree is missing `node_modules`, `.venv` or `.env`.
265	- Cleaning up stale branches, worktrees and sessions.
266	- Cloning, creating or auditing repositories across a machine.
267	- Promoting an experiment into a real project.
268	- "Which repo do I spend my time in?"
269	- Setting up a `.gitignore`, or a harness worktree showing as untracked.
270	- Adopting a machine that already has repos, worktrees and sessions.
271	- Recursively scanning, indexing, or physically reorganising existing repos.
272	- Configuring a flat repo/worktree layout or generating config for one.
273
274	## When NOT to use it
275
276	- **Commit messages, SemVer, branch naming, PR-vs-main tiering** — that is the
277	  `git-workflow` skill. This one links to it rather than restating it.
278	- **Driving herdr panes and agents directly** — that is the `herdr` skill.
279	- A single `git add` + `git commit` needs no tooling at all.
280
281	## Reference files
282
283	- `references/bootstrap.md` — read before scanning or organising an existing
284	  machine; includes the non-destructive index default and move safety gates.
285	- `references/worktree-ownership.md` — who owns which worktree, and how a
286	  worktree gets a working environment. Read before creating one.
287	- `references/task-lifecycle.md` — HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, when to park, and how
288	  work moves between machines.
289	- `references/runtime-herdr.md` — how `dev` and herdr divide responsibility,
290	  and the sidebar configuration that makes task state visible.
291	- `references/commands.md` — the full command reference, generated from the
292	  binary by `dev skill sync` so it cannot drift.
293
294	## Gotchas
295
296	- **`dev` is a shell function, not just a binary.** Commands that move you into
297	  a checkout print a `cd` directive for the wrapper installed by
298	  `eval "$(dev shell-init zsh)"`. Without it they print a path and do not move
299	  you — that is not a bug.
300	- **A worktree is a clean checkout.** It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv` and
301	  none of the gitignored env files. `dev` provisions it; `--no-provision`
302	  skips that and leaves you to it.
303	- **Only gitignored files are copied into a worktree.** Listing a *tracked*
304	  file in `worktree.include` does nothing, because git already put it there on
305	  the correct branch — and copying it would overwrite that version.
306	- **Removing a worktree never deletes the branch.** Those are separate
307	  decisions; conflating them is how work gets lost.
308	- **`dev done` defaults to reporting.** With neither `--ff` nor `--pr` it
309	  explains the options and changes nothing.
310	- **The stats sampler must be scheduled.** `dev stats` is empty until
311	  `dev stats backfill` runs once and `dev stats sample` runs periodically.
312
```

1	# dev and herdr
2
3	Read this when working on a machine that runs herdr, or when a task's state
4	should be visible in the sidebar.
5
6	## The division
7
8	```
9	herdr    per-host runtime: what is running, where the panes are, which agent
10	         is working right now
11	dev      cross-host intent: which change streams exist, what state each is in,
12	         what to do next
13	git      durable truth: the commits
14	```
15
16	herdr is deliberately **not** synced between machines, and `dev` does not try
17	to. Each host runs its own herdr; `dev ls --json` is the aggregation point:
18
19	```bash
20	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json
21	ssh jingle-247 dev ls --json
22	```
23
24	## What dev asks herdr to do
25
26	`dev` shells out to the herdr CLI, which emits JSON for everything it needs:
27
28	| dev operation | herdr command |
29	|---|---|
30	| list live sessions | `workspace list` + `pane list` (panes carry the cwd) |
31	| open a checkout | `workspace create --cwd <dir> --label <name>` |
32	| open a **worktree** | `worktree open --path <path> --label <name>` |
33	| close a session | `workspace close <id>` |
34	| show task state | `workspace report-metadata <id> --source dev --token …` |
35
36	`worktree open` rather than `workspace create` for a worktree is what gives the
37	checkout git provenance in herdr: it appears grouped under its parent repo's
38	space with its own branch and ahead/behind row, rather than as an unrelated
39	directory.
40
41	`dev` does **not** call `herdr worktree create` — see
42	`worktree-ownership.md` for why.
43
44	Note that `workspace close` only ends herdr's session state. It does not delete
45	the directory, the worktree or the branch. That separation is exactly the one
46	`dev park` relies on.
47
48	## Making task state visible in the sidebar
49
50	`dev` reports two metadata tokens on the workspace hosting a task:
51
52	- `$stage` — `HOT`, `WARM`, `COLD`, `DONE`
53	- `$next` — the task's next action
54
55	A token only renders if the sidebar row layout names it. Setting one with no
56	matching layout entry succeeds silently and shows nothing, so add this to
57	`~/.config/herdr/config.toml`:
58
59	```toml
60	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
61	rows = [
62	  ["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"],
63	  ["branch", "git_status"],
64	  ["$next"],
65	]
66	```
67
68	Which turns a row into:
69
70	```
71	● atp-sipui · HOT
72	  fix/gx-security-recovery ↑2
73	  finish the refresh regression test
74	```
75
76	That is far more useful than leaving four agents running in the hope that
77	seeing their names jogs your memory.
78
79	Because the layout is pinned by hand, re-check it against `herdr --default-config`
80	after a herdr upgrade — upstream changes to the default rows will not reach a
81	customised layout.
82
83	## Sidebar hygiene
84
85	The sidebar is working memory, not storage. Aim for three to seven hot spaces
86	per machine; everything else lives in `dev ls`.
87
88	`dev sweep` reports live sessions with no task recorded, which is usually where
89	the excess is. For each one, either `dev start` in that directory to track it,
90	or just close it — now that closing is not the same as forgetting.
91
92	## Agents are processes, not bookmarks
93
94	An agent pane with useful context in it is tempting to leave running forever.
95	Don't: herdr surfaces a resumable `agent_session` id, and `dev` stores it on
96	the task, so the conversation can be resumed after the process is gone.
97
98	Structure the isolation this way:
99
100	```
101	one independent change stream
102	        → one worktree
103	        → one workspace
104	        → N tabs / panes
105	        → N agents
106	```
107
108	Not one worktree per agent.
109
110	## Without herdr
111
112	`dev` selects `herdr` → `tmux` → `none`, in that order, and `runtime.backend`
113	pins it explicitly. The `none` backend prints a `cd` directive for the shell
114	wrapper instead of opening a session — so every core operation still works with
115	nothing but git installed.
116
```

```text
1	# Worktree ownership
2
3	Read this before creating a worktree, or when a new checkout is missing its
4	dependencies or `.env`.
5
6	## The confusion this resolves
7
8	Three mechanisms create git worktrees, and they all look interchangeable:
9
10	- `claude --worktree <name>` / `isolation: worktree` / `/batch` — Claude Code's
11	  own, under `.claude/worktrees/`.
12	- `herdr worktree create --branch … --base …` — creates a checkout under
13	  `~/.herdr/worktrees/` and opens it as a herdr workspace.
14	- `git worktree add` by hand, or a tool like Worktrunk.
15
16	They are all standard git worktrees underneath, so nothing *breaks* if you mix
17	them. What breaks is the mental model: two lifecycle owners for one checkout,
18	and no single answer to "where do worktrees live on this machine?"
19
20	## The rule
21
22	| Kind of worktree | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
23	|---|---|---|---|
24	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
25	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` | dies with the turn |
26	| Everything else | **`dev`** | as above | as above |
27
28	**Might a human come back to it tomorrow → `dev`. Does it die with this agent
29	turn → Claude Code native.**
30
31	Concretely:
32
33	- Two agents implementing *different approaches* to the same problem, so the
34	  best can be picked → Claude Code worktrees. They are disposable.
35	- Two agents working on *disjoint files of one feature* → no worktree at all.
36	  One checkout, one branch, separate panes. Worktrees isolate change streams;
37	  panes isolate agents.
38	- A feature you will still be working on next week → `dev start`.
39	- Picking up on a different machine → `dev park --cold --push` here,
40	  `dev resume` there. The branch is the identity; the directory is a cache.
41
42	## Why `dev` does not call `herdr worktree create`
43
44	`dev` runs `git worktree add` itself, then calls
45	`herdr worktree open --path <path> --label <task>`.
46
47	The path policy has to hold on machines without herdr — a laptop, a CI box, a
48	server you ssh into. Delegating placement to herdr would mean worktrees land
49	somewhere different depending on what happens to be installed. Creating the
50	checkout with git and asking herdr only to *open* it keeps one policy and still
51	gets the full sidebar treatment: the workspace is grouped under its parent repo
52	with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
53
54	## Never nest a worktree inside a repository
55
56	`.claude/worktrees/` is acceptable for turn-scoped work because Claude Code
57	cleans it up and the directory is gitignored. For anything longer-lived, a
58	checkout inside another checkout means every file watcher, language server,
59	indexer, backup tool and `rg` run in the outer repo sees a second copy of the
60	whole tree.
61
62	`dev` refuses to create one, and will tell you to point
63	`paths.worktree_path` somewhere outside the repo.
64
65	If you do use `.claude/worktrees/`, keep `.claude/worktrees/` in `.gitignore`
66	so the contents never show as untracked files in the main checkout.
67
68	## Where dev puts them
69
70	Default:
71
72	```
73	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
74	```
75
76	Fully configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine — a
77	different volume, a different naming convention:
78
79	```toml
80	[paths]
81	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
82	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
83	```
84
85	Variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`,
86	`date`. Filters: `|slug` (filesystem-safe: `feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`),
87	`|lower`, `|base`.
88
89	The reason for a separate root rather than siblings of the repo: with one or
90	two worktrees, `repo/` and `repo.feat-auth/` side by side is perfectly clear.
91	With ten, the projects directory stops answering "what projects do I have?" —
92	the filesystem hierarchy starts doing git's job badly.
93
94	## Provisioning: making a worktree actually usable
95
96	A worktree is a **clean checkout**. It has no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, and
97	none of the gitignored files the project needs to run. Without provisioning,
98	every new worktree starts broken.
99
100	`dev wt create` (and `dev start`) builds an inspectable provisioning plan,
101	then applies it. See the plan before creating anything:
102
103	```bash
104	dev wt plan                 # detect project types and show every action
105	dev wt plan --write         # seed a committed .dev.toml from the result
106	dev wt provision --dry-run  # plan for an existing checkout
107	```
108
109	The settings live under `[worktree]` globally or in the repo's own `.dev.toml`:
110
111	```toml
112	[worktree]
113	# Gitignored files to carry over.
114	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
115
116	# Heavy directories to symlink instead of copy. Opt-in and empty by default —
117	# sharing node_modules across checkouts breaks native builds often enough that
118	# it must never happen by accident.
119	link = []
120
121	# "auto" detects from lockfiles, or give an explicit list.
122	post_create = "auto"
123
124	# How installed dependencies arrive. The safe default is reinstall.
125	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
126
127	[worktree.strategies]
128	node = "copy"               # override one ecosystem
129	```
130
131	**Only files that are both listed *and* gitignored are copied.** A tracked file
132	is already in the new checkout on the correct branch; copying the source
133	branch's version over it would be wrong. The classic mistake is listing
134	`.vscode/settings.json` — it is committed, so it is already there.
135
136	`post_create = "auto"` detects one command per ecosystem:
137
138	| Marker | Command |
139	|---|---|
140	| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` |
141	| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` |
142	| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
143	| `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
144	| `yarn.lock` | `yarn install --immutable` |
145	| `go.mod` | `go mod download` |
146	| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fetch` |
147	| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` |
148
149	A detected command whose tool is not installed is skipped, not failed. A failed
150	command is reported but leaves the checkout in place — it is usable, and
151	throwing it away would cost the branch for nothing.
152
153
154	## Copy, reinstall, link, or skip?
155
156	This is a per-ecosystem correctness decision, not merely a speed preference:
157
158	| Strategy | Effect | Default use |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| `reinstall` | Run the lockfile-derived install command | Always sound; default |
161	| `copy` | Duplicate the dependency directory from the source checkout | Faster where path-independent |
162	| `link` | Share one directory between checkouts | Fastest; usually unsafe |
163	| `skip` | Leave dependencies absent | Container/CI-driven projects |
164
165	`dev` encodes the non-obvious facts:
166
167	- Python `.venv` **cannot be copied or linked**: `pyvenv.cfg`, activation
168	  scripts and entry points bake in the old absolute path. `uv sync` uses a
169	  shared cache and is normally cheap anyway.
170	- Node `node_modules` can be copied, including pnpm's symlinks (links are
171	  recreated, not dereferenced). Sharing one tree is refused because an install
172	  in either checkout silently changes the other.
173	- Go modules are already in a global content-addressed cache; there is no local
174	  directory worth copying.
175	- Cargo `target/` can be copied, but is often larger than rebuilding. Sharing
176	  it is refused because concurrent builds write the same lock/artifacts.
177
178	An unsound configured strategy is not obeyed blindly: `dev wt plan` says why
179	and narrows it back to `reinstall`. A typo likewise becomes a warning rather
180	than silently skipping dependencies.
181
182	`post_create` and strategy are separate axes. An explicit command list replaces
183	the *derived install commands* but does not disable a `copy` strategy. A project
184	can copy `node_modules` and then run `make bootstrap`.
185
186	Per-repo override, committed next to the code so it reaches every machine:
187
188	```toml
189	# <repo>/.dev.toml
190	[worktree]
191	include     = [".env", "config/local.json"]
192	post_create = ["make bootstrap"]
193
194	[worktree.strategies]
195	node = "copy"
196	```
197
198	Re-run provisioning on an existing checkout with `dev wt provision`.
199
200	## Cleanup
201
202	```bash
203	dev wt rm feat/auth      # removes the checkout; the branch survives
204	```
205
206	Removing a worktree and abandoning a change stream are different decisions.
207	`dev` never deletes a branch as a side effect, and refuses to remove a checkout
208	with uncommitted changes without an explicit `--force`.
209
210	If a directory was deleted behind git's back, `dev wt rm` and `dev sweep` prune
211	the stale administrative entry instead of failing.
212
```
