```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2
3	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
4	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
5
6	## The problem
7
8	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
9	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
10	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
11	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
12
13	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
14	not the runtime.
15
16	## Pick a checkout mode before a lifecycle
17
18	A task records human intent; it does not imply a worktree:
19
20	| Command | Checkout boundary | Use when |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| `dev repo open api` | none; no task | browsing or truly ad-hoc work |
23	| `dev start api -t typo --direct` | current branch, usually main | one short tracked change |
24	| `dev start api -t small --branch-only` | branch in canonical checkout | lightweight isolation, no concurrency |
25	| `dev start api -t auth --base main` | branch + linked worktree | interruption, experiment, parallel writer |
26
27	Direct tasks go HOT ↔ WARM and finish with plain `dev done`; they cannot go
28	COLD because the canonical checkout cannot be removed. Branch-only tasks can go
29	cold after push by switching the canonical checkout back to base. The full
30	state machine below describes the default worktree mode.
31
32	Do not create isolation before it has a job. Equally, a new parallel worktree
33	starts from committed HEAD — it does not carry dirty main changes — so
34	checkpoint first when the new task depends on them.
35
36	## The four states
37
38	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
39	|---|---|---|---|
40	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
41	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
42	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
43	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
44
45	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
46
47	```
48	        dev start
49	            │
50	            ▼
51	         🔥 hot ──── dev done ────► ✅ done
52	          │  ▲
53	   dev park│  │dev resume
54	          ▼  │
55	        🌤 warm
56	          │  ▲
57	dev park  │  │dev resume
58	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)
59	        ❄️ cold
60	```
61
62	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
63	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
64
65	## Parking
66
67	```bash
68	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
69	```
70
71	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
72	next, closes the runtime session, and leaves the checkout boundary exactly
73	where it is. In direct mode that is the current branch; in worktree mode it is
74	the branch and linked checkout.
75
76	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
77	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
78	supply one.
79
80	Useful variations:
81
82	```bash
83	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
84	dev park --cold --push            # push, remove the worktree, keep the branch
85	dev park --keep-session           # record the state, leave the session open
86	```
87
88	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
89
90	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
91
92	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
93	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
94	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
95
96	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
97	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
98	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
99	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
100
101	## Cold, and why it is safe
102
103	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
104
105	- the branch still holds every commit;
106	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
107	  them too;
108	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
109
110	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
111	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
112
113	## Moving work between machines
114
115	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
116	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
117
118	On the machine holding the work:
119
120	```bash
121	dev park --cold --push
122	```
123
124	On the machine picking it up:
125
126	```bash
127	dev resume <task> --fetch
128	```
129
130	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
131	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
132	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
133	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
134
135	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
136	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
137	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
138
139	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
140	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
141	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
142
143	## Sweeping
144
145	```bash
146	dev sweep            # report only
147	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
148	```
149
150	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
151
152	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
153	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about.
154	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
155	  pushed, that could go cold.
156
157	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
158	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
159
160	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. The
161	reason cleanup usually does not happen is not unwillingness; it is the absence
162	of a trustworthy guarantee that the work is recoverable. Reporting first, and
163	requiring confirmation, is that guarantee.
164
165	## Integration
166
167	```bash
168	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
169	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via gh or glab
170	```
171
172	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
173	keeping in the base's history?**
174
175	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
176	  stay legible.
177	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
178	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
179
180	`dev done` refuses on a dirty tree, and `--delete-branch` only removes a branch
181	git agrees is fully contained in the base. "Merged" is not always "finished" —
182	work often continues on a branch after its first integration, which is why the
183	branch survives by default.
184
```
</details></tool-use>

12	func TestRenderHasValidFrontmatter(t *testing.T) {

14		if err != nil {

16		}

19		}

# Parallel agents

How to run several coding agents without them stepping on each other.

## The one rule

> **Worktree per change stream. Exact pane per agent.**

Not one worktree per agent. Isolation follows the *git mutation boundary*, not
who is typing.

```
one independent change stream
        → one worktree
        → one Herdr workspace
        → one exact launch pane
        → one or more coordinated agents
```

## Choose the operation

| Intent | Action |
|---|---|
| Observe existing work | `herdr agent get/read/wait`; do not send probe keys or focus it |
| Spawn independent work | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --base <committed-ref> --json`, validate the exact new pane, then launch there |
| Handoff the same task | Settle the old session, checkpoint dirty code, get explicit user agreement, then resume with a new forked session ID |

A new independent task does not need to wait for an unrelated agent. It does
need a committed base: dirty state in another checkout is not inherited.

## Shared-checkout collision guard

Herdr-aware open/start/resume paths compare recognized agents by canonical Git
worktree root and reject a checkout occupied by another pane. `idle`, `done`,
`blocked`, `working`, and `unknown` are all occupied states. Only the calling
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is excluded.

`--allow-shared-checkout` is an explicit escape hatch for agents whose disjoint
file ownership has already been coordinated. Never add it speculatively.
Default `dev start` worktree creation remains allowed because it creates a new
checkout boundary.

Use `dev status` in a checkout to see recognized activities.

## When agents can share a checkout

They can when file ownership is explicit and disjoint:

| Parallel work | Same checkout? |
|---|---|
| One researching, one coding | yes, if only one writes |
| Frontend and backend with owned paths | yes, with explicit coordination |
| Both editing one manifest/API surface | no |
| Either changing HEAD, rebasing, formatting globally, or running codegen | no |
| Unknown file ranges | no |

## Ownership boundaries

```
dev         durable task, branch and checkout lifecycle
Herdr       workspace, pane, process detection and live state
SpecStory   rendered history rooted at the launch checkout
Git         durable code and review artifacts
```

A pane move changes layout, not process cwd. `EnterWorktree` does not prove an
already-running SpecStory writer rebound to a new path. Start the new process
from the target worktree root instead.

## Launching a background agent

`dev start` creates the task/worktree/runtime target; it does not start an
agent. The bundled `dev-cli` skill owns the fail-closed cross-tool workflow and
supports standard Claude/Codex plus the local one-shot Copilot launchers.

Do not infer a pane from focus or sidebar order. Missing, reused, fallback,
non-Herdr, or unverified panes are not launch targets.

## Cleanup is explicit

Herdr `done` means a turn settled; it does not mean history is synced, review is
complete, code is committed, or the workspace may close.

- `dev park` closes the workspace and keeps the checkout.
- `dev park --cold --push` closes the workspace and removes a reconstructible checkout.
- `dev done --ff` integrates and cleans up the workspace/worktree.
- `dev done --pr` leaves the task and checkout for review.
- `dev sweep` reports first; `--apply` is a separate confirmed action.

`--cold --keep-session` is rejected because a live session must not point at a
removed checkout.

## Bringing environment into a worktree

Every worktree is a clean checkout. `dev` provisions gitignored files listed in
`worktree.include` and dependencies configured for the repo.

`.claude/settings.local.json` is not a universal default. The one-shot Copilot
wrappers materialize or inject their own backend. Add that exact path to
`worktree.include` only for an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile;
`dev` copies only a regular, gitignored file and never logs its contents.

# Parallel background agents

Read this when starting independent agent work while another agent remains live,
or when launching an agent into a worktree created by `dev start --json`.

## Boundary and owners

> **Worktree per change stream; one SpecStory root per worktree; exact pane per
> agent; exact transcript/plan finalization.**

- `dev` owns the durable task, branch and checkout.
- Herdr owns workspace/pane layout and live process detection.
- SpecStory owns rendered history rooted at the process launch checkout.
- Git owns the code, transcript and plan that survive cleanup.

`dev start` does not start an agent. This workflow composes `dev`, Herdr and
SpecStory after verifying each boundary.

## Preflight

- [ ] `test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1`
- [ ] `dev doctor`
- [ ] `command -v specstory`
- [ ] Explicit task name and committed base ref are known.
- [ ] New work does not depend on another checkout's uncommitted state.
- [ ] Launch profile and permission mode are explicit.

If the new task needs dirty state, wait for the owning agent to make a checkpoint
commit and use that exact commit/ref as `--base`. Do not stash, reset, switch, or
copy another agent's checkout.

## Create and validate the target

Choose a human runtime label that describes the child and its origin, for
example `child-task ← parent-agent` or `child-task ← w1Z`. IDs remain transient
Herdr metadata; the task/branch identity does not change.

```bash
result="$(dev start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>' \
  --runtime-label '<child ← origin>' --json)" || {
  # Side effects may exist even though no success JSON was emitted. Stop and
  # reconcile the reported task/worktree manually; do not retry blindly.
  exit 1
}
```

Accept the result only when all of these are true:

```text
mode == "worktree"
repo_path, worktree_path and checkout are absolute
checkout == worktree_path
runtime.name == "herdr"
runtime.surface == "worktree"
runtime.opened == true
runtime.created == true
runtime.root_pane_id is non-empty
```

Missing/reused/fallback/non-Herdr results remain useful tasks/worktrees, but are
not launchable targets. Stop without guessing another pane.

When invoked from another Herdr workspace, a newly created target may report
`origin.workspace_id` and `origin.pane_id`. `dev` also annotates only the target
workspace with `$origin_workspace`/`$origin_pane`; it skips missing or self
origins and never persists them in the task TOML.

## Verify the exact pane

Use only `runtime.root_pane_id` from the JSON object:

```bash
herdr pane get "$root_pane_id"
herdr pane process-info --pane "$root_pane_id"
```

Verify:

- pane cwd and foreground cwd equal the JSON `checkout`;
- it is the returned target workspace/pane, not the caller pane;
- no agent is recognized there;
- process info shows an interactive shell ready for launch.

Do not use current/focused pane, sidebar order, or `pane list` to choose a
fallback. The launch command itself is the final availability gate.

## Select a launcher profile

A new external process does **not** inherit the parent agent's permission mode.
A resumed/forked Claude session also does not restore bypass mode. Therefore the
caller must explicitly choose both profile and permission mode; never infer or
elevate one when unknown.

| Profile | Exact root-pane command shape | Backend state |
|---|---|---|
| standard Claude | `specstory run claude -c claude [native args]` | normal project/config resolution |
| standard Codex | `specstory run codex -c codex [native args]` | normal project/config resolution |
| `claude-copilot-once` | call the shell function directly with native args | wrapper already runs SpecStory, creates a fresh destination pin, removes only its own pin |
| `codex-copilot-once` | call the shell function directly with native args | wrapper already runs SpecStory and injects backend through CLI |
| sticky/plain Claude | `specstory run claude -c claude [native args]` | require exact `.claude/settings.local.json` in `worktree.include` and verify it exists in the target |

Do not add a second watcher for any of these profiles. The standard profiles use
`specstory run`; both `*-copilot-once` wrappers already invoke SpecStory and
preserve argv.

For an explicitly requested Claude bypass launch, include:

```text
claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions
```

For explicit handoff/fork with bypass, include both because the resumed session
does not restore it:

```text
claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --resume <uuid> --fork-session
```

Without explicit bypass, use the selected non-elevated mode/profile. Never copy
permission flags from assumptions about the parent process or user-wide config.

The one-shot wrapper examples are shell functions, so execute through the
interactive shell in the exact pane. Preserve every native argument after the
function name. Standard profiles may be sent as the direct `specstory run`
command shown above.

## Launch, detect and name

Run the selected command in the exact interactive root pane. Then let Herdr
detect the process and assign the requested unique agent name; do not start a
second process merely to obtain a name.

After detection, use Herdr's explicit agent surface to rename/verify the process
and submit work:

```bash
herdr agent rename "$root_pane_id" "$agent_name"
herdr agent get "$agent_name"
herdr agent prompt "$agent_name" "$explicit_prompt"
```

The prompt intentionally omits `--wait`, so independent work continues in the
background. Report checkout, branch, workspace, exact pane, profile and agent
name. Observe later with `agent get`, `agent read`, and `agent wait`; never focus
or send probe keys.

Treat `working`, `blocked`, `idle`, `done`, and `unknown` as occupied. `blocked`
requires a user decision. `done` means turn-settled, not cleanup-ready.

## Shared-checkout override

`dev` guards direct/branch tasks and existing-checkout open/resume paths when
another recognized Herdr agent resolves to the same canonical Git worktree.
Only the exact caller `HERDR_PANE_ID` is excluded.

Use global `--allow-shared-checkout` only after agents have explicit, disjoint
file ownership. This skill must never add it automatically. Default worktree
creation needs no override because it creates an independent checkout.

## Project-local backend state

Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` to global/default includes. It is
needed only by an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile:

```toml
[worktree]
include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
```

The file must be a regular, gitignored source file. `dev` copies only explicitly
included matches, refuses symlink sources, never overwrites a destination, and
logs only the relative path—not file contents. Verify the target file exists
before launching; otherwise stop rather than silently falling back to another
backend.

The `claude-copilot-once` and `codex-copilot-once` profiles do not need this
copy: their verified wrappers manage backend selection themselves.

## Finalize artifacts and clean up

Before park/integration, settle the agent, identify the exact session UUID, and
from the target worktree root run:

```bash
specstory sync claude -s <exact-session-id>   # or the selected provider
```

Stage exact transcript and plan paths. If one UUID has multiple rendered
candidates, require an explicit path; do not choose by mtime or bulk-sync every
session in the checkout.

Cleanup remains explicit and is never triggered by Herdr `done`:

- `dev park --next '<next>'` closes the workspace and keeps the worktree.
- `dev park --cold --push` closes the workspace and removes the pushed checkout.
- `dev done --ff` integrates and cleans up runtime/worktree.
- `dev done --pr` leaves task/runtime/worktree state for review.
- `dev sweep` reports first; use `--apply` only after review/confirmation.

`dev park --cold --keep-session` is invalid because it would strand a live
session on a removed checkout.

# dev and Herdr

Read this on a Herdr machine, when task state should appear in the sidebar, or
when a `dev start --json` result will be used to launch an agent.

## Division of responsibility

```
Herdr       per-host workspace, pane, process and live-agent state
dev         durable task, branch and checkout lifecycle
SpecStory   history writer rooted at the launched process checkout
Git         durable commits, transcript and plan
```

Herdr is not synced between machines. `dev` persists only its task facts and the
advisory runtime handle; root pane, runtime label and origin metadata are
transient create results.

## What dev asks Herdr to do

| dev operation | Herdr command |
|---|---|
| list live sessions | `workspace list` + `pane list` |
| list pane-level agent activity | `agent list` |
| open a checkout | `workspace create --cwd <dir> --no-focus --label <name>` |
| open a worktree | `worktree open --path <path> --no-focus --label <name>` |
| close a session | `workspace close <id>` |
| show task/origin metadata | `workspace report-metadata <id> --source dev --token …` |

`dev` creates worktrees with Git and only asks Herdr to open them. First-class
`worktree open` gives the workspace Git provenance and branch/ahead-behind data.
A plain-workspace fallback reports `surface=workspace` honestly.

A root pane is launchable only when the same successful `worktree open` response
proves a newly created layout. Reuse, fallback, missing/malformed responses,
Tmux, and the `none` runtime never supply a launchable pane. `--no-focus`
preserves the caller's context; never substitute the focused/current pane.

Read `parallel-agents.md` for the exact machine workflow, pane verification,
SpecStory profiles and permission-mode rules.

## Collision preflight

On Herdr, `dev` compares recognized agent cwd values by canonical Git worktree
root before direct/branch starts and existing-checkout open/resume operations.
Only exact `HERDR_PANE_ID` is excluded. Every recognized state—including
`idle`, `done`, and `unknown`—is occupied.

The root `--allow-shared-checkout` escape hatch is only for coordinated agents
with disjoint ownership. Never add it automatically. A default `dev start`
worktree is still allowed because it creates a separate checkout.

`dev status` shows recognized activities for the current worktree.

## Runtime label and origin

`dev start --runtime-label '<human label>'` changes only the workspace label; it
does not change task ID, name, branch, or persisted schema. When a new Herdr
workspace is created from inside another Herdr pane, `dev` annotates only the
target with:

- `$origin_workspace = HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`
- `$origin_pane = HERDR_PANE_ID`

Missing origin or an origin equal to the target workspace is skipped. The JSON
creation result returns the label and origin IDs, but task TOML does not.

For parallel launch, derive a readable label such as `child-task ← parent-agent`
or `child-task ← w1Z`; keep opaque IDs in origin metadata.

## Sidebar metadata

Task annotations use `$stage` and `$next`; origin annotations use
`$origin_workspace` and `$origin_pane`. Tokens render only if the local Herdr
row layout names them. Reporting an unused token succeeds silently.

```toml
[ui.sidebar.spaces]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"],
  ["branch", "git_status"],
  ["$next"],
]
```

## Cleanup semantics

Herdr agent `done` means the latest turn settled. It does not establish that
history is synced, review is complete, code is committed, or cleanup is safe.
Never auto-close based on agent state.

- `dev park` closes the workspace and keeps the worktree.
- `dev park --cold --push` closes and removes a reconstructible checkout.
- `dev done --ff` integrates and cleans up.
- `dev done --pr` leaves task/runtime/worktree for review.
- `dev sweep` reports first.

`workspace close` itself touches no branch or checkout. `--cold --keep-session`
is rejected so a session cannot remain pointed at a removed directory.

## Agent sessions are not yet attached by dev

Herdr exposes live agent session IDs and `Task.AgentSession` exists in the task
schema, but production `start`, `park`, and `resume` do not currently capture or
attach an agent conversation. Resume reopens/rebuilds the checkout and runtime;
agent-session handoff remains an explicit launcher operation.

## Without Herdr

Runtime selection is Herdr → Tmux → none unless pinned. Tmux can report session
creation/reuse but no pane. `none` emits a shell `cd` directive in human mode;
`dev start --json` suppresses that directive and stays pure JSON.

# Worktree ownership

Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.

## The rule

| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until explicit park/done/sweep cleanup |
| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |

Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
coordination override—not a default.

`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
new process from the target worktree root.

## Why dev creates the checkout

`dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run
`worktree open --path <path> --no-focus`. Path policy therefore remains stable
on machines without Herdr, while Herdr still displays repo/branch provenance.
A fallback plain workspace is reported as such and is not an exact agent launch
target.

Never nest a durable worktree inside another checkout. Every watcher, language
server, backup tool and search then sees a second copy of the repository.

## Paths

Default:

```text
~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
```

Configurable through `paths.worktree_root` and `paths.worktree_path`, with
`worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`, and `date`
variables plus `slug`, `lower`, and `base` filters.

Always pass `--base` for unattended creation. A new branch otherwise inherits
the current HEAD, which may be an unrelated feature.

## Provisioning

A worktree is a clean checkout. `dev wt create` and `dev start` build and apply
an inspectable plan:

```bash
dev wt plan
dev wt plan --write
dev wt provision --dry-run
```

Effective settings come from global config or committed repo `.dev.toml`:

```toml
[worktree]
include = [".env", ".env.local"]
link = []
post_create = "auto"
strategy = "reinstall"
```

Only paths that are both explicitly included and genuinely gitignored are
copied. Tracked files already have the branch-correct version. Included files
must be regular files; symlink sources are refused rather than followed, and
file contents are never logged.

### Project-local Claude backend state

`.claude/settings.local.json` stays gitignored and is **not** a universal default
include. The verified `claude-copilot-once` wrapper creates/removes only its own
fresh backend pin; `codex-copilot-once` injects its backend via CLI. Neither
needs a copied project file.

An explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile may opt in exactly:

```toml
[worktree]
include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
```

Verify the file arrived before launch. If absent, stop instead of allowing the
launcher to fall back silently to another backend. `dev` logs the relative path
only, never its contents.

## Dependency strategies

- `reinstall`: safe default; run lockfile-derived installer.
- `copy`: duplicate path-independent dependency trees.
- `link`: explicit and usually unsafe for mutable dependencies.
- `skip`: for external/container-managed environments.

`dev` refuses unsound choices, such as copied/linked Python virtualenvs, and
reports missing tools or failed setup without deleting the usable checkout.

## Cleanup

- `dev wt rm <branch>` removes only the checkout; branch survives.
- `dev park` closes runtime, keeps worktree/branch.
- `dev park --cold --push` closes runtime and removes the pushed worktree.
- `dev done --ff` integrates and cleans runtime/worktree.
- `dev done --pr` leaves everything active for review.
- `dev sweep` reports first; `--apply` is separate.

Dirty checkout removal requires explicit force. Herdr `done` is not a cleanup
signal, and `--cold --keep-session` is rejected.

````

65	## The lifecycle
66
67	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
68	|---|---|---|---|
69	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
70	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session **closed** | back within days |
71	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
72	| ✅ `done` | merged | nothing | entry survives until swept |
73
74	```bash
75	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main   # → hot
76	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip    # → warm, session closed
77	dev park --cold --push                             # → cold, worktree removed
78	dev resume "token refresh"                         # → hot, rebuilt if needed
79	dev done --ff                                      # → done, integrated
80	dev sweep                                          # what has gone stale
81	```
82
83	### A task does not have to mean a worktree
84
85	Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:
86
87	```bash
88	# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
89	dev repo open api
90
91	# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
92	dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct
93
94	# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
95	dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
96
97	# Default: independent branch + worktree, provisioned and runtime-opened.
98	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main
99	```
100
101	Direct work can be parked WARM and resumed, but cannot go COLD because the
102	canonical checkout cannot be removed. `dev done` on a clean direct task needs
103	no `--ff` or `--pr`: the work is already on its destination branch.
104
105	Start direct for one change stream, then create a normal worktree task later
106	when real parallelism appears. A new worktree starts from committed HEAD; dirty
107	main changes are deliberately not smuggled into it, so checkpoint first when
108	the parallel task depends on them.
109
110	### The dashboard
111
112	Bare `dev` (or `dev tui`) opens three lists, switched with `tab`:
113
114	- **TASKS** — the change streams dev is tracking. What am I working on.
115	- **REPOS** — every repository under the scan roots, with its branch, dirty
116	  state, worktree count and per-state task tally, sorted so anything in flight
117	  is at the top. What do I have here.
118	- **REMOTE** — repositories visible through the authenticated `gh` and `glab`
119	  CLIs, marked when a local clone exists. What can I open or clone.
120
121	TASKS and REPOS come from the same code paths as `dev ls` and `dev repo list`,
122	so they cannot disagree. The repo list matters on day one: with forty repositories and
123	no tasks recorded yet, a task-only dashboard would just be empty.
124
125	Navigation is vim-style, arrows alongside:
126
127	```
128	j k        move                 ctrl+d ctrl+u   half a page
129	g G        top / bottom         h l / tab       previous / next view
```

224	## Worktree ownership
225
226	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
227	to improvise:
228
229	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
230	|---|---|---|---|
231	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until `dev done` / `dev sweep` |
232	| Turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | dies with the turn |
233	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
234
235	**Might you come back tomorrow → `dev`. Dies with this agent turn → Claude
236	Code native.**
237
238	`dev` does not delegate placement to herdr because the path policy has to hold
239	on machines without herdr. It creates the checkout with plain git and asks
240	herdr only to *open* it — which still surfaces it in the sidebar grouped under
241	its parent repo with its own branch and ahead/behind row.
242
243	`dev` refuses to create a worktree inside a repository: a checkout nested in
244	another checkout makes every indexer, file watcher and `rg` run see a second
245	copy of the tree.
246
247	### Provisioning
248
249	A worktree is a clean checkout — no `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`.
250	Without provisioning, every new one starts broken. `dev` copies the gitignored
251	files you list, optionally symlinks heavy directories, and runs a setup
252	command detected from the lockfiles:
253
254	```toml
255	[worktree]
256	include     = [".env", ".env.local"]   # only files that are ALSO gitignored
257	link        = []                       # opt-in; sharing node_modules is risky
258	post_create = "auto"                   # uv.lock → uv sync, package-lock.json → npm ci, …
259	```
260
261	**Copy or reinstall?** Reinstalling is always correct but can take minutes;
262	copying is fast but only sound for dependency trees carrying no absolute paths.
263	That is a per-ecosystem fact, not a preference, so dev knows it:
264
265	```toml
266	[worktree]
267	strategy = "reinstall"      # reinstall | copy | link | skip
268
269	[worktree.strategies]
270	node = "copy"               # node_modules copies soundly
271	```
272
273	Asking to copy a virtualenv is refused with the reason — it bakes its own
274	absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg` and `bin/activate` — and narrowed back to
275	reinstalling rather than silently producing a broken checkout.
276
277	`dev wt plan` shows exactly what a new worktree of a repository would get:
278	which project types were detected, which tools are missing, and every file and
279	command involved. `dev wt plan --write` seeds a `<repo>/.dev.toml` from it, so
280	a project can commit its own setup and every machine provisions the same way.
281
282	```
283	$ dev wt plan
284	PROJECT  MANAGER  FROM               DEPENDENCIES  TOOL
```

425
426	## Configuration
427
428	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml`. Write a commented starter with
429	`dev config init`; see the effective settings with `dev config show`; open the
430	actual file in `$VISUAL` / `$EDITOR` with either form:
431
432	```bash
433	dev edit
434	dev config edit
435	DEV_EDITOR=unused dev edit --editor "code --wait"   # explicit override
436	```
437
438	If the file does not exist, `edit` generates the machine-detected starter first
439	rather than opening an empty file. Resolution is `--editor` → `$VISUAL` →
440	`$EDITOR` → `nvim` → `vim` → `vi`.
441
442	Every path is configurable, because the right answer depends on the machine —
443	a faster volume, a different naming convention:
444
445	```toml
446	[paths]
447	scan_roots    = ["~/Documents/Program", "~/src/tries"]
448	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/worktrees"
449	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}/{{branch|slug}}"
450	state_dir     = "~/.local/share/dev"        # point at a git repo to sync it
451	```
452
453	Template variables: `worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`,
454	`host`, `date`. Filters: `|slug` (`feat/auth/x` → `feat-auth-x`), `|lower`,
455	`|base`. A typo in a variable name fails at load, not as a directory literally
456	named `{{rep}}`.
457
458	A flat project layout is already first-class — it needs no migration and no
459	special mode:
460
461	```toml
462	[paths]
463	scan_roots   = ["~/code"]
464	project_root = "~/code"       # repo new/clone/graduate land at ~/code/<repo>
465	worktree_root = "/mnt/fast/wt"
466	worktree_path = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo|lower}}--{{branch|slug}}"
467	```
468
469	Omit `--category` and canonical repos stay flat. Categories are metadata the
470	user may choose, never a directory structure dev imposes.
471
472	## Multiple machines
473
474	Do not sync worktrees or runtime state. Sync branches, and let the remote be
475	the handoff boundary:
476
477	```bash
478	dev park --cold --push      # on the machine holding the work
479	dev resume <task> --fetch   # on the machine picking it up
480	```
481
482	`dev` records an owner host per task and refuses to resume someone else's
483	without `--force`. Two machines committing to one branch is the reliable way
484	to produce a conflict here; the ownership check prevents it.
485
486	For a cross-machine view, `dev ls --json` is a stable contract:
487
488	```bash
489	ssh jingle-235 dev ls --json | jq '.[] | select(.state=="hot")'
490	```
491
492	## The agent skill
493
494	`dev` ships the agent skill that documents it, embedded in the binary — the
495	same pattern `herdr --skill` uses. A skill vendored separately drifts from the
496	tool it describes, and an agent reading a stale command list is worse than one
497	reading none.
498
499	```bash
500	dev skill install    # → ~/.agents/skills/dev-cli, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills
501	dev --skill          # print it, for a dotfiles installer to sync
502	dev skill sync       # regenerate the command reference from the command tree
503	dev skill sync --check   # fail if it has drifted — wire into CI
504	```
505
506	The skill defers to the companion `git-workflow` skill for commit conventions,
507	SemVer and branch naming rather than restating them. It owns what is new: the
508	worktree ownership rule, the task lifecycle, and how `dev` and herdr divide
509	responsibility.
```

109	// generateCommandReference renders the whole command tree as markdown. This is
110	// the single source of truth for what the skill tells an agent dev can do.
111	func generateCommandReference(root *cobra.Command) string {
112		var b strings.Builder
113		b.WriteString("<!-- generated by `dev skill sync`; do not edit by hand -->\n\n")
114		writeCommand(&b, root, 0)
115		return b.String()
116	}

118	func writeCommand(b *strings.Builder, c *cobra.Command, depth int) {
119		if c.Hidden || c.Name() == "no-help" || c.Name() == "completion" {
120			return
121		}
122		if depth > 0 {
123			fmt.Fprintf(b, "### `%s`\n\n%s\n\n", c.CommandPath(), firstLine(c.Short))
124			if usage := c.UseLine(); usage != "" {
125				fmt.Fprintf(b, "```\n%s\n```\n\n", usage)
126			}
127			if flags := renderFlags(c); flags != "" {
128				b.WriteString(flags)
129				b.WriteString("\n")
130			}
131		}
132		for _, sub := range c.Commands() {
133			writeCommand(b, sub, depth+1)
134		}
135	}

140			if f.Hidden {
141				return
142			}
143			name := "--" + f.Name
144			if f.Shorthand != "" {
145				name = "-" + f.Shorthand + ", " + name
146			}
147			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- `%s` — %s\n", name, f.Usage)
148		})
149		return b.String()
150	}
151
152	func firstLine(s string) string {
153		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
154			return s[:i]
155		}
156		return s
157	}

# dev and Herdr

Read this on a Herdr machine, when task state should appear in the sidebar, or
when a `dev start --json` result will be used to launch an agent.

## Division of responsibility

```
Herdr       per-host workspace, pane, process and live-agent state
dev         durable task, branch and checkout lifecycle
SpecStory   history writer rooted at the launched process checkout
Git         durable commits, transcript and plan
```

Herdr is not synced between machines. `dev` persists task facts and an advisory
runtime handle; root-pane data is a transient create result.

## What dev asks Herdr to do

| dev operation | Herdr command |
|---|---|
| list live sessions | `workspace list` + `pane list` |
| list pane-level agent activity | `agent list` |
| open a checkout | `workspace create --cwd <dir> --no-focus --label <name>` |
| open a worktree | `worktree open --path <path> --no-focus --label <repo/branch>` |
| close a session | `workspace close <id>` |
| show task state | `workspace report-metadata <id> --source dev --token …` |

`dev` creates worktrees with Git and only asks Herdr to open them. First-class
`worktree open` gives the child native repository/worktree grouping plus
branch/ahead-behind data. Worktree-mode `dev start` uses the same `repo/branch`
label as `dev wt create`; no special origin labels or metadata are needed.

A plain-workspace fallback reports `surface=workspace` honestly. A root pane is
automatically launchable only when the same successful `worktree open` response
proves a newly created layout. Reuse, fallback, missing/malformed responses,
Tmux, and the `none` runtime never supply a launchable pane. `--no-focus`
preserves the caller's context; never substitute the focused/current pane.

Read `parallel-agents.md` for exact machine validation, pane verification,
SpecStory profiles and permission-mode rules.

## Collision preflight

On Herdr, `dev` compares recognized agent cwd values by canonical Git worktree
root before direct/branch starts and existing-checkout open/resume operations.
Only exact `HERDR_PANE_ID` is excluded. Every recognized state—including
`idle`, `done`, and `unknown`—is occupied.

The root `--allow-shared-checkout` escape hatch is only for coordinated agents
with disjoint ownership. Never add it automatically. A default `dev start`
worktree is still allowed because it creates a separate checkout.

`dev status` shows recognized activities for the current worktree.

## Sidebar metadata

Task annotations use `$stage` and `$next`. Tokens render only if the local Herdr
row layout names them; reporting an unused token succeeds silently.

```toml
[ui.sidebar.spaces]
rows = [
  ["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"],
  ["branch", "git_status"],
  ["$next"],
]
```

## Cleanup semantics

Herdr agent `done` means the latest turn settled. It does not establish that
history is synced, review is complete, code is committed, or cleanup is safe.
Never auto-close based on agent state.

- `dev park` closes the workspace and keeps the worktree.
- `dev park --cold --push` closes and removes a reconstructible checkout.
- `dev done --ff` integrates and cleans up.
- `dev done --pr` leaves task/runtime/worktree for review.
- `dev sweep` reports first.

`workspace close` itself touches no branch or checkout. `--cold --keep-session`
is rejected so a session cannot remain pointed at a removed directory.

## Agent sessions are not yet attached by dev

Herdr exposes live agent session IDs and `Task.AgentSession` exists in the task
schema, but production `start`, `park`, and `resume` do not currently capture or
attach an agent conversation. Resume reopens/rebuilds the checkout and runtime;
agent-session handoff remains an explicit launcher operation.

## Without Herdr

Runtime selection is Herdr → Tmux → none unless pinned. Tmux can report session
creation/reuse but no pane. `none` emits a shell `cd` directive in human mode;
`dev start --json` suppresses that directive and stays pure JSON.

````

1	# Parallel background agents
2
3	Read this when starting independent agent work while another agent remains live,
4	or when launching an agent into a worktree created by `dev start --json`.
5
6	## Boundary and owners
7
8	> **Worktree per change stream; one SpecStory root per worktree; exact pane per
9	> agent; exact transcript/plan finalization.**
10
11	- `dev` owns the durable task, branch and checkout.
12	- Herdr owns workspace/pane layout and live process detection.
13	- SpecStory owns rendered history rooted at the process launch checkout.
14	- Git owns the code, transcript and plan that survive cleanup.
15
16	`dev start` does not start an agent. This workflow composes `dev`, Herdr and
17	SpecStory after verifying each boundary.
18
19	## Preflight
20
21	- [ ] `test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1`
22	- [ ] `dev doctor`
23	- [ ] `command -v specstory`
24	- [ ] Explicit task name and committed base ref are known.
25	- [ ] New work does not depend on another checkout's uncommitted state.
26	- [ ] Launch profile and permission mode are explicit.
27
28	If the new task needs dirty state, wait for the owning agent to make a checkpoint
29	commit and use that exact commit/ref as `--base`. Do not stash, reset, switch, or
30	copy another agent's checkout.
31
32	## Create and validate the target
33
34	Choose a human runtime label that describes the child and its origin, for
35	example `child-task ← parent-agent` or `child-task ← w1Z`. IDs remain transient
36	Herdr metadata; the task/branch identity does not change.
37
38	```bash
39	result="$(dev start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>' \
40	  --runtime-label '<child ← origin>' --json)" || {
41	  # Side effects may exist even though no success JSON was emitted. Stop and
42	  # reconcile the reported task/worktree manually; do not retry blindly.
43	  exit 1
44	}
45	```
46
47	Accept the result only when all of these are true:
48
49	```text
50	mode == "worktree"
51	repo_path, worktree_path and checkout are absolute
52	checkout == worktree_path
53	runtime.name == "herdr"
54	runtime.surface == "worktree"
55	runtime.opened == true
56	runtime.created == true
57	runtime.root_pane_id is non-empty
58	```
59
60	Missing/reused/fallback/non-Herdr results remain useful tasks/worktrees, but are
61	not launchable targets. Stop without guessing another pane.
62
63	When invoked from another Herdr workspace, a newly created target may report
64	`origin.workspace_id` and `origin.pane_id`. `dev` also annotates only the target
65	workspace with `$origin_workspace`/`$origin_pane`; it skips missing or self
66	origins and never persists them in the task TOML.
67
68	## Verify the exact pane
69
70	Use only `runtime.root_pane_id` from the JSON object:
71
72	```bash
73	herdr pane get "$root_pane_id"
74	herdr pane process-info --pane "$root_pane_id"
75	```
76
77	Verify:
78
79	- pane cwd and foreground cwd equal the JSON `checkout`;
80	- it is the returned target workspace/pane, not the caller pane;
81	- no agent is recognized there;
82	- process info shows an interactive shell ready for launch.
83
84	Do not use current/focused pane, sidebar order, or `pane list` to choose a
85	fallback. The launch command itself is the final availability gate.
86
87	## Select a launcher profile
88
89	A new external process does **not** inherit the parent agent's permission mode.
90	A resumed/forked Claude session also does not restore bypass mode. Therefore the
91	caller must explicitly choose both profile and permission mode; never infer or
92	elevate one when unknown.
93
94	| Profile | Exact root-pane command shape | Backend state |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| standard Claude | `specstory run claude -c claude [native args]` | normal project/config resolution |
97	| standard Codex | `specstory run codex -c codex [native args]` | normal project/config resolution |
98	| `claude-copilot-once` | call the shell function directly with native args | wrapper already runs SpecStory, creates a fresh destination pin, removes only its own pin |
99	| `codex-copilot-once` | call the shell function directly with native args | wrapper already runs SpecStory and injects backend through CLI |
100	| sticky/plain Claude | `specstory run claude -c claude [native args]` | require exact `.claude/settings.local.json` in `worktree.include` and verify it exists in the target |
101
102	Do not add a second watcher for any of these profiles. The standard profiles use
103	`specstory run`; both `*-copilot-once` wrappers already invoke SpecStory and
104	preserve argv.
105
```

```text
135-## Worktrees
136-
137-```bash
138-herdr worktree list [--workspace ID | --cwd PATH]
139-herdr worktree create [--workspace ID | --cwd PATH] [--branch NAME] [--base REF] [--path PATH] [--label TEXT] [--focus] [--no-focus]
140:herdr worktree open [--workspace ID | --cwd PATH] (--path PATH | --branch NAME) [--label TEXT] [--focus] [--no-focus]
141-herdr worktree remove --workspace ID [--force]
142-```
143-
144-Worktrees are normal Herdr workspaces with Git checkout provenance. `worktree create` creates a Git worktree checkout, opens it as a workspace, and groups it with the parent repo workspace. If `--branch` names an existing local branch, Herdr checks it out; otherwise it creates the branch from `--base` or `HEAD`. Without `--path`, Herdr creates the checkout under `<worktrees.directory>/<repo>/<branch-slug>`.
145-
146-`workspace close` closes only Herdr state. To delete the checkout, run `worktree remove`. It runs `git worktree remove`, never deletes the branch, and requires `--force` when Git refuses a dirty checkout.
147-
148-## Tabs
149-
150-```bash
151-herdr tab list [--workspace <workspace_id>]
152-herdr tab create [--workspace <workspace_id>] [--cwd PATH] [--label TEXT] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--focus] [--no-focus]
153-herdr tab get <tab_id>
154-herdr tab focus <tab_id>
155-herdr tab rename <tab_id> <label>
156-herdr tab close <tab_id>
157-```
158-
159-A tab is another terminal layout inside a workspace. Without `--workspace`, `tab create` uses the active workspace and fails if none exists. Its JSON response exposes `.result.tab.tab_id` and `.result.root_pane.pane_id`. Closing a workspace's last tab also closes the workspace, matching the TUI close-tab action. If `confirm_close` is enabled and closing the tab would also close a whole worktree group, `tab close` returns a `confirmation_required` error instead.
160-
161-Workspace and tab creation, and pane splitting, leave focus unchanged by default. `--focus` selects the new layout; `--no-focus` states the default explicitly. Without `--cwd`, new terminals follow the configured `terminal.new_cwd` policy, which follows the source pane or workspace by default. Each `--env KEY=VALUE` adds or replaces that variable in the new root shell.
162-

29	func newSweepCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {

32			staleDays int

39
40	Cleanup usually fails not because people are unwilling but because there is no
41	trustworthy way to be sure the work is recoverable. So sweep reports first and
42	only changes things with --apply, confirming each one unless you pass --yes.
43	Nothing here ever deletes uncommitted work.`,
44			Args: cobra.NoArgs,

48				if err != nil {
49					return err
50				}
51				rt := app.Runtime()
52				rows := inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{})
53				stale := time.Duration(staleDays) * 24 * time.Hour
54
55				var sugg []suggestion
56				for _, r := range rows {
57					sugg = append(sugg, suggestFor(app, ctx, rt, r, stale)...)
58				}
59
60				// Live sessions no task claims: the other half of a crowded sidebar.
61				if sessions, err := rt.List(ctx); err == nil {
62					if orphans := inventory.Orphans(sessions, rows); len(orphans) > 0 {
63						fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d live session(s) with no task recorded:\n", len(orphans))
64						for _, s := range orphans {
65							dir := "—"
66							if len(s.Dirs) > 0 {
67								dir = config.Contract(s.Dirs[0])

69							fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %-24s %s\n", truncate(s.Label, 24), dir)
70						}

72					}
73				}
74
75				if len(sugg) == 0 {
76					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nNothing to sweep — every task matches its recorded state.")

78				}
79
80				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\n%d suggestion(s):\n\n", len(sugg))

85				}

89					return nil
90				}

119
120		switch {
121		// A hot task with no live session is the commonest drift: the session was
122		// closed (or the machine rebooted) without parking.
123		case t.State == task.Hot && !r.Live():
124			out = append(out, suggestion{
125				row:    r,
126				reason: fmt.Sprintf("hot but no live session, idle %s", humanAge(r.Age())),
127				action: fmt.Sprintf("mark %s warm", t.ID),
128				apply: func() error {
129					t.State = task.Warm
130					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
131				},
132			})
133
134		// A warm task nobody has touched in weeks is a candidate for cold: keeping
135		// the worktree costs disk and clutters every listing.
136		case t.State == task.Warm && r.Age() > stale:
137			reason := fmt.Sprintf("warm and untouched for %s", humanAge(r.Age()))
138			if r.Status.Dirty() {
139				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + ", but has uncommitted work",
140					action: "commit or `dev park --wip` before going cold — not changed automatically"})
141				break
142			}
143			if !r.Status.Synced() {
144				out = append(out, suggestion{row: r, reason: reason + fmt.Sprintf(", not pushed (%s)", r.Status.Summary()),
145					action: fmt.Sprintf("push %s so it can go cold: dev park %s --cold --push", t.Branch, t.ID)})
146				break
147			}
148			out = append(out, suggestion{
149				row:    r,
150				reason: reason + ", clean and pushed",
151				action: fmt.Sprintf("go cold: remove %s (branch and remote keep the work)", config.Contract(r.Checkout)),
152				apply: func() error {
153					m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: app.Err}
154					if t.WorktreePath != "" {
155						if err := m.Remove(ctx, wt.RemoveRequest{
156							RepoPath: t.RepoPath, Path: t.WorktreePath, RuntimeHandle: t.RuntimeHandle,
157						}); err != nil {
158							return err
159						}
160						t.WorktreePath = ""
161					}
162					t.State, t.RuntimeHandle = task.Cold, ""
163					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
164				},
165			})
166
167		// A done task's entry has served its purpose once the branch is gone.
168		case t.State == task.Done:
169			out = append(out, suggestion{
170				row:    r,
171				reason: "merged",
172				action: fmt.Sprintf("reap the task entry %s", t.ID),
173				apply:  func() error { return app.Tasks.Delete(t.ID) },
174			})
175		}
176
177		// Drift that is independent of the lifecycle stage.
178		if r.WorktreeMissing && t.WorktreePath != "" {
179			wtPath := t.WorktreePath
180			out = append(out, suggestion{
181				row:    r,
182				reason: "records a worktree that git no longer knows about",
183				action: fmt.Sprintf("clear the stale worktree path %s", config.Contract(wtPath)),
184				apply: func() error {
185					if err := gitx.PruneWorktrees(ctx, t.RepoPath); err != nil {
186						return err
187					}
188					t.WorktreePath = ""
189					if t.State == task.Hot || t.State == task.Warm {
190						t.State = task.Cold
191					}
192					return app.Tasks.Save(t)
193				},
194			})
195		}
196		return out
197	}
198
199	func confirm(app *App, in *bufio.Reader, action string) bool {
200		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s? [y/N] ", action)
201		line, err := in.ReadString('\n')
202		if err != nil {
203			return false
204		}
205		answer := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(line))
206		return answer == "y" || answer == "yes"
207	}

237	// Orphans reports live runtime sessions that no task claims — the "I opened
238	// this and never wrote it down" case that makes a sidebar grow without bound.
239	func Orphans(sessions []runtime.Session, rows []Row) []runtime.Session {
240		claimed := map[string]bool{}
241		for _, r := range rows {
242			if r.Session != nil {
243				claimed[r.Session.Handle] = true
244			}
245		}
246		var out []runtime.Session
247		for _, s := range sessions {
248			if !claimed[s.Handle] {
249				out = append(out, s)
250			}
251		}
252		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Label < out[j].Label })
253		return out
254	}

package cli

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
)

func runtimeForTask(app *App, t *task.Task) runtime.Runtime {
	if t.RuntimeHandle != "" && t.RuntimeName != "" {
		return app.runtimeNamed(t.RuntimeName)
	}
	return app.Runtime()
}

func setTaskRuntime(t *task.Task, rt runtime.Runtime, opened runtime.OpenResult) {
	t.RuntimeHandle = persistedRuntimeHandle(rt, opened)
	if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
		t.RuntimeName = ""
		return
	}
	t.RuntimeName = rt.Name()
}

func clearTaskRuntime(t *task.Task) {
	t.RuntimeHandle = ""
	t.RuntimeName = ""
}

func runtimeHandleCovers(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, handle, checkout string) (bool, error) {
	if handle == "" || rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" {
		return false, nil
	}
	sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	for _, session := range sessions {
		if session.Handle == handle && session.Covers(checkout) {
			return true, nil
		}
	}
	return false, nil
}

// closeTaskRuntime validates an opaque persisted handle before sending it back
// to its recorded backend. A stale handle is cleared without being fed to a
// different backend; a close error leaves both provenance fields intact.
func closeTaskRuntime(ctx context.Context, app *App, t *task.Task, checkout string) (runtime.Runtime, error) {
	rt := runtimeForTask(app, t)
	if t.RuntimeHandle == "" {
		return rt, nil
	}
	live, err := runtimeHandleCovers(ctx, rt, t.RuntimeHandle, checkout)
	if err != nil {
		return rt, fmt.Errorf("validate %s runtime session %s: %w", rt.Name(), t.RuntimeHandle, err)
	}
	if !live {
		clearTaskRuntime(t)
		return rt, nil
	}
	if err := rt.Close(ctx, t.RuntimeHandle); err != nil {
		return rt, err
	}
	clearTaskRuntime(t)
	return rt, nil
}

205	// inventory. Every returned row is occupied; lifecycle state is descriptive and
206	// is deliberately not used to decide whether another agent may share its cwd.
207	func (h *Herdr) AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error) {
208		var res struct {
209			Agents []herdrPane `json:"agents"`
210		}
211		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, "agent", "list"); err != nil {
212			return nil, err
213		}
214		out := make([]AgentActivity, 0, len(res.Agents))
215		for _, p := range res.Agents {
216			cwd := p.ForegroundCWD
217			if cwd == "" {
218				cwd = p.CWD
219			}
220			out = append(out, AgentActivity{
221				PaneID: p.PaneID, WorkspaceID: p.WorkspaceID,
222				Agent: p.Agent, Name: p.Name, Status: p.AgentStatus, CWD: cwd,
223			})
224		}
225		return out, nil
226	}
227
228	// Open implements Runtime. An already-open directory is focused rather than
229	// opened twice.
230	func (h *Herdr) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
231		existing, err := h.List(ctx)
232		if err != nil {
233			return OpenResult{}, err
234		}
235		for _, s := range existing {
236			if s.Covers(dir) {
237				if err := h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", s.Handle); err != nil {
238					return OpenResult{}, err
239				}
240				return OpenResult{Handle: s.Handle, Surface: "workspace", Opened: true}, nil
241			}
242		}
243		args := []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", dir, "--no-focus"}
244		if label != "" {
245			args = append(args, "--label", label)
246		}
247		var res struct {
248			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
249			RootPane  herdrPane      `json:"root_pane"`
250		}
251		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
252			return OpenResult{}, err
253		}
254		if res.Workspace.WorkspaceID == "" {
255			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr workspace create: response has no workspace id")
256		}
257		if res.RootPane.PaneID == "" {
258			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr workspace create: response has no root pane")
259		}
260		return OpenResult{
261			Handle: res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, Surface: "workspace", Opened: true,
262			Created: true, RootPaneID: res.RootPane.PaneID,
263		}, nil
264	}
265
266	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
267	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
268	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
269	// ahead/behind row.
270	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
271		args := []string{"worktree", "open"}
272		if source := h.parentWorktreeSource(ctx, path); source != "" {
273			// Pin the canonical parent checkout instead of relying on the calling
274			// pane. This preserves native nested grouping even when dev is invoked
275			// from a different Herdr workspace.
276			args = append(args, "--cwd", source)
277		}
278		args = append(args, "--path", path, "--no-focus")
279		if label != "" {
280			args = append(args, "--label", label)
281		}
282		var res struct {
283			Workspace   herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
284			Worktree    herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
285			RootPane    herdrPane      `json:"root_pane"`
286			AlreadyOpen bool           `json:"already_open"`
287		}
288		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
289			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
290			// more than it being tagged with git provenance. A fallback root pane is
291			// withheld so callers cannot mistake it for a first-class worktree target.
292			fallback, fallbackErr := h.Open(ctx, path, label)
293			fallback.RootPaneID = ""
294			fallback.Surface = "workspace"
295			return fallback, fallbackErr
296		}
297		handle := res.Workspace.WorkspaceID
298		if handle == "" {
299			handle = res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID
300		}
301		if handle == "" {
302			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response has no workspace id")
303		}
304		if !res.AlreadyOpen && res.RootPane.PaneID == "" {
305			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: new workspace response has no root pane")
306		}
307		rootPaneID := ""
308		if !res.AlreadyOpen {
309			rootPaneID = res.RootPane.PaneID
310		}
311		return OpenResult{
312			Handle: handle, Surface: "worktree", Opened: true,
313			Created: !res.AlreadyOpen, RootPaneID: rootPaneID,
314		}, nil
315	}
316
317	func (h *Herdr) parentWorktreeSource(ctx context.Context, path string) string {
318		if h.worktreeSource != nil {
319			return h.worktreeSource(ctx, path)
320		}
321		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-C", path, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
322		out, err := cmd.Output()
323		if err != nil {
324			return ""
325		}
326		common := strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
327		if common == "" {
328			return ""
329		}

package wt

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestCopyFileRejectsSourceReplacedAfterLstat(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	source := filepath.Join(dir, "settings.local.json")
	outside := filepath.Join(dir, "outside.json")
	dest := filepath.Join(dir, "copied.json")
	if err := os.WriteFile(source, []byte(`{"backend":"expected"}`), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	expected, err := os.Lstat(source)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(outside, []byte(`{"secret":"outside"}`), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Remove(source); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Symlink(outside, source); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	err = copyFile(source, dest, expected)
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "source changed") {
		t.Fatalf("copyFile should reject the swapped source, got %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(dest); !os.IsNotExist(err) {
		t.Fatalf("destination should not be created after source swap: %v", err)
	}
}

	herdr := &activityRuntime{name: "herdr", sessions: []runtime.Session{{Handle: "w7", Dirs: []string{r.Root}}}}
	tmux := &activityRuntime{name: "tmux"}
	app := &App{runtimeInstance: tmux, runtimesByName: map[string]runtime.Runtime{"herdr": herdr}}
	tk := &task.Task{RuntimeHandle: "w7", RuntimeName: "herdr"}

	resolved, closed, err := closeTaskRuntime(context.Background(), app, tk, r.Root)
	if err != nil || !closed || resolved != herdr {

	if tk.RuntimeHandle != "" || tk.RuntimeName != "" {

	}
}

package cli

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/config"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx/gittest"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/wt"
)

func lifecycleConfig(t *testing.T) config.Config {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := config.Default()
	cfg.Paths.WorktreeRoot = filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "Worktrees")
	cfg.Paths.WorktreePath = "{{worktree_root}}/{{repo}}/{{branch|slug}}"
	cfg.Worktree.Include = nil
	cfg.Worktree.PostCreate = config.PostCreate{}
	return cfg
}

func TestParkColdCloseFailureKeepsCheckoutAndTaskRuntime(t *testing.T) {
	r := gittest.New(t)
	r.WithRemote()
	cfg := lifecycleConfig(t)
	res, err := (&wt.Manager{Cfg: cfg}).Create(context.Background(), wt.CreateRequest{
		RepoPath: r.Root, Branch: "feat/close-failure", Base: "main", NoRuntime: true,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r.GitIn(res.Path, "push", "-u", "origin", "feat/close-failure")

	rt := &activityRuntime{
		sessions: []runtime.Session{{Handle: "w7", Dirs: []string{res.Path}}},
		closeErr: errors.New("close failed"),
	}
	store := task.NewStore(t.TempDir())
	tk := &task.Task{
		Name: "close failure", Repo: "repo", RepoPath: r.Root,
		Branch: "feat/close-failure", Base: "main", WorktreePath: res.Path,
		Mode: task.ModeWorktree, State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(),
		RuntimeHandle: "w7", RuntimeName: "herdr",
	}
	if err := store.Save(tk); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	app := &App{Cfg: cfg, Tasks: store, Out: &bytes.Buffer{}, Err: &bytes.Buffer{}, runtimeInstance: rt}
	cmd := newParkCmd(app)
	cmd.SilenceErrors, cmd.SilenceUsage = true, true
	cmd.SetArgs([]string{tk.ID, "--cold"})
	err = cmd.Execute()
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "refusing cold cleanup") {
		t.Fatalf("cold close failure = %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(res.Path, "README.md")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("cold park removed checkout after close failure: %v", err)
	}
	got, err := store.Get(tk.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.State != task.Hot || got.WorktreePath != res.Path || got.RuntimeHandle != "w7" || got.RuntimeName != "herdr" {
		t.Fatalf("task changed after refused cold cleanup: %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestDoneCloseFailureKeepsIntegratedWorktreeAndRuntime(t *testing.T) {
	r := gittest.New(t)
	cfg := lifecycleConfig(t)
	res, err := (&wt.Manager{Cfg: cfg}).Create(context.Background(), wt.CreateRequest{
		RepoPath: r.Root, Branch: "feat/done-close-failure", Base: "main", NoRuntime: true,
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r.Write("placeholder", "")
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(res.Path, "feature.txt"), []byte("done\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	r.GitIn(res.Path, "add", "feature.txt")
	r.GitIn(res.Path, "commit", "-m", "feat: done")

	rt := &activityRuntime{
		sessions: []runtime.Session{{Handle: "w7", Dirs: []string{res.Path}}},
		closeErr: errors.New("close failed"),
	}
	store := task.NewStore(t.TempDir())
	tk := &task.Task{
		Name: "done close failure", Repo: "repo", RepoPath: r.Root,
		Branch: "feat/done-close-failure", Base: "main", WorktreePath: res.Path,
		Mode: task.ModeWorktree, State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(),
		RuntimeHandle: "w7", RuntimeName: "herdr",
	}
	if err := store.Save(tk); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	app := &App{Cfg: cfg, Tasks: store, Out: &bytes.Buffer{}, Err: &bytes.Buffer{}, runtimeInstance: rt}
	cmd := newDoneCmd(app)
	cmd.SilenceErrors, cmd.SilenceUsage = true, true
	cmd.SetArgs([]string{tk.ID, "--ff"})
	err = cmd.Execute()
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "worktree kept") {
		t.Fatalf("done close failure = %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(res.Path, "feature.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("done removed worktree after close failure: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(r.Root, "feature.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("fast-forward should already be integrated: %v", err)
	}
	got, err := store.Get(tk.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got.State != task.Hot || got.RuntimeHandle != "w7" || got.RuntimeName != "herdr" {
		t.Fatalf("task should remain reconcilable after close failure: %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestTUIWorktreeStartUsesNativeLabelAndNoNoneHandle(t *testing.T) {

	}
	tk := tuiStartedTask(row, "auth", "feat/auth", "main", created, runtime.None{})
	if tk.RuntimeHandle != "" || tk.RuntimeName != "" {
		t.Fatalf("TUI persisted None pseudo-handle: %+v", tk)
	}
}

83	Do not use current/focused pane, sidebar order, or `pane list` to choose a

86	## Select a launcher profile
87
88	A new external process does **not** inherit the parent agent's permission mode.
89	A resumed/forked Claude session also does not restore bypass mode. Therefore the
90	caller must explicitly choose both profile and permission mode; never infer or
91	elevate one when unknown.
92
93	| Profile | Exact root-pane command shape | Backend state |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| standard Claude | `specstory run claude -c claude [native args]` | normal project/config resolution |
96	| standard Codex | `specstory run codex -c codex [native args]` | normal project/config resolution |

98	| `codex-copilot-once` | call the shell function directly with native args | wrapper already runs SpecStory and injects backend through CLI |
99	| sticky/plain Claude | `specstory run claude -c claude [native args]` | require exact `.claude/settings.local.json` in `worktree.include` and verify it exists in the target |

101	Do not add a second watcher for any of these profiles. The standard profiles use

111	For explicit handoff/fork with bypass, include both because the resumed session

116	```

118	Without explicit bypass, use the selected non-elevated mode/profile. Never copy

127
128	Send the fully shell-quoted selected command only to the exact returned pane:
129
130	```bash
131	herdr pane run "$root_pane_id" "$launch_command"
132	```

134	Run the selected command in the exact interactive root pane. Then let Herdr
135	detect the process and assign the requested unique agent name; do not start a
136	second process merely to obtain a name.

138	After detection, use Herdr's explicit agent surface to rename/verify the process

150	or send probe keys.

152	Treat `working`, `blocked`, `idle`, `done`, and `unknown` as occupied. `blocked`

155	## Shared-checkout override
156
157	`dev` guards direct/branch tasks and existing-checkout open/resume paths when
158	another recognized Herdr agent resolves to the same canonical Git worktree.
159	Only the exact caller `HERDR_PANE_ID` is excluded.

166
167	Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` to global/default includes. It is

108	## Parallel background work
109
110	Read `references/parallel-agents.md` before spawning an independent agent while
111	another remains live. The fail-closed workflow uses `dev start --json`, requires
112	a newly created first-class Herdr worktree and its exact returned root pane,
113	then launches an explicit SpecStory/profile command there. Reused, fallback,
114	non-Herdr, missing or unverified panes are never launch targets.
115
116	`dev` guards direct/branch and existing-checkout open/resume paths when another
117	recognized Herdr agent occupies the same canonical Git worktree. Every state,
118	including `idle`, `done`, and `unknown`, is occupied; only the caller's exact
119	`HERDR_PANE_ID` is excluded. Never add `--allow-shared-checkout` unless agents
120	already have coordinated disjoint file ownership.
121
122	A new external agent does not inherit the parent permission mode, and a resumed
123	Claude fork does not restore bypass. Require an explicit profile/mode and never
124	silently elevate. Herdr `done` is turn-settled—not artifact/commit/cleanup done.
125
126	## Everyday commands
127
128	```bash
129	dev                        # interactive dashboard (plain listing when piped)
130	dev edit                   # open the effective config; generate it first if absent
131	dev ls                     # what am I working on, everywhere
132	dev ls --json              # stable machine-readable form (also over ssh)
133	dev status                 # what is this directory: repo, branch, task, session
134	dev sweep                  # what has gone stale or drifted, and what to do
135	dev sweep --apply          # act on it, confirming each change
136
137	dev wt create feat/auth --base main    # worktree at the configured path
138	dev wt list                            # every worktree of this repo
139	dev wt plan                            # what a new worktree would be set up with
140	dev wt plan --write                    # seed a committed .dev.toml from it
141	dev wt rm feat/auth                    # remove the checkout; the branch stays
142
143	dev repo list              # every repo under the scan roots
144	dev repo clone owner/name  # clone into the right place, via gh or glab
145	dev repo sync --all        # fetch + prune, and report what moved
146	dev repo remote [query]     # search authenticated gh + glab repositories
147	dev bootstrap ~/code       # recursively inventory an existing machine
148	dev bootstrap ~/code --index ~/Projects   # plan a non-destructive symlink catalog
149	dev gitignore              # .gitignore from GitHub templates + the common bits
150	dev adopt                  # import existing worktrees/sessions/branches as tasks
151
152	dev try redis-streams      # dated scratch directory for an experiment
153	dev graduate redis-streams --category Infra   # promote it into a real project
154
155	dev stats --heatmap        # where the time actually went
156	dev stats backfill --repo api  # seed one repo; TUI H then b does this in place
157	dev stats path             # durable XDG data, not cache
158	dev cache list             # regenerable forge/gitignore caches
159	dev help worktrees         # quick-reference pages
160	```

164	## Bootstrapping and adopting an existing machine
165
166	Read `references/bootstrap.md` before recursively scanning paths, creating a
167	symlink index, moving physical repositories, or generating layout config. Move
168	is destructive and must follow its report → review → apply procedure.
169
170	There is nothing to migrate for ordinary use. `dev` discovers repositories through
171	`paths.scan_roots` and never moves, renames or deletes anything.
172
173	```bash
174	dev config init     # detects this machine's roots; every value stays editable
175	dev adopt           # report existing worktrees, sessions and unmerged branches
176	dev adopt --apply   # record them as tasks (nothing on disk changes)
177	```
178
179	Do not assume the user's layout is `~/Documents/Program`. Run `dev config show`
180	or `dev repo list` to see what this machine is actually configured for.
181
182	## Dashboard and forge inventory
183
184	The TUI has TASKS, REPOS and REMOTE views, switched with tab or vim-style h/l.
185	REMOTE queries authenticated `gh` and `glab` lazily, uses a short-lived private
186	cache, and `/` filters provider, owner/name and description. Enter opens a local
187	clone; `c` confirms before cloning an absent remote. Use `dev repo remote
188	[query] --json` for the non-interactive form; `--cached` avoids a network query.
189
190	REPOS has explicit LIVE and LATEST columns: latest is the newest dirty-file
191	mtime, commit, or task update. Detail shows the Herdr/tmux handle and agent
192	status. `[tui.repos]` chooses columns and default sort; `O` cycles sort and `R`
193	reverses it.
194
195	`H` opens the selected repo's heatmap. On an empty panel, `b` backfills only
196	that repo and redraws; `r` rereads existing stats. Stats live in
197	`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/stats.db` and are durable observations, not cache — use
198	`dev stats clear` with an explicit scope. `dev cache clear` only removes
199	regenerable forge/gitignore data under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev`.
200
201	`e` edits config and returning live-reloads data/tool bindings; `r` reloads
202	explicitly. Runtime
203	backend changes require restarting the TUI.
204
205	External tools are explicit `[[tui.tools]]` config. Run `dev tui tools` before
206	recommending a binding; it shows the exact command and whether it is available.
207	Commands run through `$SHELL` in the selected checkout. For an alias/function
208	that exists only in shell rc, set `interactive = true`; dev uses `$SHELL -lic`
209	and evaluates the command after rc loading. Prefer an executable on PATH when
210	the binding should be portable across machines.
211
212	## Editing configuration
213
214	Use `dev edit` (or `dev config edit`) rather than guessing the XDG path. It
215	opens the file selected by `--config`, generating the machine-detected starter
216	when absent, and resolves `--editor` → `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → nvim/vim/vi.
217
218	## Rules for agents
219
220	1. **Do not equate task with worktree.** Ad-hoc opening needs no task; `--direct`
221	   tracks current/main; `--branch-only` is lightweight isolation; default
222	   worktree is for interruption/experimentation/parallelism.
223
224	2. **Always pass `--base` for branch/worktree tasks.** Without it a new branch starts from the current
225	   HEAD, so starting a task while standing on `feature/A` silently builds on
226	   `feature/A`. This is the single most common way to produce a confusing
227	   history unattended.
228
229	3. **Never `--force` a worktree removal on your own.** `dev wt rm` refuses a
230	   checkout with uncommitted changes; that refusal is the feature. Ask the
231	   user before overriding it.
232
233	4. **Report drift, do not fix it silently.** `dev sweep` without `--apply`
234	   changes nothing. Show the user its output rather than running `--apply --yes`
235	   for them.
236
237	5. **Prefer a checkpoint commit over `git stash`.** A stash is invisible in the
238	   log, easy to forget, and cannot be pushed — so it can never reach another
239	   machine. `dev park --wip` makes a `wip:` commit instead.
240
241	6. **One writer per branch at a time.** `dev resume` refuses a task owned by
242	   another host without `--force`. Before overriding, confirm that machine has
243	   pushed.
244
245	7. **Check `dev wt plan` before blaming a worktree.** A worktree that comes up
246	   broken is nearly always a provisioning gap, not a git problem. The plan
247	   shows the detected project types, which tools are missing, and exactly what
248	   would be copied or run. Dependencies arrive by a per-ecosystem strategy —
249	   `reinstall` (default), `copy`, `link` or `skip` — and dev refuses an unsound
250	   one rather than producing a broken checkout: a virtualenv cannot be copied,
251	   because it bakes its own absolute path into `pyvenv.cfg`.
252
253	8. **Do not create a worktree per agent.** Worktrees isolate *change streams*;
254	   panes isolate *agents*. Several agents belong in one checkout only after
255	   explicit disjoint ownership; the collision guard otherwise refuses it.
256
257	9. **Parallel launch is exact-pane and fail-closed.** Accept only a new
258	   first-class Herdr worktree/root pane from `dev start --json`. Never infer from
259	   focus/sidebar order, relocate SpecStory with mid-session `EnterWorktree`, or
260	   treat any recognized agent state as a free pane. Never add
261	   `--allow-shared-checkout` without coordinated ownership.
262
263	10. **Launcher profile and permission mode are explicit.** Standard Claude/Codex
264	    use `specstory run`; verified `*-copilot-once` wrappers run directly because
265	    they already wrap SpecStory. A child process/resumed fork does not inherit
266	    bypass, so never elevate an unknown mode. Read `parallel-agents.md`.
267
268	11. **Cleanup is explicit, never agent-state-driven.** Herdr `done` means a turn
269	    settled. Sync/stage exact artifacts first; use park/done/sweep semantics,
270	    and never auto-close from `done`.
271
272	12. **Prefer `dev bootstrap --index` over `--move`.** If the problem is
273	   navigation, a symlink catalog solves it without changing the authoritative
274	   paths. For a physical move, never add `--apply --yes` on the user's behalf;
275	   blocked rows are preconditions to resolve, not checks to bypass.
276
277	13. **`dev adopt` without `--apply` changes nothing.** Show the user its report
278	   rather than applying it for them — which branches count as work in flight is
279	   their judgement, not yours.
280
281	14. **Do not call stats.db a cache.** Session/WakaTime observations may not be
282	   reconstructible. Use `dev stats clear --repo/--source/--all`; use
283	   `dev cache clear` only for remote/gitignore caches.
